Linden Shore Mutual, workers' compensation, Maryland. Edition of July 2025. Internal use by underwriting and premium
audit.

This excerpt holds the general paragraphs and the class codes our current new-business employers fall under. Audit
files cite a paragraph by its identifier (CG-01, CG-02 and so on). A class code is cited by the paragraph that
describes it.

## General

**CG-01. Premium basis.** Premium is charged per USD 100 of payroll in each class code at the rate underwriting sets
for that code. Payroll is reported for the policy period being audited.

**CG-02. Assigning codes.** An employer is assigned the class code that describes its principal business. An employee
whose work is described by another code in this guide is reported under that code. An employer may carry several codes.

**CG-03. Payroll.** Payroll is the gross remuneration paid to employees for the period: wages, salaries, commissions
and bonuses. Expense reimbursements that the employer can document, such as travel and lodging costs, are not payroll.

**CG-05. Owners and executive officers.** An owner or executive officer who has filed an election of exclusion is not
counted. An owner who is included is counted under the code for the work the owner does.

**CG-06. Subcontractors.** Payments to a subcontractor who does not carry workers' compensation insurance for its own
workers may be treated as payroll of the employer, under the code for the work the subcontractor performed.

**CG-07. Division of payroll.** When an employee performs work in more than one classification and the employer keeps
records of the time spent in each, the employee's payroll may be divided between the codes.

## Class codes

**CG-04. C-110 Clerical office employees.** Employees whose duties are confined to an office: correspondence,
bookkeeping, dispatching by telephone or radio, drafting and estimating at a desk, and professional staff who work in
the office.

**CG-11. R-310 Roofing.** Installation, repair and removal of roofs and roof coverings on any building, including
work on scaffolds and ladders at the roof line.

**CG-12. R-320 Siding and gutters.** Installation and repair of exterior siding, gutters, downspouts and exterior trim
below the roof line. Roofing work is described by CG-11.

**CG-13. L-620 Landscaping and lawn care.** Lawn mowing, planting, mulching and the care of grounds.

**CG-15. H-420 Residential homebuilding.** Construction and remodeling of dwellings: framing, drywall, interior
finish, carpentry and general labor at the building site. Roofing work is described by CG-11 and electrical wiring
by CG-21.

**CG-21. E-510 Electrical wiring.** Installation and repair of electrical wiring and fixtures inside buildings,
including service connections.

**CG-22. M-830 Metal fabrication shop.** Cutting, bending and welding of sheet and structural metal in a shop.

**CG-31. T-610 Courier and delivery drivers.** Drivers of vans and light trucks delivering parcels and documents,
and helpers who ride on the delivery vehicles.

**CG-35. G-950 Parking garage attendants.** Parking and retrieving customer vehicles.

**CG-41. F-710 Restaurants.** Preparation and service of meals: kitchen staff, servers, hosts and dishwashers.

**CG-42. F-720 Off-site caterers.** Preparation of food and its service at events away from the employer's premises,
including the catering crew of an employer that also runs a restaurant.

**CG-51. N-910 Home health care.** Personal care and nursing services in clients' homes.

Linden Shore Mutual, workers' compensation, Maryland. Edition of July 2025. Internal use by underwriting and premium
audit.

This excerpt holds the general paragraphs and the class codes our current new-business employers fall under. Audit
files cite a paragraph by its identifier (CG-01, CG-02 and so on). A class code is cited by the paragraph that
describes it.

## General

**CG-01. Premium basis.** Premium is charged per USD 100 of payroll in each class code at the rate underwriting sets
for that code. Payroll is reported for the policy period being audited.

**CG-02. Assigning codes.** An employer is assigned the class code that describes its principal business. An employee
whose work is described by another code in this guide is reported under that code. An employer may carry several codes.

**CG-03. Payroll.** Payroll is the gross remuneration paid to employees for the period: wages, salaries, commissions
and bonuses. Expense reimbursements that the employer can document, such as travel and lodging costs, are not payroll.

**CG-05. Owners and executive officers.** An owner or executive officer who has filed an election of exclusion is not
counted. An owner who is included is counted under the code for the work the owner does.

**CG-06. Subcontractors.** Payments to a subcontractor who does not carry workers' compensation insurance for its own
workers may be treated as payroll of the employer, under the code for the work the subcontractor performed.

**CG-07. Division of payroll.** When an employee performs work in more than one classification and the employer keeps
records of the time spent in each, the employee's payroll may be divided between the codes.

## Class codes

**CG-04. C-110 Clerical office employees.** Employees whose duties are confined to an office: correspondence,
bookkeeping, dispatching by telephone or radio, drafting and estimating at a desk, and professional staff who work in
the office.

**CG-11. R-310 Roofing.** Installation, repair and removal of roofs and roof coverings on any building, including
work on scaffolds and ladders at the roof line.

**CG-12. R-320 Siding and gutters.** Installation and repair of exterior siding, gutters, downspouts and exterior trim
below the roof line. Roofing work is described by CG-11.

**CG-13. L-620 Landscaping and lawn care.** Lawn mowing, planting, mulching and the care of grounds.

**CG-15. H-420 Residential homebuilding.** Construction and remodeling of dwellings: framing, drywall, interior
finish, carpentry and general labor at the building site. Roofing work is described by CG-11 and electrical wiring
by CG-21.

**CG-21. E-510 Electrical wiring.** Installation and repair of electrical wiring and fixtures inside buildings,
including service connections.

**CG-22. M-830 Metal fabrication shop.** Cutting, bending and welding of sheet and structural metal in a shop.

**CG-31. T-610 Courier and delivery drivers.** Drivers of vans and light trucks delivering parcels and documents,
and helpers who ride on the delivery vehicles.

**CG-35. G-950 Parking garage attendants.** Parking and retrieving customer vehicles.

**CG-41. F-710 Restaurants.** Preparation and service of meals: kitchen staff, servers, hosts and dishwashers.

**CG-42. F-720 Off-site caterers.** Preparation of food and its service at events away from the employer's premises,
including the catering crew of an employer that also runs a restaurant.

**CG-51. N-910 Home health care.** Personal care and nursing services in clients' homes.

    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.temp.cleanup)
        self.root = Path(self.temp.name)
        self.employer = self.root / "another-input-location"
        self.employer.mkdir()
        self.guide = self.root / "guide.md"
        self.guide.write_text(GUIDE, encoding="utf-8")
        self.interview = self.root / "interview.md"
        self.interview.write_text(INTERVIEW, encoding="utf-8")

            (self.employer / filename).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        self.set_times()
        self.set_visits()

    def set_times(self, first=15, second=14):
        rows = []
        for employee, name, count in [("F1", "Example First", first), ("F2", "Example Second", second)]:
            for offset in range(count):
                rows.append(f"{date(2025,1,1)+timedelta(days=offset)},{employee},{name},JOB-1,roofing,8.0\n")
            rows.append(f"2025-02-01,{employee},{name},JOB-2,siding,8.0\n")
        (self.employer / "crew-timesheets.csv").write_text(TIME_HEADER + "".join(rows), encoding="utf-8")

    def set_visits(self, estimator=5, bookkeeper=0, unassigned=0):
        rows = []
        for employee, name, count in [("E1", "Example Estimator", estimator), ("B1", "Example Books", bookkeeper)]:
            for offset in range(count):
                rows.append(f"{date(2025,3,1)+timedelta(days=offset)},{employee},{name},Site A,09:00\n")
        for offset in range(unassigned):
            rows.append(f"{date(2025,4,1)+timedelta(days=offset)},,Unattributed Visitor,Site A,10:00\n")
        (self.employer / "site-signin-log.csv").write_text(SITE_HEADER + "".join(rows), encoding="utf-8")

    def run_contractor(self, **kwargs):
        return process_employer(self.guide, self.employer, self.interview, **kwargs)

        result = self.run_contractor()

        self.assertEqual(len(result.roofing_days["F1"]), 15)
        self.assertEqual(len(result.roofing_days["F2"]), 14)

# Contractor Processing Implementation Plan

**Goal:** Extend the existing in-memory workflow to roofing/siding contractor evidence, preserving all previous results and the four foundational components.

**Design:** Add `contractor_processing.py` with a narrow, source-bound adapter. Add a configurable crew-timesheet filename and result fields for roofing dates, governing-field evidence and employee application comparisons. Dispatch from affirmative business activities, not employer names. Reuse `RuleEvaluator.evaluate`, shared finalization, allocator and application comparison unchanged.

**Rules:** Group valid, positive-work timesheet rows by register employee and distinct roofing date. Apply the existing 15-day rule only with evidence of both roofing and siding operations. Determine the unique governing field code from classified field-worker wages before evaluating office payroll. Missing field decisions, uncertain membership, ties and unsupported scope leave governing code OPEN. Evaluate office workers using the existing contractor visit rule; an evidenced office bookkeeper is not automatically clerical by title.

**Unattributed sign-ins:** Retain rows without a register identity as OPEN source questions, without assigning them to an employee. For office workers, evaluate lower and upper possible visit-date sets using the existing evaluator. Verify a classification only when both possible endpoints return the same code; otherwise keep the employee OPEN. This makes the county-inspector row auditable without fabricating an employee identity or exact visit count.

**Application attribution:** The application lists code totals/headcounts, not employee assignments. Infer former employee codes only when each code has a unique exact wage/headcount subset and those subsets form a disjoint complete partition. Bound the search and return OPEN comparisons on ambiguity. Clearly mark inferred mappings for employer confirmation, separately from verified employee classifications.

**Files:** Modify only existing `employer_processing.py` and `EMPLOYER_PROCESSING.md`; create the contractor adapter, integration tests and this plan. Protect 67 other existing files by SHA-256 and compare complete previous-employer results, excluding only newly added empty result fields.

**Constraints:** No source modification, final deliverables, commits, pushes, synchronization, deployment or upload; preserve Entire capture.

Linden Shore Mutual, workers' compensation, Maryland. Edition of July 2025. Internal use by underwriting and premium
audit.

This excerpt holds the general paragraphs and the class codes our current new-business employers fall under. Audit
files cite a paragraph by its identifier (CG-01, CG-02 and so on). A class code is cited by the paragraph that
describes it.

## General

**CG-01. Premium basis.** Premium is charged per USD 100 of payroll in each class code at the rate underwriting sets
for that code. Payroll is reported for the policy period being audited.

**CG-02. Assigning codes.** An employer is assigned the class code that describes its principal business. An employee
whose work is described by another code in this guide is reported under that code. An employer may carry several codes.

**CG-03. Payroll.** Payroll is the gross remuneration paid to employees for the period: wages, salaries, commissions
and bonuses. Expense reimbursements that the employer can document, such as travel and lodging costs, are not payroll.

**CG-05. Owners and executive officers.** An owner or executive officer who has filed an election of exclusion is not
counted. An owner who is included is counted under the code for the work the owner does.

**CG-06. Subcontractors.** Payments to a subcontractor who does not carry workers' compensation insurance for its own
workers may be treated as payroll of the employer, under the code for the work the subcontractor performed.

**CG-07. Division of payroll.** When an employee performs work in more than one classification and the employer keeps
records of the time spent in each, the employee's payroll may be divided between the codes.

## Class codes

**CG-04. C-110 Clerical office employees.** Employees whose duties are confined to an office: correspondence,
bookkeeping, dispatching by telephone or radio, drafting and estimating at a desk, and professional staff who work in
the office.

**CG-11. R-310 Roofing.** Installation, repair and removal of roofs and roof coverings on any building, including
work on scaffolds and ladders at the roof line.

**CG-12. R-320 Siding and gutters.** Installation and repair of exterior siding, gutters, downspouts and exterior trim
below the roof line. Roofing work is described by CG-11.

**CG-13. L-620 Landscaping and lawn care.** Lawn mowing, planting, mulching and the care of grounds.

**CG-15. H-420 Residential homebuilding.** Construction and remodeling of dwellings: framing, drywall, interior
finish, carpentry and general labor at the building site. Roofing work is described by CG-11 and electrical wiring
by CG-21.

**CG-21. E-510 Electrical wiring.** Installation and repair of electrical wiring and fixtures inside buildings,
including service connections.

**CG-22. M-830 Metal fabrication shop.** Cutting, bending and welding of sheet and structural metal in a shop.

**CG-31. T-610 Courier and delivery drivers.** Drivers of vans and light trucks delivering parcels and documents,
and helpers who ride on the delivery vehicles.

**CG-35. G-950 Parking garage attendants.** Parking and retrieving customer vehicles.

**CG-41. F-710 Restaurants.** Preparation and service of meals: kitchen staff, servers, hosts and dishwashers.

**CG-42. F-720 Off-site caterers.** Preparation of food and its service at events away from the employer's premises,
including the catering crew of an employer that also runs a restaurant.

**CG-51. N-910 Home health care.** Personal care and nursing services in clients' homes.

Linden Shore Mutual, workers' compensation, Maryland. Edition of July 2025. Internal use by underwriting and premium
audit.

This excerpt holds the general paragraphs and the class codes our current new-business employers fall under. Audit
files cite a paragraph by its identifier (CG-01, CG-02 and so on). A class code is cited by the paragraph that
describes it.

## General

**CG-01. Premium basis.** Premium is charged per USD 100 of payroll in each class code at the rate underwriting sets
for that code. Payroll is reported for the policy period being audited.

**CG-02. Assigning codes.** An employer is assigned the class code that describes its principal business. An employee
whose work is described by another code in this guide is reported under that code. An employer may carry several codes.

**CG-03. Payroll.** Payroll is the gross remuneration paid to employees for the period: wages, salaries, commissions
and bonuses. Expense reimbursements that the employer can document, such as travel and lodging costs, are not payroll.

**CG-05. Owners and executive officers.** An owner or executive officer who has filed an election of exclusion is not
counted. An owner who is included is counted under the code for the work the owner does.

**CG-06. Subcontractors.** Payments to a subcontractor who does not carry workers' compensation insurance for its own
workers may be treated as payroll of the employer, under the code for the work the subcontractor performed.

**CG-07. Division of payroll.** When an employee performs work in more than one classification and the employer keeps
records of the time spent in each, the employee's payroll may be divided between the codes.

## Class codes

**CG-04. C-110 Clerical office employees.** Employees whose duties are confined to an office: correspondence,
bookkeeping, dispatching by telephone or radio, drafting and estimating at a desk, and professional staff who work in
the office.

**CG-11. R-310 Roofing.** Installation, repair and removal of roofs and roof coverings on any building, including
work on scaffolds and ladders at the roof line.

**CG-12. R-320 Siding and gutters.** Installation and repair of exterior siding, gutters, downspouts and exterior trim
below the roof line. Roofing work is described by CG-11.

**CG-13. L-620 Landscaping and lawn care.** Lawn mowing, planting, mulching and the care of grounds.

**CG-15. H-420 Residential homebuilding.** Construction and remodeling of dwellings: framing, drywall, interior
finish, carpentry and general labor at the building site. Roofing work is described by CG-11 and electrical wiring
by CG-21.

**CG-21. E-510 Electrical wiring.** Installation and repair of electrical wiring and fixtures inside buildings,
including service connections.

**CG-22. M-830 Metal fabrication shop.** Cutting, bending and welding of sheet and structural metal in a shop.

**CG-31. T-610 Courier and delivery drivers.** Drivers of vans and light trucks delivering parcels and documents,
and helpers who ride on the delivery vehicles.

**CG-35. G-950 Parking garage attendants.** Parking and retrieving customer vehicles.

**CG-41. F-710 Restaurants.** Preparation and service of meals: kitchen staff, servers, hosts and dishwashers.

**CG-42. F-720 Off-site caterers.** Preparation of food and its service at events away from the employer's premises,
including the catering crew of an employer that also runs a restaurant.

**CG-51. N-910 Home health care.** Personal care and nursing services in clients' homes.

Linden Shore Mutual, workers' compensation, Maryland. Edition of July 2025. Internal use by underwriting and premium
audit.

This excerpt holds the general paragraphs and the class codes our current new-business employers fall under. Audit
files cite a paragraph by its identifier (CG-01, CG-02 and so on). A class code is cited by the paragraph that
describes it.

## General

**CG-01. Premium basis.** Premium is charged per USD 100 of payroll in each class code at the rate underwriting sets
for that code. Payroll is reported for the policy period being audited.

**CG-02. Assigning codes.** An employer is assigned the class code that describes its principal business. An employee
whose work is described by another code in this guide is reported under that code. An employer may carry several codes.

**CG-03. Payroll.** Payroll is the gross remuneration paid to employees for the period: wages, salaries, commissions
and bonuses. Expense reimbursements that the employer can document, such as travel and lodging costs, are not payroll.

**CG-05. Owners and executive officers.** An owner or executive officer who has filed an election of exclusion is not
counted. An owner who is included is counted under the code for the work the owner does.

**CG-06. Subcontractors.** Payments to a subcontractor who does not carry workers' compensation insurance for its own
workers may be treated as payroll of the employer, under the code for the work the subcontractor performed.

**CG-07. Division of payroll.** When an employee performs work in more than one classification and the employer keeps
records of the time spent in each, the employee's payroll may be divided between the codes.

## Class codes

**CG-04. C-110 Clerical office employees.** Employees whose duties are confined to an office: correspondence,
bookkeeping, dispatching by telephone or radio, drafting and estimating at a desk, and professional staff who work in
the office.

**CG-11. R-310 Roofing.** Installation, repair and removal of roofs and roof coverings on any building, including
work on scaffolds and ladders at the roof line.

**CG-12. R-320 Siding and gutters.** Installation and repair of exterior siding, gutters, downspouts and exterior trim
below the roof line. Roofing work is described by CG-11.

**CG-13. L-620 Landscaping and lawn care.** Lawn mowing, planting, mulching and the care of grounds.

**CG-15. H-420 Residential homebuilding.** Construction and remodeling of dwellings: framing, drywall, interior
finish, carpentry and general labor at the building site. Roofing work is described by CG-11 and electrical wiring
by CG-21.

**CG-21. E-510 Electrical wiring.** Installation and repair of electrical wiring and fixtures inside buildings,
including service connections.

**CG-22. M-830 Metal fabrication shop.** Cutting, bending and welding of sheet and structural metal in a shop.

**CG-31. T-610 Courier and delivery drivers.** Drivers of vans and light trucks delivering parcels and documents,
and helpers who ride on the delivery vehicles.

**CG-35. G-950 Parking garage attendants.** Parking and retrieving customer vehicles.

**CG-41. F-710 Restaurants.** Preparation and service of meals: kitchen staff, servers, hosts and dishwashers.

**CG-42. F-720 Off-site caterers.** Preparation of food and its service at events away from the employer's premises,
including the catering crew of an employer that also runs a restaurant.

**CG-51. N-910 Home health care.** Personal care and nursing services in clients' homes.

Linden Shore Mutual, workers' compensation, Maryland. Edition of July 2025. Internal use by underwriting and premium
audit.

This excerpt holds the general paragraphs and the class codes our current new-business employers fall under. Audit
files cite a paragraph by its identifier (CG-01, CG-02 and so on). A class code is cited by the paragraph that
describes it.

## General

**CG-01. Premium basis.** Premium is charged per USD 100 of payroll in each class code at the rate underwriting sets
for that code. Payroll is reported for the policy period being audited.

**CG-02. Assigning codes.** An employer is assigned the class code that describes its principal business. An employee
whose work is described by another code in this guide is reported under that code. An employer may carry several codes.

**CG-03. Payroll.** Payroll is the gross remuneration paid to employees for the period: wages, salaries, commissions
and bonuses. Expense reimbursements that the employer can document, such as travel and lodging costs, are not payroll.

**CG-05. Owners and executive officers.** An owner or executive officer who has filed an election of exclusion is not
counted. An owner who is included is counted under the code for the work the owner does.

**CG-06. Subcontractors.** Payments to a subcontractor who does not carry workers' compensation insurance for its own
workers may be treated as payroll of the employer, under the code for the work the subcontractor performed.

**CG-07. Division of payroll.** When an employee performs work in more than one classification and the employer keeps
records of the time spent in each, the employee's payroll may be divided between the codes.

## Class codes

**CG-04. C-110 Clerical office employees.** Employees whose duties are confined to an office: correspondence,
bookkeeping, dispatching by telephone or radio, drafting and estimating at a desk, and professional staff who work in
the office.

**CG-11. R-310 Roofing.** Installation, repair and removal of roofs and roof coverings on any building, including
work on scaffolds and ladders at the roof line.

**CG-12. R-320 Siding and gutters.** Installation and repair of exterior siding, gutters, downspouts and exterior trim
below the roof line. Roofing work is described by CG-11.

**CG-13. L-620 Landscaping and lawn care.** Lawn mowing, planting, mulching and the care of grounds.

**CG-15. H-420 Residential homebuilding.** Construction and remodeling of dwellings: framing, drywall, interior
finish, carpentry and general labor at the building site. Roofing work is described by CG-11 and electrical wiring
by CG-21.

**CG-21. E-510 Electrical wiring.** Installation and repair of electrical wiring and fixtures inside buildings,
including service connections.

**CG-22. M-830 Metal fabrication shop.** Cutting, bending and welding of sheet and structural metal in a shop.

**CG-31. T-610 Courier and delivery drivers.** Drivers of vans and light trucks delivering parcels and documents,
and helpers who ride on the delivery vehicles.

**CG-35. G-950 Parking garage attendants.** Parking and retrieving customer vehicles.

**CG-41. F-710 Restaurants.** Preparation and service of meals: kitchen staff, servers, hosts and dishwashers.

**CG-42. F-720 Off-site caterers.** Preparation of food and its service at events away from the employer's premises,
including the catering crew of an employer that also runs a restaurant.

**CG-51. N-910 Home health care.** Personal care and nursing services in clients' homes.

def process_employer(
    guide_path: str | Path, employer_path: str | Path, interview_path: str | Path, *,
    files: EmployerFiles = EmployerFiles(),
) -> ProcessingResult:
    """Reread authoritative paths; return calculations/evidence without writing files.

    Adapters handle corroborated restaurant, legal-office and contractor duties.
    Unsupported contexts and ambiguous/missing evidence are OPEN, never guessed.
    """
    issues = []
    try:
        inputs = read_inputs(guide_path, employer_path)
    except InputError as exc:
        return ProcessingResult(open_items=(OpenItem("Input sources", str(exc), "Supply readable, valid authoritative source documents."),))
    try:
        interview = read_markdown(interview_path)
        interview_errors = ()
    except InputError as exc:
        interview = None
        interview_errors = (str(exc),)
        issues.append(OpenItem("Interview", str(exc), "Provide the preserved authoritative interview for house rules."))
    documents = {str(doc.path.relative_to(inputs.records_root)): doc for doc in inputs.records}

    def get(filename, expected_type):
        document = documents.get(filename)
        if not isinstance(document, expected_type):
            issues.append(OpenItem(filename, f"Required evidence {inputs.records_root / filename} is missing or has the wrong format.", "Provide the authoritative source at the configured location."))
            return None
        return document

    business = get(files.business, MarkdownSource)
    notes = get(files.notes, MarkdownSource)
    payroll = get(files.payroll, CSVSource)
    application = get(files.application, MarkdownSource)
    legal_office = bool(business and re.search(r"\bis (?:an? )?(?:[a-z0-9-]+ )?law office\b", " ".join(business.text.lower().split())))
    contractor = bool(business and re.search(r"\b(?:replaces roofs|(?:installs|performs) (?:roofing|siding)|roofing and siding contractor)\b", " ".join(business.text.lower().split())))
    receipt_table = None if legal_office or contractor else get(files.receipts, CSVSource)
    period = _period(business, issues)
    receipts = _receipts(receipt_table, period, issues)
    if payroll is None:
        return ProcessingResult(inputs=inputs, period=period, receipts=receipts, open_items=tuple(issues))
    try:
        register = records_from_csv(payroll)
    except AllocationError as exc:
        issues.append(OpenItem("Payroll register", str(exc), "Correct the authoritative register; no payroll total is invented."))
        return ProcessingResult(inputs=inputs, period=period, receipts=receipts, open_items=tuple(issues))
    evaluator = RuleEvaluator(inputs.guide, interview, source_errors=interview_errors)
    if legal_office:
        # Lazy import keeps the small evidence adapter separate while sharing
        # the established workflow models and finalization calculations.
        from legal_office_processing import evaluate_legal_office
        log = get(files.site_signins, CSVSource)
        office = evaluate_legal_office(inputs, business, notes, log, payroll, register, period, evaluator, files)
        issues.extend(office.open_items)
        return _finish(inputs, payroll, period, receipts, register, office.decisions, issues, application, interview, interview_errors,
                       proposals=office.proposals, site_visits=office.site_visits)
    if contractor:
        from contractor_processing import evaluate_contractor, compare_employee_application
        crew = get(files.crew_timesheets, CSVSource)
        log = get(files.site_signins, CSVSource)
        evaluated = evaluate_contractor(inputs, business, notes, crew, log, payroll, register, period, evaluator, files)
        issues.extend(evaluated.open_items)
        result = _finish(inputs, payroll, period, receipts, register, evaluated.decisions, issues, application, interview, interview_errors,
                         site_visits=evaluated.site_visits)
        comparisons, comparison_issues = compare_employee_application(result)
        return replace(result, roofing_days=evaluated.roofing_days, governing_field=evaluated.governing_field,
                       employee_comparisons=comparisons, unassigned_site_records=evaluated.unassigned_site_records,
                       open_items=result.open_items + comparison_issues)
    business_text = business.text.lower() if business else ""
    notes_text = notes.text.lower() if notes else ""
    context_text = business_text + "\n" + notes_text
    context_refs = tuple(_source(doc, "business description" if doc is business else "auditor field notes") for doc in (business, notes) if doc is not None)
    mapped_names = {files.business, files.notes, files.payroll, files.application, files.receipts}
    unmapped = [doc for name, doc in documents.items() if name not in mapped_names and not _adjustment_evidence(doc)]
    extra_columns = set(payroll.columns) - {"employee_id", "name", "position", "wages_paid"}
    if unmapped or extra_columns:
        issues.append(OpenItem("Unmapped employer evidence", "Additional source files or payroll columns are outside this adapter's schema and may change actual-duty findings.", "Review and map the additional evidence before assigning employee codes.", tuple(_source(doc, "unmapped evidence") for doc in unmapped) + ((_source(payroll, "unmapped payroll columns"),) if extra_columns else ())))
    restaurant = bool(re.search(r"\bis (?:an? )?(?:\d+-seat )?restaurant\b|\bthis restaurant\b", business_text))
    dining_observed = "kitchen" in notes_text and "dining room" in notes_text
    mixed_observed = "catering" in notes_text and "prepare" in notes_text and "serve" in notes_text and "venue" in notes_text and "restaurant shifts" in notes_text
    # This narrow adapter does not interpret individual exceptions or alternative
    # occupations. Any such evidence requires review, rather than a title match.
    exception = bool(re.search(r"\b(?:actual duties|misleading|bookkeep\w*|clerical|office|driver|roof\w*|siding|landscap\w*|nurs\w*|parking)\b", notes_text))
    # Business descriptions may legitimately mention customers' office events or
    # an outside accountant. Explicit employee-duty exceptions still need review.
    exception = exception or bool(re.search(r"\b(?:actual duties|misleading|bookkeep\w*|clerical)\b", business_text))
    negated_duties = bool(re.search(r"\b(?:no|not|never|without|unconfirmed|unknown)\b[^.!?\n]{0,60}\b(?:kitchen|dining room|restaurant shifts|prepare|serve|meal preparation|duties)\b", context_text))
    negated_industry = bool(re.search(r"\b(?:no|not|never)\b[^.!?\n]{0,30}\brestaurant\b", business_text))
    context_conflict = exception or negated_duties or negated_industry or bool(unmapped) or bool(extra_columns)
    if context_conflict:
        issues.append(OpenItem("Duty evidence requires review", "The supplied prose contains negated observations, employee duty exceptions or other occupations outside this adapter's supported restaurant context.", "Review actual duties and resolve exceptions before assigning a code; titles do not override those statements.", context_refs))
    timesheets_present = any("timesheet" in Path(name).stem.lower() for name in documents)
    no_timesheets = bool(re.search(r"\bno (?:employee )?timesheets (?:are available|exist|were kept)\b", context_text))
    positive_timesheets = bool(re.search(r"(?:^|[.!?]\s+)\s*(?:employee )?timesheets (?:are|were) (?:available|kept|provided)\b|\b(?:we|employer) (?:has|have|keeps|kept) (?:employee )?timesheets\b", context_text, re.M))
    sheets = True if timesheets_present or positive_timesheets else False if no_timesheets else None
    has_catering = any(_CATERING_POSITION.match(str(row.values.get("position", ""))) for row in payroll.rows)
    if has_catering and sheets is not False:
        issues.append(OpenItem("Employee timesheets", "No record confirms that employee timesheets are unavailable, or timesheet records are present; the verified mixed-duty rule requires no employee timesheets.", "Confirm timesheet availability and provide records or an authoritative no-timesheets statement.", context_refs))
    if has_catering and (timesheets_present or positive_timesheets) and no_timesheets:
        issues.append(OpenItem("Conflicting timesheet evidence", "Field notes deny available timesheets but a source or another statement indicates timesheets exist.", "Resolve the conflicting evidence before applying the no-timesheets rule.", context_refs))
    decisions = {}
    for employee, row in zip(register, payroll.rows):
        evidence = (employee.source, *context_refs)
        position = str(row.values.get("position", ""))
        if period is None or not restaurant or business is None or notes is None or context_conflict:
            decision = _pending("Confirm this employee's actual duties, restaurant industry and exact audit period; this adapter has no rule for other contexts.", evidence)
        elif _CATERING_POSITION.match(position):
            facts = RuleFacts(employee.employee_id, "restaurant", "catering_crew", period.start, period.end,
                              complete=bool(receipts and receipts.coverage_confirmed),
                              evidence_sources=(*evidence, *(receipts.sources if receipts else ())),
                              mixed_catering_restaurant_duties=mixed_observed,
                              employee_timesheets_available=sheets,
                              total_gross_receipts=receipts.total if receipts else None,
                              offsite_catering_receipts=receipts.offsite if receipts else None)
            guide_refs, verified_guide = _guide_refs(evaluator, ("CG-02", "CG-07", "CG-41", "CG-42"))
            decision = evaluator.evaluate("catering_receipts", facts) if verified_guide else _pending("The current guide's catering definitions differ from verified CG-02/CG-07/CG-41/CG-42; obtain auditor review.", facts.evidence_sources, guide_refs)
        elif _RESTAURANT_POSITION.fullmatch(position) and dining_observed:
            decision = _direct_restaurant(evaluator, evidence)
        else:
            decision = _pending("Register title and supplied observations do not establish supported actual duties; obtain employee duty evidence or an applicable rule.", evidence)
        decisions[employee.employee_id] = decision
        if decision.status == "OPEN":
            issues.append(OpenItem(f"{employee.name} [{employee.employee_id}]", decision.reason, "; ".join(decision.required_confirmation), decision.evidence_sources + decision.rule_sources))
    return _finish(inputs, payroll, period, receipts, register, decisions, issues, application, interview, interview_errors)


def _finish(inputs, payroll, period, receipts, register, decisions, issues, application, interview, interview_errors, *, proposals=None, site_visits=None):
    """Share the existing exact-cent allocation, comparison and reconciliation."""
    allocation = allocate_payroll(register, decisions)
    # Rebuild the register from the loaded raw rows, independently of emitted lines.
    independent = reconcile_payroll(records_from_csv(payroll), allocation.lines)
    if not independent.reconciled:
        raise AllocationError("Independent payroll reconciliation failed")
    adjuster = PayrollAdjuster(inputs.guide, interview, source_errors=interview_errors)
    # No monetary adjustment schema is adapted in this first restaurant path.
    # Use the existing component for the empty evidenced set and expose any
    # candidate documents as OPEN, without accepting unbound external claims.
    adjustments = adjuster.evaluate_batch()
    unadapted_adjustments = False
    for document in inputs.records:
        if _adjustment_evidence(document):
            unadapted_adjustments = True
            issues.append(OpenItem("Unadapted adjustment evidence", f"{document.path} may contain adjustment evidence that has not been supplied as verified typed cases.", "Provide sourced subcontractor/travel cases before treating adjustment processing as complete.", (_source(document, "adjustment evidence"),)))
    cents = {code: _cents(amount, code) for code, amount in allocation.by_code.items()}
    for code, amount in adjustments.by_code.items():
        cents[code] = cents.get(code, 0) + _cents(amount, code)
    by_code = {code: _money(amount) for code, amount in sorted(cents.items())}
    comparison = _application(application, register, allocation, by_code, unadapted_adjustments, issues)
    return ProcessingResult(inputs, period, receipts, register, decisions, allocation, adjustments, by_code, comparison, independent, tuple(issues), proposals or {}, site_visits or {})

# Homebuilding Processing Implementation Plan

**Goal:** Integrate source-bound general homebuilding, office-site rules and subcontractor adjustments while preserving all three existing employer paths.

**Design:** Add a narrow `homebuilding_processing.py` adapter and configurable payment/certificate filenames. INSURANCE-01 — Implement Step 1: Reusable input reader.

Create a minimal Python input-reading component under skills/class-code-assistant/.

Requirements:
1. Accept configurable paths for the Classification Guide and employer records.
2. Read Markdown and CSV files without hard-coding the six employers or their answers.
3. Preserve classification paragraph identifiers and source filenames.
4. Parse payroll money using Decimal, not floating-point arithmetic.
5. Validate missing files, malformed CSVs, and invalid payroll amounts with clear errors.
6. Add focused tests using small synthetic fixtures.
7. Run the reader against /home/maxg/insurance01-inputs and report the results.

For this step, do not classify employees, calculate allocations, or generate final deliverables.

Preserve existing files and Entire capture. Do not commit, push, synchronize, deploy, or upload anything.

Explain the design and tests performed.

INSURANCE-01 — Implement a reusable classification-rule evaluator.

Build on the existing input reader without rewriting it.

Read the original Classification Guide and preserved interview transcript. Implement the verified house practices for contractor office site visits, roofing/siding thresholds, courier weekly ride-alongs, and the catering gross-receipts threshold.

Preserve each rule's source reference and its applicability boundaries. Do not apply contractor-specific rules to unrelated industries.

If evidence is insufficient or no rule exists, return an OPEN decision with the reason and required human confirmation. Never invent a classification.

Add focused synthetic tests for thresholds, exceptions, and missing evidence. Run them and report results.

Do not calculate final payroll allocations or generate deliverables yet. Do not commit, push, synchronize, or upload anything. Preserve Entire capture.

INSURANCE-01 — Implement the base payroll allocation component.

Build on the existing input reader and classification evaluator without rewriting them.

1. Implement reusable payroll allocation functions using Python Decimal, preserving amounts to the cent.
2. Accept verified classification decisions and employee payroll records as inputs.
3. Aggregate wages by classification code without double-counting.
4. Preserve each employee's source record and applicable rule reference.
5. Keep unresolved classifications OPEN, with their payroll amounts tracked separately rather than assigning a guessed code.
6. Reconcile allocated and unresolved wages against the payroll register.
7. Add focused synthetic tests for correct totals, multiple classifications, missing decisions, and rounding.
8. Run tests and report results.

For this step, exclude subcontractor payments and travel allowance adjustments; we will implement those separately.

Do not generate final deliverables yet. Do not hard-code employer answers. Do not commit, push, synchronize, or upload anything. Preserve Entire capture.

INSURANCE-01 — Implement reusable payroll adjustments.

Build on the existing reader, rule evaluator, and payroll allocator without rewriting them.

Implement:

1. Subcontractor adjustments: verify certificates cover the entire audit period; include 60% of payments without valid coverage under the documented work code.
2. Treat expired or missing certificates according to Nadia's confirmed rule. Flag mismatched subcontractor names as OPEN rather than assuming identity.

Report test results, limitations, and remaining OPEN cases.

## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/home/maxg/.codex/skills/.system`
- `r1` = `/home/maxg/.codex/plugins/cache/fellowship-apprentice-workspace/apprentice-workspace/local/library/skills`
- `r2` = `/home/maxg/.codex/plugins/cache/openai-curated-remote`
- `r3` = `/home/maxg/.codex/plugins/cache/openai-curated-remote/sites/1.1.3/skills`
- `r4` = `/home/maxg/.codex/plugins/cache/openai-curated-remote/superpowers/7.0.1/skills`
- `r5` = `/home/maxg/.codex/plugins/cache/openai-curated-remote/work-pets/0.1.6/skills`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
- apprentice-workspace:choose-automation-approach: Guide an adaptive interview to choose proportionate deployment, integration, credential, and high-stakes controls when designing or revisiting an automated workflow. (file: r1/choose-automation-approach/SKILL.md)
- apprentice-workspace:command-failed: A command, install or setup step failed and you are not sure what to do with it. Use when the user says it did not work, it is broken, I got an error, I am stuck, 跑不起來, 壞掉了, 卡住了, or pastes an error they have not explained. Also use when a setup step has been retried more than once without changing anything. (file: r1/command-failed/SKILL.md)
- apprentice-workspace:create-skill: Scaffold new Claude Code skill following architecture principles (three-tier disclosure, gotchas, eval). Use when user asks to create, build, or author a new skill or SKILL.md. (file: r1/create-skill/SKILL.md)
- apprentice-workspace:diagnosing-bugs: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow. (file: r1/diagnosing-bugs/SKILL.md)
- apprentice-workspace:digest-doc: Digest a document the business already has into a page-sourced fact-sheet. One family: article - anything written down, from a supplier agreement to a printed procedure to a web page. Use on digest this, summarize this document, or a document the owner hands you. (file: r1/digest-doc/SKILL.md)
- apprentice-workspace:drive-portal: Use when driving a legacy or government web form through the Chrome extension — popup uploads, nested framesets, derived hidden fields, or a save that fails with an error naming nothing. (file: r1/drive-portal/SKILL.md)
- apprentice-workspace:explain: Use when the reader is unfamiliar with a field and needs to reach competence, not merely asking how something works. Applies the explanation register; explanation and digest stay separate. (file: r1/explain/SKILL.md)
- apprentice-workspace:flowchart: Build a flowchart, system map or process diagram as validated inline SVG - ISO 5807 symbols, automatic layered placement, four self-tested checks. Use whenever a document needs a diagram. (file: r1/flowchart/SKILL.md)
- apprentice-workspace:grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases. (file: r1/grilling/SKILL.md)
- apprentice-workspace:interview-recording: Use when an interview recording must become a session record: transcribe with speaker labels, refine, reduce to key points, decisions, open questions. Fires on transcribe this interview. (file: r1/interview-recording/SKILL.md)
- apprentice-workspace:kb-restructure: Rename, move, re-nest, or ARCHIVE a KB file/dir without breaking inbound refs — discover, classify live-vs-historical, execute, fix, verify (split/merge staged). Fire on any structural mutation ask. (file: r1/kb-restructure/SKILL.md)
- apprentice-workspace:onboarding: Walk a new AI Fellowship apprentice from a fresh machine to a working workspace, verifying each step that a command can verify and recording the ones only they can confirm. Use on an apprentice's first session, and again on any later session while the record still shows unfinished items. Do not use it to set up a client engagement — that is playbook-environment-setup.md, which assumes everything this skill installs. (file: r1/onboarding/SKILL.md)
- apprentice-workspace:scan-agent-skill: Scan a local agent skill package for prompt injection, data exfiltration, malicious code, obfuscation, and risky tool use with a pinned security scanner. Use before installing or executing a third-party skill, after modifying a skill, or before handing a skill over. Do not use a clean scan as proof that a skill is safe. (file: r1/scan-agent-skill/SKILL.md)
- apprentice-workspace:setup: Set up the apprentice workspace folder, with its rules, in the repository you are working in. Use once in each new repository, or when apprentice-workspace/ is missing or incomplete. (file: r1/setup/SKILL.md)
- apprentice-workspace:video-to-markdown: Turn a screen recording into one markdown file — the full transcript as the spine, screenshots interleaved at the moment each screen was on display. Use on a screen recording of someone doing their work, a walkthrough, a demo, plus an optional audio-only continuation file. (file: r1/video-to-markdown/SKILL.md)
- apprentice-workspace:workspace-help: Answer an apprentice's "how do I ...?" and "where does this go?" questions about this workspace by listing what is actually in it right now and reading its manifests, never from a remembered inventory. Use whenever someone asks which skills they have, where a file belongs, what a playbook or skill is for, what they are allowed to edit, or which tool to reach for. Do not use it to run a playbook or to set anything up. (file: r1/workspace-help/SKILL.md)
- apprentice-workspace:writing-for-agents: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md. (file: r1/writing-for-agents/SKILL.md)
- apprentice-workspace:youtube-transcript: Turn a video URL into a clean markdown transcript — free captions when the video carries them, a local transcription pass when it does not. Triggers on youtube transcript, transcribe this video, get the text of that walkthrough. (file: r1/youtube-transcript/SKILL.md)
- plugin-management:plugin-management: Discover and suggest relevant plugins, inspect app permissions and dependencies, and manage plugin connections or removal. Use when the user asks about plugins or when a task would materially benefit from an external app, account, service, or data source that available tools cannot access. (file: r2/plugin-management/0.1.0/skills/plugin-management/SKILL.md)
- sites:sites: Use Sites when the user wants a website built for them (including a landing page, portfolio, dashboard, portal, tracker, hub, game, event registration, or tool), requests changes to a website already built with Sites, wants to publish a website with Sites, or wants to manage Sites hosting. (file: r3/sites/SKILL.md)
- sites:sites-remix: Remix a Site built with the Sites plugin into a new Site. Use when the user has identified the source Site and asks to remix it. (file: r3/sites-remix/SKILL.md)
- superpowers:brainstorming: You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, modifying behavior, or planning anything new, in software or out of it (a talk, a business, a renovation). (file: r4/brainstorming/SKILL.md)
- superpowers:diagnosing-superpowers: Use when a superpowers session went wrong and your human partner wants to know why — repeated work, ignored plans, stumbles, poor results, a skill that didn't fire, "it took too long", "why is it so expensive", "what is it doing" — or wants to build a bug report for the superpowers maintainers, for the current session or a past one identified by id or path, on any harness. (file: r4/diagnosing-superpowers/SKILL.md)
- superpowers:receiving-code-review: Use when receiving code review feedback, before implementing suggestions, especially if feedback seems unclear or technically questionable - requires technical rigor and verification, not performative agreement or blind implementation (file: r4/receiving-code-review/SKILL.md)
- superpowers:requesting-code-review: Use when completing tasks, implementing major features, or before merging to verify work meets requirements (file: r4/requesting-code-review/SKILL.md)
- superpowers:systematic-debugging: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes (file: r4/systematic-debugging/SKILL.md)
- superpowers:test-driven-development: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code (file: r4/test-driven-development/SKILL.md)
- superpowers:using-superpowers: Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring skill invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions (file: r4/using-superpowers/SKILL.md)
- superpowers:verification-before-completion: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always (file: r4/verification-before-completion/SKILL.md)
- superpowers:writing-plans: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code (file: r4/writing-plans/SKILL.md)
- superpowers:writing-skills: Use when creating new skills, editing existing skills, or verifying skills work before deployment (file: r4/writing-skills/SKILL.md)
- work-pets:create-pet: Create, repair, validate, preview, upload, or activate an animated v2 pet in ChatGPT Work mode from a character idea, brand cue, or reference image. Use for new ChatGPT Pets, custom mascots, non-pixel styles, and unattached sprite sheets requiring nine animation states plus sixteen look directions. Preserve Library artifacts and Pets MCP lifecycle behavior. Exclude real pets, standalone images, and other-app pets; clarify before invoking. (file: r5/create-pet/SKILL.md)
- work-pets:pets: List, inspect, select, download, or delete animated pets in ChatGPT Work mode. Use for an explicit pet in ChatGPT or established ChatGPT Pets context. Exclude real-world and other-app pets; clarify before invoking. (file: r5/pets/SKILL.md)
- work-pets:update-pet: Inspect, validate, preview, repair, or update a custom pet in ChatGPT Work mode, including its name, description, or sprite sheet. Use for a pet in ChatGPT or established ChatGPT Pets context. Exclude real-world and other-app pets; clarify before invoking. (file: r5/update-pet/SKILL.md)

# Homebuilding Processing Implementation Plan

**Goal:** Integrate source-bound general homebuilding, office-site rules and subcontractor adjustments while preserving all three existing employer paths.

**Design:** Add a narrow `homebuilding_processing.py` adapter and configurable payment/certificate filenames. Reuse the reader, evaluator office rule, allocator, existing adjustment component, application attribution and shared finalizer. The internal adapter reads every supplied payment/certificate row; no external unbound monetary-case API is introduced. Only `employer_processing.py` and its API documentation change among existing files.

**Employees and owner:** CG-02/CG-15 support corroborated construction duties; the roofing/siding 15-day rule is inapplicable to general homebuilding. Derive governing evidence from field wages and check that recorded competing subcontractor exposures cannot overturn it. Use confirmed/possible office visit bounds as in Bay Crest. Preserve the estimator OPEN where four matched visits plus an unattributed row can cross the threshold. Record documented owner election separately; never invent or subtract owner wages absent from the register. Contradictory owner register presence stays OPEN.

**Subcontractors:** Bind original payment amounts/invoices/work/dates and certificate names/dates to reader rows. Exact full-period certificates exclude payments. Missing coverage after examining the complete supplied inventory invokes the existing 60-percent component. Lexically related, differently named certificate candidates are attached solely for OPEN review, never identity or coverage acceptance. Counterfactual missing-coverage calculations may provide separate proposals; no guessed identity or proposal contributes verified money. General framing/drywall use CG-15, roofing CG-11. Missing inventories or malformed/duplicate monetary evidence cannot become a fabricated zero adjustment total.

**Accounting:** Reconcile employee wages independently, subcontractor payment basis independently, and confirmed payroll as register wages plus verified subcontractor additions. Keep unresolved employee classifications distinct from unresolved subcontractor payment basis. Class totals contain only verified assignments; proposed additions are separate. Missing critical monetary sources prevent a combined confirmation.

**Verification:** Synthetic fixtures cover full/expired/missing/mismatched certificates, dates/names/invoices, scope, owner evidence, four/five-day bounds, source completeness and exact cents. Actual data is checked through independent raw CSV sums. Preserve old result digests after removing only newly added empty fields. Protect 70 existing files by SHA-256; retain Entire capture and no Git writes or external actions.

- [ ] Add failing synthetic and actual-source integration tests.
- [ ] Implement the source-bound adapter, owner assessment, internal adjustment integration and combined reconciliation.
- [ ] Run the complete suite and a read-only independent review; resolve findings.
- [ ] Verify all actual rows/cents/references, previous result equality, protected files and Git status; report findings without final deliverables.

from dataclasses import replace
from decimal import Decimal, localcontext
import csv
import io
import os
from pathlib import Path
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

COMPONENT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(COMPONENT))
from employer_processing import EmployerFiles, process_employer
from test_contractor_processing import GUIDE as CONTRACTOR_GUIDE, INTERVIEW, SITE_HEADER

GUIDE = CONTRACTOR_GUIDE.replace("**CG-06.", "**CG-05. Owners and executive officers.** An owner or executive officer who has filed an election of exclusion is not\ncounted. An owner who is included is counted under the code for the work the owner does.\n\n**CG-06.") + """
**CG-15. H-420 Residential homebuilding.** Construction and remodeling of dwellings: framing, drywall, interior
finish, carpentry and general labor at the building site. Roofing work is described by CG-11 and electrical wiring
by CG-21.
"""
BUSINESS = """# Independent Homes: business description
Audit period January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025.
Independent Homes builds single-family houses: framing, drywall, finish carpentry and site labor with its own crew, and subcontractors for some trades.
Four employees. The owner, Excluded Person, has filed an election of exclusion and is not on the payroll register.
"""
NOTES = """# Auditor field notes
Office in a converted house; three houses under construction. The office manager, Manager One,
drives material and paperwork out to the sites and meets inspectors there; the owner calls it "running errands".
The estimator visits a site now and then to measure. The bookkeeper stays in the office.
Three subcontractors were paid in the period (framing, drywall and roofing). The owner says they are all insured; we
collected the certificates of insurance the owner could find.
"""
PAYROLL = """employee_id,name,position,wages_paid
H1,Field One,Carpenter,100.00
E1,Estimator One,Estimator,50.00
M1,Manager One,Office Manager,60.00
B1,Books One,Bookkeeper,40.00
"""
APPLICATION = """# Application
| Class code (employer's choice) | Employees | Payroll (USD) |
|---|---|---|
| H-420 | 1 | 100.00 |
| C-110 | 3 | 150.00 |
"""
PAYMENTS = """date,subcontractor,work,invoice,amount_paid
2025-03-01,FrameBuild Co.,framing,FRAME-1,50.00
2025-04-01,DryBuild,drywall,DRY-1,20.05
2025-05-01,RoofBuild,roofing,ROOF-1,30.00
"""
CERTIFICATES = """subcontractor,certificate_no,coverage_from,coverage_to
FrameBuild Co.,CERT-F,2025-01-01,2025-12-31
RoofBuild & Siding LLC,CERT-R,2025-01-01,2025-06-30
"""


class HomebuildingIntegrationTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.temp.cleanup)
        self.root = Path(self.temp.name)
        self.employer = self.root / "independent-homebuilding-inputs"
        self.employer.mkdir()
        self.guide = self.root / "guide.md"
        self.guide.write_text(GUIDE, encoding="utf-8")
        self.interview = self.root / "interview.md"
        self.interview.write_text(INTERVIEW, encoding="utf-8")
        for filename, text in {"business-description.md": BUSINESS, "field-notes.md": NOTES,
                               "payroll-register.csv": PAYROLL, "application.md": APPLICATION,
                               "subcontractor-payments.csv": PAYMENTS, "insurance-certificates.csv": CERTIFICATES}.items():
            (self.employer / filename).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        self.set_visits()

    def set_visits(self, estimator=3):
        rows = [f"2025-02-{index+1:02d},E1,Estimator One,Site A,09:00\n" for index in range(estimator)]
        rows += [f"2025-03-{index+1:02d},M1,Manager One,Site A,10:00\n" for index in range(5)]
        rows.append("2025-04-15,,County inspector,Site A,11:00\n")
        (self.employer / "site-signin-log.csv").write_text(SITE_HEADER + "".join(rows), encoding="utf-8")

    def run_homes(self, **kwargs):
        return process_employer(self.guide, self.employer, self.interview, **kwargs)

    def test_employee_rules_subcontractor_additions_and_combined_reconciliation(self):
        result = self.run_homes()
        self.assertEqual(result.allocation.by_code, {"H-420": Decimal("160.00"), "C-110": Decimal("90.00")})
        self.assertEqual(result.by_code, {"H-420": Decimal("172.03"), "C-110": Decimal("90.00")})
        self.assertEqual(result.governing_field.class_code, "H-420")
        self.assertEqual(result.adjustments.reconciliation.basis_total, Decimal("100.05"))
        self.assertEqual(result.adjustments.reconciliation.payroll_added, Decimal("12.03"))
        self.assertEqual(result.adjustments.reconciliation.nonpayroll, Decimal("58.02"))
        self.assertEqual(result.adjustments.reconciliation.unresolved_basis, Decimal("30.00"))
        self.assertTrue(result.combined_reconciliation.reconciled)
        self.assertEqual(result.combined_reconciliation.confirmed_payroll, Decimal("262.03"))
        self.assertEqual(result.owner_assessment.status, "EXCLUDED")
        self.assertEqual(result.owner_assessment.removed_wages, Decimal("0.00"))
        self.assertEqual(result.employee_comparisons["M1"].status, "CHANGE")

    def test_mismatched_certificate_remains_open_with_original_identity_and_proposal(self):
        result = self.run_homes()
        line = next(line for line in result.adjustments.lines if line.adjustment_id == "ROOF-1")
        self.assertEqual(line.status, "OPEN")
        self.assertEqual(line.input_record.subcontractor, "RoofBuild")
        self.assertEqual(line.certificates[0].subcontractor, "RoofBuild & Siding LLC")
        self.assertEqual(line.payroll_added, Decimal("0.00"))
        self.assertEqual(line.proposal.payroll_added, Decimal("18.00"))
        self.assertEqual(line.input_record.decision.class_code, "R-310")

    def test_exact_name_expired_certificate_adds_sixty_percent_even_before_lapse(self):
        path = self.employer / "insurance-certificates.csv"
        path.write_text(CERTIFICATES.replace("RoofBuild & Siding LLC", "RoofBuild"), encoding="utf-8")
        result = self.run_homes()
        self.assertEqual(result.adjustments.by_code, {"H-420": Decimal("12.03"), "R-310": Decimal("18.00")})
        self.assertEqual(result.combined_reconciliation.confirmed_payroll, Decimal("280.03"))
        path.write_text(CERTIFICATES.replace("RoofBuild & Siding LLC", "RoofBuild").replace("2025-06-30", "2025-12-31"), encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertNotIn("R-310", self.run_homes().adjustments.by_code)

    def test_unrelated_missing_certificate_is_not_hidden_by_a_different_vendor_certificate(self):
        line = next(line for line in self.run_homes().adjustments.lines if line.adjustment_id == "DRY-1")
        self.assertEqual(line.status, "VERIFIED")
        self.assertEqual(line.class_code, "H-420")
        self.assertEqual(line.payroll_added, Decimal("12.03"))
        self.assertTrue(line.input_record.raw_record)
        self.assertTrue(any(ref.locator == "CG-06" for ref in line.rule_sources))

    def test_missing_inventory_is_unknown_not_a_documented_missing_certificate(self):
        (self.employer / "insurance-certificates.csv").unlink()
        result = self.run_homes()
        self.assertEqual(result.adjustments.reconciliation.payroll_added, Decimal("0.00"))
        self.assertEqual(result.adjustments.reconciliation.unresolved_basis, Decimal("100.05"))
        self.assertTrue(all(line.status == "OPEN" for line in result.adjustments.lines))

    def test_missing_payments_do_not_fabricate_a_confirmed_combined_total(self):
        (self.employer / "subcontractor-payments.csv").unlink()
        result = self.run_homes()
        self.assertIsNone(result.combined_reconciliation)
        self.assertTrue(result.open_items)

    def test_duplicate_invoice_is_a_source_error_without_a_partial_combined_total(self):
        path = self.employer / "subcontractor-payments.csv"
        path.write_text(PAYMENTS + PAYMENTS.splitlines()[1] + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        result = self.run_homes()
        self.assertIsNone(result.combined_reconciliation)
        self.assertTrue(any("duplicate" in item.reason.lower() for item in result.open_items))

    def test_unknown_subcontractor_work_and_missing_certificate_dates_stay_open(self):
        path = self.employer / "subcontractor-payments.csv"
        path.write_text(PAYMENTS.replace("DryBuild,drywall", "DryBuild,unknown work"), encoding="utf-8")
        result = self.run_homes()
        self.assertEqual(next(line for line in result.adjustments.lines if line.adjustment_id == "DRY-1").status, "OPEN")
        (self.employer / "insurance-certificates.csv").write_text(CERTIFICATES.replace("2025-12-31", ""), encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertEqual(next(line for line in self.run_homes().adjustments.lines if line.adjustment_id == "FRAME-1").status, "OPEN")

    def test_four_confirmed_visits_plus_an_unattributed_date_preserves_open_classification(self):
        self.set_visits(estimator=4)
        result = self.run_homes()
        self.assertEqual(result.decisions["E1"].status, "OPEN")
        self.assertEqual(result.independent_reconciliation.unresolved_total, Decimal("50.00"))
        self.assertEqual(result.combined_reconciliation.confirmed_payroll, Decimal("262.03"))
        self.assertEqual(result.combined_reconciliation.classified_payroll, Decimal("212.03"))
        self.assertEqual(result.proposals["E1"].class_code, "C-110")

    def test_owner_exclusion_requires_the_documented_election_and_consistent_register(self):
        path = self.employer / "business-description.md"
        path.write_text(BUSINESS.replace("has filed an election of exclusion", "has not filed an election of exclusion"), encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertEqual(self.run_homes().owner_assessment.status, "OPEN")
        path.write_text(BUSINESS, encoding="utf-8")
        (self.employer / "payroll-register.csv").write_text(PAYROLL + "OWN,Excluded Person,Owner,10.00\n", encoding="utf-8")
        result = self.run_homes()
        self.assertEqual(result.owner_assessment.status, "OPEN")
        self.assertEqual(result.independent_reconciliation.register_total, Decimal("260.00"))
        self.assertEqual(result.decisions["OWN"].status, "OPEN")

    def test_competing_unresolved_subcontractor_exposure_cannot_silently_choose_governing_code(self):
        (self.employer / "subcontractor-payments.csv").write_text(PAYMENTS.replace("ROOF-1,30.00", "ROOF-1,1000.00"), encoding="utf-8")
        result = self.run_homes()
        self.assertIsNone(result.governing_field.class_code)
        self.assertEqual(result.decisions["M1"].status, "OPEN")

    def test_configurable_sources_reread_and_keep_low_precision_cents_exact(self):
        (self.employer / "subcontractor-payments.csv").rename(self.employer / "invoices.csv")
        files = replace(EmployerFiles(), subcontractor_payments="invoices.csv")
        with localcontext() as context:
            context.prec = 3
            result = self.run_homes(files=files)
        self.assertEqual(result.adjustments.reconciliation.payroll_added, Decimal("12.03"))
        self.assertEqual(result.combined_reconciliation.confirmed_payroll, Decimal("262.03"))
        self.assertTrue(all(line.input_record.source.source.endswith("invoices.csv") for line in result.adjustments.lines))


class LocalSevernIntegrationTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_actual_employees_all_eight_payments_and_separate_reconciliations(self):
        root = Path(os.environ.get("INSURANCE01_TEST_INPUTS", "/home/maxg/insurance01-inputs"))
        interview = COMPONENT.parents[1] / "interviews" / "ch03-premium-audit-20261105-0222(1).md"
        if not root.is_dir() or not interview.is_file():
            self.skipTest("Authoritative local development snapshots are unavailable")
        employer = root / "employer-files" / "severn-homebuilders"
        result = process_employer(root / "classification-guide.md", employer, interview)
        self.assertEqual(result.allocation.by_code, {"H-420": Decimal("344511.00"), "C-110": Decimal("46118.25")})
        self.assertEqual(result.decisions["SH-E06"].status, "OPEN")
        self.assertEqual(result.decisions["SH-E07"].class_code, "H-420")
        self.assertEqual(len(result.site_visits["SH-E06"]), 4)
        self.assertEqual(len(result.site_visits["SH-E07"]), 11)
        self.assertEqual(result.independent_reconciliation.register_total, Decimal("461879.70"))
        self.assertEqual(result.independent_reconciliation.unresolved_total, Decimal("71250.45"))
        self.assertEqual(len(result.adjustments.lines), 8)
        self.assertEqual(result.adjustments.by_code, {"H-420": Decimal("24693.39")})
        self.assertEqual(result.adjustments.reconciliation.basis_total, Decimal("152117.05"))
        self.assertEqual(result.adjustments.reconciliation.nonpayroll, Decimal("81478.01"))
        self.assertEqual(result.adjustments.reconciliation.unresolved_basis, Decimal("45945.65"))
        self.assertEqual(result.by_code, {"H-420": Decimal("369204.39"), "C-110": Decimal("46118.25")})
        self.assertEqual(result.combined_reconciliation.confirmed_payroll, Decimal("486573.09"))
        self.assertEqual(result.combined_reconciliation.classified_payroll, Decimal("415322.64"))
        self.assertTrue(result.combined_reconciliation.reconciled)
        self.assertTrue(result.independent_reconciliation.reconciled)
        self.assertTrue(result.adjustments.reconciliation.reconciled)
        proposed = sum(line.proposal.payroll_added for line in result.adjustments.lines if line.proposal)
        self.assertEqual(proposed, Decimal("27567.39"))
        self.assertEqual(result.owner_assessment.status, "EXCLUDED")
        wages = list(csv.DictReader(io.StringIO((employer / "payroll-register.csv").read_text())))
        payments = list(csv.DictReader(io.StringIO((employer / "subcontractor-payments.csv").read_text())))
        self.assertEqual(sum(Decimal(row["wages_paid"]) for row in wages), Decimal("461879.70"))
        self.assertEqual(sum(Decimal(row["amount_paid"]) for row in payments), Decimal("152117.05"))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

# Homebuilding Processing Implementation Plan

**Goal:** Integrate source-bound general homebuilding, office-site rules and subcontractor adjustments while preserving all three existing employer paths.

**Design:** Add a narrow `homebuilding_processing.py` adapter and configurable payment/certificate filenames. Reuse the reader, evaluator office rule, allocator, existing adjustment component, application attribution and shared finalizer. The internal adapter reads every supplied payment/certificate row; no external unbound monetary-case API is introduced. Only `employer_processing.py` and its API documentation change among existing files.
