    open_items: tuple[OpenItem, ...]


_GUIDE_WORDING = {
    "CG-02": "**CG-02. Assigning codes.** An employer is assigned the class code that describes its principal business. An employee whose work is described by another code in this guide is reported under that code. An employer may carry several codes.",
    "CG-04": "**CG-04. C-110 Clerical office employees.** Employees whose duties are confined to an office: correspondence, bookkeeping, dispatching by telephone or radio, drafting and estimating at a desk, and professional staff who work in the office.",
    "CG-07": "**CG-07. Division of payroll.** When an employee performs work in more than one classification and the employer keeps records of the time spent in each, the employee's payroll may be divided between the codes.",
    "CG-11": "**CG-11. R-310 Roofing.** Installation, repair and removal of roofs and roof coverings on any building, including work on scaffolds and ladders at the roof line.",
    "CG-12": "**CG-12. R-320 Siding and gutters.** Installation and repair of exterior siding, gutters, downspouts and exterior trim below the roof line. Roofing work is described by CG-11.",
}


def _guide_valid(evaluator, rule, identifiers):
    refs = [ref for ref in evaluator.rule_sources[rule] if ref.locator in identifiers]
    return all(sum(ref.locator == key for ref in refs) == 1 for key in identifiers) and all(
        " ".join(ref.excerpt.split()) in (_GUIDE_WORDING[ref.locator], _GUIDE_WORDING[ref.locator] + " ## Class codes") for ref in refs)


def _day(text, period):
    day = date.fromisoformat(text)
    if day.isoformat() != text or period is None or not period.start <= day <= period.end:
        raise ValueError("date is outside the audit period or not canonical")
    return day


def evaluate_contractor(inputs, business, notes, crew, log, payroll, register, period, evaluator, files):
    employees = {row.employee_id: row for row in register}
    context = tuple(_source(doc, "business description" if doc is business else "auditor field notes") for doc in (business, notes) if doc)
    business_text = " ".join(business.text.lower().split())
    note_text = " ".join(" ".join(line for line in notes.text.lower().splitlines() if not line.lstrip().startswith("#")).split()) if notes else ""
    observed_estimator = bool(re.search(r"(?:^|[.!?]\s+|\band )the estimator was measuring a house for a quote\.", note_text))
    observed_bookkeeper = bool(re.search(r"(?:^|[.!?]\s+)the bookkeeper works in the office\.", note_text))
    mapped = {files.business, files.notes, files.payroll, files.application, files.crew_timesheets, files.site_signins}
    extra = [doc for doc in inputs.records if str(doc.path.relative_to(inputs.records_root)) not in mapped and not _adjustment_evidence(doc)]
    global_errors = []
    if extra or set(payroll.columns) != {"employee_id", "name", "position", "wages_paid"}:
        global_errors.append("Unmapped source files or payroll columns require duty-evidence review.")
        context += tuple(_source(doc, "unmapped evidence") for doc in extra)
    if notes is None or period is None:
        global_errors.append("Confirm field observations and the exact audit period.")
    if re.search(r"\b(?:actual duties|misleading|exclusively|contrary|instead)\b", business_text + " " + note_text):
        global_errors.append("Exceptional or conflicting duty prose is outside this adapter's supported observations; obtain duty review.")
    context_text = business_text + " " + note_text
    if re.search(r"\b(?:timesheets?|sign[- ]in|crew time|records?|pages)\b[^.!?]{0,150}\b(?:missing|incomplete|unavailable|lost|unconfirmed|not complete)\b|\b(?:missing|incomplete|unavailable|lost|unconfirmed)\b[^.!?]{0,100}\b(?:timesheets?|sign[- ]in|crew time|records?|pages)\b", context_text):
        global_errors.append("Explicit missing or incomplete audit-period records prevent a complete-evidence assertion; obtain the missing pages and confirmation.")
    if re.search(r"\b(?:bookkeeper|estimator)\b[^.!?]{0,80}\b(?:install\w*|repair\w*|roof\w*|field work)\b", context_text):
        global_errors.append("Physical-work statements conflict with the supported office-role observations; confirm employee duties and rule scope.")
    role_counts = Counter(str(row.raw_record.values.get("position", "")).lower() for row in register)
    dual = bool(re.search(r"\b(?:replaces roofs|performs roofing|installs roofing)\b", business_text) and re.search(r"\binstalls siding\b", business_text))
    if re.search(r"\b(?:no|not|never|unconfirmed|unknown)\b[^.!?]{0,60}\b(?:roof\w*|siding|field work|crew time)\b", business_text + " " + note_text):
        dual = False
    field_rows = {key: [] for key in employees}
    roof_dates = {key: set() for key in employees}
    field_errors = {key: [] for key in employees}
    field_global = []
    field_global_refs = []
    crew_valid = crew is not None and set(crew.columns) == {"date", "employee_id", "name", "job_id", "work_type", "hours"}
    work_types = set()
    if not crew_valid:
        field_global.append("Crew timesheets are missing or have an unsupported schema; missing records cannot establish zero roofing days.")
    else:
        for row, ref in _row_references(crew):
            key = row.values["employee_id"]
            if key not in employees or row.values["name"] != employees[key].name:
                field_global.append("A crew timesheet identity conflicts with the register; confirm identity without assuming an alias.")
                global_errors.append("Conflicting crew identities may implicate office staff; resolve the actual employee identity before classification.")
                field_global_refs.append(ref)
                if key in employees:
                    field_rows[key].append(ref)
                continue
            field_rows[key].append(ref)
            try:
                day = _day(row.values["date"], period)
                hours = Decimal(row.values["hours"])
                kind = row.values["work_type"]
                if not hours.is_finite() or not Decimal(0) < hours <= Decimal(24) or not row.values["job_id"].strip() or kind not in {"roofing", "siding", "gutters"}:
                    raise ValueError("unsupported work or invalid hours/job evidence")
                work_types.add(kind)
                if kind == "roofing":
                    roof_dates[key].add(day)
            except (ValueError, TypeError, InvalidOperation):
                field_errors[key].append(f"{ref.locator}: invalid date, work type, hours or job evidence; obtain corrected actual-duty records.")
    dual = dual and {"roofing", "siding"}.issubset(work_types)
    field_ids = tuple(key for key in employees if field_rows[key])
    decisions = {}

def _guide_valid(evaluator, rule, identifiers):
    refs = [ref for ref in evaluator.rule_sources[rule] if ref.locator in identifiers]

        " ".join(ref.excerpt.split()) in (_GUIDE_WORDING[ref.locator], _GUIDE_WORDING[ref.locator] + " ## Class codes") for ref in refs)


def _day(text, period):
    day = date.fromisoformat(text)
    if day.isoformat() != text or period is None or not period.start <= day <= period.end:
        raise ValueError("date is outside the audit period or not canonical")

    observed_estimator = bool(re.search(r"(?:^|[.!?]\s+|\band )the estimator was measuring a house for a quote\.", note_text))

Your job is to review completed work against its plan or requirements and identify issues before they cascade. ## What Was Implemented [DESCRIPTION] ## Requirements / Plan [PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS] ## Git Range to Review **Base:** [BASE_SHA] **Head:** [HEAD_SHA] ```bash git diff --stat [BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA] git diff [BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA] ``` ## The spec is a vision document The spec says what the software must do. It does not enumerate every input, environment, or condition the software will meet. For behavior the spec is silent on, judge by what a reasonable person using this software would expect: a reasonable person's expectation is a requirement, and a spec's silence is not permission. Grade such findings by their effect on that person, not by whether the spec mentions the trigger. ## Declined to judge Before your verdict, list every behavior you considered and set aside as outside the plan or spec, one line each, with the reason. The executor rules on each line; nothing you set aside is dropped silently. An empty list means you set nothing aside. ## Read-Only Review Your review is read-only on this checkout. Do not mutate the working tree, the index, HEAD, or branch state in any way. Use tools like `git show`, `git diff`, and `git log` to inspect history. If you need a working copy of a different revision, check it out into a separate temporary directory (e.g. `git worktree add /tmp/review-[SHA] [SHA]`) — never move HEAD on this checkout. ## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents Do all of this review yourself. Never spawn a subagent to review part of the diff, and never spawn another reviewer for a second opinion. This process already provides every review seat the work gets; a reviewer you spawn duplicates one of them at full cost, and its verdict counts for nothing. If the diff feels too large for one pass, review it in passes yourself and say so in your report. ## What to Check **Plan alignment:** - Does the implementation match the plan / requirements? - Are deviations justified improvements, or problematic departures? - Is all planned functionality present? **Code quality:** - Clean separation of concerns? - Proper error handling? - Type safety where applicable? - DRY without premature abstraction? - Edge cases handled? **Architecture:** - Sound design decisions? - Reasonable scalability and performance? - Security concerns? - Integrates cleanly with surrounding code? **Testing:** - Tests verify real behavior, not mocks? - Edge cases covered? - Integration tests where they matter? - All tests passing? **Production readiness:** - Migration strategy if schema changed? - Backward compatibility considered? - Documentation complete? - No obvious bugs? ## Calibration Categorize issues by actual severity. Not everything is Critical. Acknowledge what was done well before listing issues — accurate praise helps the implementer trust the rest of the feedback. If you find significant deviations from the plan, flag them specifically so the implementer can confirm whether the deviation was intentional. If you find issues with the plan itself rather than the implementation, say so. ## Output Format ### Strengths [What's well done? Be specific.] ### Issues #### Critical (Must Fix) [Bugs, security issues, data loss risks, broken functionality] #### Important (Should Fix) [Architecture problems, missing features, poor error handling, test gaps] #### Minor (Nice to Have) [Code style, optimization opportunities, documentation polish] For each issue: - Categorize by actual severity - Be specific (file:line, not vague) - Explain WHY each issue matters - Acknowledge strengths - Give a clear verdict **DON'T:** - Say "looks good" without checking - Mark nitpicks as Critical - architecture, design patterns, and best practices. Your job is to review completed work against its plan or requirements and identify issues before they cascade. ## What Was Implemented [DESCRIPTION] ## Requirements / Plan [PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS] ## Git Range to Review **Base:** [BASE_SHA] **Head:** [HEAD_SHA] ```bash git diff --stat [BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA] git diff [BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA] ``` ## The spec is a vision document The spec says what the software must do. It does not enumerate every input, environment, or condition the software will meet. For behavior the spec is silent on, judge by what a reasonable person using this software would expect: a reasonable person's expectation is a requirement, and a spec's silence is not permission. Grade such findings by their effect on that person, not by whether the spec mentions the trigger. ## Declined to judge Before your verdict, list every behavior you considered and set aside as outside the plan or spec, one line each, with the reason. The executor rules on each line; nothing you set aside is dropped silently. An empty list means you set nothing aside. ## Read-Only Review Your review is read-only on this checkout. Do not mutate the working tree, the index, HEAD, or branch state in any way. Use tools like `git show`, `git diff`, and `git log` to inspect history. If you need a working copy of a different revision, check it out into a separate temporary directory (e.g. `git worktree add /tmp/review-[SHA] [SHA]`) — never move HEAD on this checkout. ## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents Do all of this review yourself. Never spawn a subagent to review part of the diff, and never spawn another reviewer for a second opinion. This process already provides every review seat the work gets; a reviewer you spawn duplicates one of them at full cost, and its verdict counts for nothing. If the diff feels too large for one pass, review it in passes yourself and say so in your report. ## What to Check **Plan alignment:** - Does the implementation match the plan / requirements? - Are deviations justified improvements, or problematic departures? - Is all planned functionality present? **Code quality:** - Clean separation of concerns? - Proper error handling? - Type safety where applicable? - DRY without premature abstraction? - Edge cases handled? **Architecture:** - Sound design decisions? - Reasonable scalability and performance? - Security concerns? - Integrates cleanly with surrounding code? **Testing:** - Tests verify real behavior, not mocks? - Edge cases covered? - Integration tests where they matter? - All tests passing? **Production readiness:** - Migration strategy if schema changed? - Backward compatibility considered? - Documentation complete? - No obvious bugs? ## Calibration Categorize issues by actual severity. Not everything is Critical. Acknowledge what was done well before listing issues — accurate praise helps the implementer trust the rest of the feedback. If you find significant deviations from the plan, flag them specifically so the implementer can confirm whether the deviation was intentional. # Code Reviewer Prompt Template

Use this template when dispatching a code reviewer subagent.

**Purpose:** Review completed work against requirements and code quality standards before it cascades into more work.

```
Subagent (general-purpose):
  description: "Review code changes"
  prompt: |
    You are a Senior Code Reviewer with expertise in software architecture,
    design patterns, and best practices. Your job is to review completed work
    against its plan or requirements and identify issues before they cascade.

    ## What Was Implemented

    [DESCRIPTION]

    ## Requirements / Plan

    [PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS]

    ## Git Range to Review

    **Base:** [BASE_SHA]
    **Head:** [HEAD_SHA]

    ```bash
    git diff --stat [BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA]
    git diff [BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA]
    ```

    ## The spec is a vision document

    The spec says what the software must do. It does not enumerate every
    input, environment, or condition the software will meet. For behavior
    the spec is silent on, judge by what a reasonable person using this
    software would expect: a reasonable person's expectation is a
    requirement, and a spec's silence is not permission. Grade such
    findings by their effect on that person, not by whether the spec
    mentions the trigger.

    ## Declined to judge

    Before your verdict, list every behavior you considered and set aside
    as outside the plan or spec, one line each, with the reason. The
    executor rules on each line; nothing you set aside is dropped
    silently. An empty list means you set nothing aside.

    ## Read-Only Review

    Your review is read-only on this checkout. Do not mutate the working tree, the index, HEAD, or branch state in any way. Use tools like `git show`, `git diff`, and `git log` to inspect history. If you need a working copy of a different revision, check it out into a separate temporary directory (e.g. `git worktree add /tmp/review-[SHA] [SHA]`) — never move HEAD on this checkout.

    ## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents

    Do all of this review yourself. Never spawn a subagent to review part
    of the diff, and never spawn another reviewer for a second opinion.
    This process already provides every review seat the work gets; a
    reviewer you spawn duplicates one of them at full cost, and its
    verdict counts for nothing. If the diff feels too large for one
    pass, review it in passes yourself and say so in your report.

    ## What to Check

    **Plan alignment:**
    - Does the implementation match the plan / requirements?
    - Are deviations justified improvements, or problematic departures?
    - Is all planned functionality present?

    **Code quality:**
    - Clean separation of concerns?
    - Proper error handling?
    - Type safety where applicable?
    - DRY without premature abstraction?
    - Edge cases handled?

    **Architecture:**
    - Sound design decisions?
    - Reasonable scalability and performance?
    - Security concerns?
    - Integrates cleanly with surrounding code?

    **Testing:**
    - Tests verify real behavior, not mocks?
    - Edge cases covered?
    - Integration tests where they matter?
    - All tests passing?

    **Production readiness:**
    - Migration strategy if schema changed?
    - Backward compatibility considered?
    - Documentation complete?
    - No obvious bugs?

    ## Calibration

    Categorize issues by actual severity. Not everything is Critical.
    Acknowledge what was done well before listing issues — accurate praise
    helps the implementer trust the rest of the feedback.

    If you find significant deviations from the plan, flag them specifically
    so the implementer can confirm whether the deviation was intentional.
    If you find issues with the plan itself rather than the implementation,
    say so.

    ## Output Format

    ### Strengths
    [What's well done? Be specific.]

    ### Issues

    #### Critical (Must Fix)
    [Bugs, security issues, data loss risks, broken functionality]

    #### Important (Should Fix)
    [Architecture problems, missing features, poor error handling, test gaps]

    #### Minor (Nice to Have)
    [Code style, optimization opportunities, documentation polish]

    For each issue:
    - File:line reference
    - What's wrong
    - Why it matters
    - How to fix (if not obvious)

    ### Recommendations
    [Improvements for code quality, architecture, or process]

    ### Assessment

**Purpose:** Review completed work against requirements and code quality standards before it cascades into more work.

Subagent (general-purpose):
  description: "Review code changes"
  prompt: |
    You are a Senior Code Reviewer with expertise in software architecture,
    design patterns, and best practices. Your job is to review completed work
    against its plan or requirements and identify issues before they cascade.

    ## What Was Implemented

    [DESCRIPTION]

    ## Requirements / Plan

    [PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS]

    ## Git Range to Review

    **Base:** [BASE_SHA]
    **Head:** [HEAD_SHA]

    ```bash
    git diff --stat [BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA]
    git diff [BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA]
    ```

    ## The spec is a vision document

    The spec says what the software must do. It does not enumerate every
    input, environment, or condition the software will meet. For behavior
    the spec is silent on, judge by what a reasonable person using this
    software would expect: a reasonable person's expectation is a
    requirement, and a spec's silence is not permission. Grade such
    findings by their effect on that person, not by whether the spec
    mentions the trigger.

    ## Declined to judge

    Before your verdict, list every behavior you considered and set aside
    as outside the plan or spec, one line each, with the reason. The
    executor rules on each line; nothing you set aside is dropped
    silently. An empty list means you set nothing aside.

    ## Read-Only Review

    Your review is read-only on this checkout. Do not mutate the working tree, the index, HEAD, or branch state in any way. Use tools like `git show`, `git diff`, and `git log` to inspect history. If you need a working copy of a different revision, check it out into a separate temporary directory (e.g. `git worktree add /tmp/review-[SHA] [SHA]`) — never move HEAD on this checkout.

    ## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents

    Do all of this review yourself. Never spawn a subagent to review part
    of the diff, and never spawn another reviewer for a second opinion.
    This process already provides every review seat the work gets; a
    reviewer you spawn duplicates one of them at full cost, and its
    verdict counts for nothing. If the diff feels too large for one
    pass, review it in passes yourself and say so in your report.

    ## What to Check

    **Plan alignment:**
    - Does the implementation match the plan / requirements?
    - Are deviations justified improvements, or problematic departures?
    - Is all planned functionality present?

    **Code quality:**
    - Clean separation of concerns?
    - Proper error handling?
    - Type safety where applicable?
    - DRY without premature abstraction?
    - Edge cases handled?

    **Architecture:**
    - Sound design decisions?
    - Reasonable scalability and performance?
    - Security concerns?
    - Integrates cleanly with surrounding code?

    **Testing:**
    - Tests verify real behavior, not mocks?
    - Edge cases covered?
    - Integration tests where they matter?
    - All tests passing?

    **Production readiness:**
    - Migration strategy if schema changed?
    - Backward compatibility considered?
    - Documentation complete?
    - No obvious bugs?

    ## Calibration

    Categorize issues by actual severity. Not everything is Critical.
    Acknowledge what was done well before listing issues — accurate praise
    helps the implementer trust the rest of the feedback.

    If you find significant deviations from the plan, flag them specifically
    so the implementer can confirm whether the deviation was intentional.
    If you find issues with the plan itself rather than the implementation,
    say so.

    [What's well done? Be specific.]

    ### Issues

    #### Critical (Must Fix)
    [Bugs, security issues, data loss risks, broken functionality]

    [Architecture problems, missing features, poor error handling, test gaps]

name: requesting-code-review
description: Use when completing tasks, implementing major features, or before merging to verify work meets requirements
---

# Requesting Code Review

Dispatch a code reviewer subagent to catch issues before they cascade. The reviewer gets precisely crafted context for evaluation — never your session's history.

**Core principle:** Review early, review often.

## When to Request Review

**Mandatory:**
- After each task in subagent-driven development
- After completing major feature
- Before merge to main

**Optional but valuable:**
- When stuck (fresh perspective)
- Before refactoring (baseline check)
- After fixing complex bug

## How to Request

**1. Get git SHAs:**
```bash
BASE_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD~1)  # or: git merge-base origin/main HEAD
HEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
```

**2. Dispatch code reviewer subagent:**

Dispatch a `general-purpose` subagent, filling the template at [code-reviewer.md](code-reviewer.md)

**Placeholders:**
- `{DESCRIPTION}` - Brief summary of what you built
- `{PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS}` - What it should do
- `{BASE_SHA}` - Starting commit
- `{HEAD_SHA}` - Ending commit

**3. Act on feedback:**
- Fix Critical issues immediately
- Fix Important issues before proceeding
- Note Minor issues for later
- Push back if reviewer is wrong (with reasoning)

## Example

```
[Just completed Task 2: Add verification function]

You: Let me request code review before proceeding.

BASE_SHA=$(git log --oneline | grep "Task 1" | head -1 | cut -d' ' -f1)
HEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

[Dispatch code reviewer subagent]
  DESCRIPTION: Added verifyIndex() and repairIndex() with 4 issue types
  PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS: Task 2 from docs/superpowers/plans/deployment-plan.md
  BASE_SHA: a7981ec
  HEAD_SHA: 3df7661

[Subagent returns]:
  Strengths: Clean architecture, real tests
  Issues:
    Important: Missing progress indicators
    Minor: Magic number (100) for reporting interval
  Assessment: Ready to proceed

You: [Fix progress indicators]
[Continue to Task 3]
```

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "I'll just review the diff myself instead of dispatching a reviewer" | You're the coordinator — reviewing the diff inline burns the context window you need to keep driving the work. Dispatch a reviewer subagent: the diff and the evaluation live in its context, and only the findings come back to you. |
| "The reviewer needs my whole session history to understand the change" | Hand it precisely crafted context, never your session's history. That keeps the reviewer on the work product, not your thought process. |

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Skip review because "it's simple"
- Ignore Critical issues
- Proceed with unfixed Important issues
- Argue with valid technical feedback

**If reviewer wrong:**
- Push back with technical reasoning
- Show code/tests that prove it works
- Request clarification

See template at: [code-reviewer.md](code-reviewer.md)

"""Validate the packaged Skill and execute its documented preview commands."""

import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import re
import shlex
from string import Template
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

from test_electrical_processing import (
    APPLICATION, BUSINESS, GUIDE, INTERVIEW, NOTES, PAYROLL, SIGNINS,
)

COMPONENT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
SKILL = COMPONENT / "SKILL.md"


class SkillPackageTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def skill_text(self):
        self.assertTrue(SKILL.is_file(), "The reusable SKILL.md is missing")
        return SKILL.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    def test_metadata_has_valid_name_and_nonempty_description(self):
        text = self.skill_text()
        match = re.match(r"\A---\n(.*?)\n---\n", text, re.DOTALL)
        self.assertIsNotNone(match, "Skill requires YAML frontmatter")
        # This package uses two plain, single-line YAML scalars; no YAML runtime
        # dependency is needed to check that deliberately small metadata contract.
        entries = {}
        for line in match.group(1).splitlines():
            field = re.fullmatch(r"(name|description): ([^\n]+)", line)
            self.assertIsNotNone(field, f"Invalid plain metadata entry: {line!r}")
            key, value = field.groups()
            self.assertNotIn(key, entries, "Duplicate metadata field")
            self.assertNotRegex(value, r"[:#\[\]{}<>]|\A[-?&*!|>'\"%@`]")
            entries[key] = value
        self.assertEqual(set(entries), {"name", "description"})
        self.assertEqual(entries["name"], COMPONENT.name)
        self.assertRegex(entries["name"], r"\A[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*\Z")
        self.assertLessEqual(len(entries["name"]), 64)
        self.assertTrue(entries["description"].strip())
        self.assertLessEqual(len(entries["description"]), 1024)

    def test_local_references_resolve_to_existing_supporting_files(self):
        references = re.findall(r"\[[^\]]+\]\(([^\s)]+)\)", self.skill_text())
        self.assertTrue(references, "Skill must link to its supporting files")
        targets = set()
        for reference in references:
            self.assertNotIn("://", reference, "Package references should be local")
            path = (COMPONENT / reference.split("#", 1)[0]).resolve()
            self.assertTrue(path.is_relative_to(COMPONENT))
            self.assertTrue(path.is_file(), f"Broken Skill reference: {reference}")
            targets.add(path.name)
        self.assertTrue({"preview.py", "input_reader.py", "rule_evaluator.py",
                         "payroll_allocation.py", "payroll_adjustments.py",
                         "employer_processing.py"}.issubset(targets))

    def prepare_sources(self):
        temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="skill inputs ")
        self.addCleanup(temp.cleanup)
        root = Path(temp.name)
        guide, interview = root / "current guide.md", root / "complete interview.md"
        guide.write_text(GUIDE, encoding="utf-8")
        interview.write_text(INTERVIEW, encoding="utf-8")
        container = root / "new employer folders"
        container.mkdir()
        employer = container / "previously unseen business"
        employer.mkdir()
        for filename, contents in {
            "business-description.md": BUSINESS, "field-notes.md": NOTES,
            "payroll-register.csv": PAYROLL, "application.md": APPLICATION,
            "site-signin-log.csv": SIGNINS,
        }.items():
            (employer / filename).write_text(contents, encoding="utf-8")
        return {
            "AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH": str(guide), "AUDIT_INTERVIEW_PATH": str(interview),
            "AUDIT_EMPLOYER_DIR": str(employer),
            "AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT": str(container),
        }

    def documented_command(self, mode, locations):
        blocks = re.findall(r"```bash\n(.*?)\n```", self.skill_text(), re.DOTALL)
        candidates = []
        for block in blocks:
            words = shlex.split(block.replace("\\\n", ""))
            if mode in words:
                candidates.append(words)
        self.assertEqual(len(candidates), 1, f"Need one complete {mode} example")
        words = candidates[0]
        self.assertEqual(words[:3], ["python3", "-B", "preview.py"])
        expanded = [Template(word).substitute(locations) for word in words]
        return [sys.executable, *expanded[1:]]

    def run_documented(self, mode, locations, *, structured=True):
        command = self.documented_command(mode, locations)
        if structured:
            command += ["--format", "json"]
        return subprocess.run(command, cwd=COMPONENT, capture_output=True,
                              text=True, check=False)

    def test_documented_single_command_keeps_open_money_out_of_verified_totals(self):
        locations = self.prepare_sources()
        completed = self.run_documented("--employer", locations)
        self.assertEqual(completed.returncode, 0, completed.stderr)
        report = json.loads(completed.stdout)
        self.assertTrue(report["preview_only"])
        employer = report["employers"][0]
        self.assertEqual(employer["verified_by_code"],
                         {"E-510": "186.08", "C-110": "20.02"})
        self.assertEqual(employer["open_adjustment_basis"], "3.90")
        proposal = next(p for p in employer["proposals"] if p["kind"] == "adjustment")
        self.assertEqual(proposal["treatment"]["payroll_added"], "3.90")
        self.assertEqual(employer["status"], "REVIEW")
        self.assertTrue(employer["reconciliation"]["independent"]["reconciled"])
        self.assertTrue(employer["sources"])

    def test_documented_all_command_preserves_valid_employer_after_neighbor_error(self):
        locations = self.prepare_sources()
        broken = Path(locations["AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT"]) / "incomplete neighbor"
        broken.mkdir()
        completed = self.run_documented("--all-employers", locations)
        self.assertEqual(completed.returncode, 1)
        employers = json.loads(completed.stdout)["employers"]
        self.assertEqual(len(employers), 2)
        by_name = {item["employer"]: item for item in employers}
        self.assertEqual(by_name[broken.name]["status"], "ERROR")
        self.assertEqual(by_name["previously unseen business"]["verified_by_code"]["E-510"], "186.08")

    def test_documented_command_rereads_changed_authoritative_payroll(self):
        locations = self.prepare_sources()
        first = self.run_documented("--employer", locations)
        self.assertEqual(first.returncode, 0, first.stderr)
        payroll = Path(locations["AUDIT_EMPLOYER_DIR"]) / "payroll-register.csv"
        payroll.write_text(PAYROLL.replace("50.05,2,100.00", "75.05,2,100.00"),
                           encoding="utf-8")
        second = self.run_documented("--employer", locations)
        self.assertEqual(second.returncode, 0, second.stderr)
        changed = json.loads(second.stdout)["employers"][0]
        self.assertEqual(changed["verified_by_code"]["E-510"], "211.08")
        self.assertNotEqual(first.stdout, second.stdout)

    def test_documented_command_missing_guide_reports_error_without_snapshot_fallback(self):
        locations = self.prepare_sources()
        locations["AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH"] = str(Path(locations["AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH"]).with_name("missing.md"))
        completed = self.run_documented("--employer", locations)
        self.assertEqual(completed.returncode, 1)
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(completed.stdout)["status"], "ERROR")
        self.assertIn(locations["AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH"], completed.stderr)

    def test_documented_text_preview_preserves_inputs_and_creates_no_deliverables(self):
        locations = self.prepare_sources()
        root = Path(locations["AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH"]).parent

        def hashes():
            return {p.relative_to(root): hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
                    for p in root.rglob("*") if p.is_file()}

        before = hashes()
        for mode in ("--employer", "--all-employers"):
            completed = self.run_documented(mode, locations, structured=False)
            self.assertEqual(completed.returncode, 0, completed.stderr)
            for label in ("PREVIEW ONLY", "OPEN", "UNAPPROVED", "SHA-256"):
                self.assertIn(label, completed.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(hashes(), before)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Validate the packaged Skill and execute its documented preview commands."""

import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import re
import shlex
from string import Template
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

from test_electrical_processing import (
    APPLICATION, BUSINESS, GUIDE, INTERVIEW, NOTES, PAYROLL, SIGNINS,
)

COMPONENT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
SKILL = COMPONENT / "SKILL.md"


class SkillPackageTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def skill_text(self):
        self.assertTrue(SKILL.is_file(), "The reusable SKILL.md is missing")
        return SKILL.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    def test_metadata_has_valid_name_and_nonempty_description(self):
        text = self.skill_text()
        match = re.match(r"\A---\n(.*?)\n---\n", text, re.DOTALL)
        self.assertIsNotNone(match, "Skill requires YAML frontmatter")
        # This package uses two plain, single-line YAML scalars; no YAML runtime
        # dependency is needed to check that deliberately small metadata contract.
        entries = {}
        for line in match.group(1).splitlines():
            field = re.fullmatch(r"(name|description): ([^\n]+)", line)
            self.assertIsNotNone(field, f"Invalid plain metadata entry: {line!r}")
            key, value = field.groups()
            self.assertNotIn(key, entries, "Duplicate metadata field")
            self.assertNotRegex(value, r"[:#\[\]{}<>]|\A[-?&*!|>'\"%@`]")
            entries[key] = value
        self.assertEqual(set(entries), {"name", "description"})
        self.assertEqual(entries["name"], COMPONENT.name)
        self.assertRegex(entries["name"], r"\A[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*\Z")
        self.assertLessEqual(len(entries["name"]), 64)
        self.assertTrue(entries["description"].strip())
        self.assertLessEqual(len(entries["description"]), 1024)

    def test_local_references_resolve_to_existing_supporting_files(self):
        references = re.findall(r"\[[^\]]+\]\(([^\s)]+)\)", self.skill_text())
        self.assertTrue(references, "Skill must link to its supporting files")
        targets = set()
        for reference in references:
            self.assertNotIn("://", reference, "Package references should be local")
            path = (COMPONENT / reference.split("#", 1)[0]).resolve()
            self.assertTrue(path.is_relative_to(COMPONENT))
            self.assertTrue(path.is_file(), f"Broken Skill reference: {reference}")
            targets.add(path.name)
        self.assertTrue({"preview.py", "input_reader.py", "rule_evaluator.py",
                         "payroll_allocation.py", "payroll_adjustments.py",
                         "employer_processing.py"}.issubset(targets))

    def prepare_sources(self):
        temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="skill inputs ")
        self.addCleanup(temp.cleanup)
        root = Path(temp.name)
        guide, interview = root / "current guide.md", root / "complete interview.md"
        guide.write_text(GUIDE, encoding="utf-8")
        interview.write_text(INTERVIEW, encoding="utf-8")
        container = root / "new employer folders"
        container.mkdir()
        employer = container / "previously unseen business"
        employer.mkdir()
        for filename, contents in {
            "business-description.md": BUSINESS, "field-notes.md": NOTES,
            "payroll-register.csv": PAYROLL, "application.md": APPLICATION,
            "site-signin-log.csv": SIGNINS,
        }.items():
            (employer / filename).write_text(contents, encoding="utf-8")
        return {
            "AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH": str(guide), "AUDIT_INTERVIEW_PATH": str(interview),
            "AUDIT_EMPLOYER_DIR": str(employer),
            "AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT": str(container),
        }

    def documented_command(self, mode, locations):
        blocks = re.findall(r"```bash\n(.*?)\n```", self.skill_text(), re.DOTALL)
        candidates = []
        for block in blocks:
            words = shlex.split(block.replace("\\\n", ""))
            if mode in words:
                candidates.append(words)
        self.assertEqual(len(candidates), 1, f"Need one complete {mode} example")
        words = candidates[0]
        self.assertEqual(words[:3], ["python3", "-B", "preview.py"])
        expanded = [Template(word).substitute(locations) for word in words]
        return [sys.executable, *expanded[1:]]

    def run_documented(self, mode, locations, *, structured=True):
        command = self.documented_command(mode, locations)
        if structured:
            command += ["--format", "json"]
        return subprocess.run(command, cwd=COMPONENT, capture_output=True,
                              text=True, check=False)

    def test_documented_single_command_keeps_open_money_out_of_verified_totals(self):
        locations = self.prepare_sources()
        completed = self.run_documented("--employer", locations)
        self.assertEqual(completed.returncode, 0, completed.stderr)
        report = json.loads(completed.stdout)
        self.assertTrue(report["preview_only"])
        employer = report["employers"][0]
        self.assertEqual(employer["verified_by_code"],
                         {"E-510": "186.08", "C-110": "20.02"})
        self.assertEqual(employer["open_adjustment_basis"], "3.90")
        proposal = next(p for p in employer["proposals"] if p["kind"] == "adjustment")
        self.assertEqual(proposal["treatment"]["payroll_added"], "3.90")
        self.assertEqual(employer["status"], "REVIEW")
        self.assertTrue(employer["reconciliation"]["independent"]["reconciled"])
        self.assertTrue(employer["sources"])

    def test_documented_all_command_preserves_valid_employer_after_neighbor_error(self):
        locations = self.prepare_sources()
        broken = Path(locations["AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT"]) / "incomplete neighbor"
        broken.mkdir()
        completed = self.run_documented("--all-employers", locations)
        self.assertEqual(completed.returncode, 1)
        employers = json.loads(completed.stdout)["employers"]
        self.assertEqual(len(employers), 2)
        by_name = {item["employer"]: item for item in employers}
        self.assertEqual(by_name[broken.name]["status"], "ERROR")
        self.assertEqual(by_name["previously unseen business"]["verified_by_code"]["E-510"], "186.08")

    def test_documented_command_rereads_changed_authoritative_payroll(self):
        locations = self.prepare_sources()
        first = self.run_documented("--employer", locations)
        self.assertEqual(first.returncode, 0, first.stderr)
        payroll = Path(locations["AUDIT_EMPLOYER_DIR"]) / "payroll-register.csv"
        payroll.write_text(PAYROLL.replace("50.05,2,100.00", "75.05,2,100.00"),
                           encoding="utf-8")
        second = self.run_documented("--employer", locations)
        self.assertEqual(second.returncode, 0, second.stderr)
        changed = json.loads(second.stdout)["employers"][0]
        self.assertEqual(changed["verified_by_code"]["E-510"], "211.08")
        self.assertNotEqual(first.stdout, second.stdout)

    def test_documented_command_missing_guide_reports_error_without_snapshot_fallback(self):
        locations = self.prepare_sources()
        locations["AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH"] = str(Path(locations["AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH"]).with_name("missing.md"))
        completed = self.run_documented("--employer", locations)
        self.assertEqual(completed.returncode, 1)
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(completed.stdout)["status"], "ERROR")
        self.assertIn(locations["AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH"], completed.stderr)

    def test_documented_text_preview_preserves_inputs_and_creates_no_deliverables(self):
        locations = self.prepare_sources()
        root = Path(locations["AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH"]).parent

        def hashes():
            return {p.relative_to(root): hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
                    for p in root.rglob("*") if p.is_file()}

        before = hashes()
        for mode in ("--employer", "--all-employers"):
            completed = self.run_documented(mode, locations, structured=False)
            self.assertEqual(completed.returncode, 0, completed.stderr)
            for label in ("PREVIEW ONLY", "OPEN", "UNAPPROVED", "SHA-256"):
                self.assertIn(label, completed.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(hashes(), before)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

The guard only recognizes prose repeating the exact normalized visitor label. With four confirmed estimator days, adding either:

  - `The inspector who signed in on 2025-04-15 was Estimator One.`

- Other visitor roles remain possible employee days: conservative limitation consistent with the smallest correction.

- Saved deliverables remain stale: explicitly outside this authorization.
- Existing adapters’ broader prose interpretation limits: outside the changed behavior.
- Severn expectation updates in preview/electrical regression tests: necessary downstream expectations; other employer logic remains unchanged.

    mode.add_argument("--employer", type=Path)

    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", required=True, type=Path, help="Directory for verified-only employer CSVs")

    filenames = {}
    allowed = {field.name for field in fields(EmployerFiles)}
    for value in args.file:
        field, separator, path = value.partition("=")

            parser.error(f"Invalid or duplicate EmployerFiles filename override: {value!r}")
        filenames[field] = str(Path(path))
    try:
        report = generate_csvs(args.guide, args.interview, employer=args.employer,
            all_employers=args.all_employers, output_dir=args.output_dir, review_state=args.review_state,
            files=replace(EmployerFiles(), **filenames))
    except (CSVGenerationError, OSError, ValueError) as exc:
        print(f"ERROR: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f"Verified-only CSV generation: {report['status']}")

import hashlib, json, pathlib, subprocess, sys
before = json.loads(sys.argv[1])
allowed = {
 "skills/class-code-assistant/homebuilding_processing.py",
 "skills/class-code-assistant/tests/test_homebuilding_processing.py",
 "skills/class-code-assistant/tests/test_preview.py",
 "skills/class-code-assistant/tests/test_electrical_processing.py",
}
changed, unexpected = [], []
for name, old in before["files"].items():
    path = pathlib.Path(name)
    stat = path.stat()
    content_changed = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() != old["sha256"]
    metadata_changed = stat.st_mode != old["mode"] or float(stat.st_mtime_ns) != float(old["mtime_ns"])
    if content_changed or metadata_changed:
        changed.append(name)
        if name not in allowed: unexpected.append(name)
assert not unexpected, unexpected
assert set(changed) == allowed, changed
refs = subprocess.check_output(["git", "for-each-ref", "--format=%(refname) %(objectname)", "refs/entire", "refs/heads/entire"], text=True).splitlines()
assert refs == before["entire_refs"], refs
assert subprocess.check_output(["git", "branch", "--show-current"], text=True).strip() == before["branch"]
assert subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], text=True).strip() == before["head"]
assert not subprocess.check_output(["git", "diff", "--cached", "--name-only"], text=True).strip()
untracked = subprocess.check_output(["git", "ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard"], text=True).splitlines()
expected_docs = sorted(p for p in before["files"] if p.startswith("docs/"))
assert sorted(untracked) == expected_docs, untracked
print(json.dumps({"changed_files":changed,"protected_files_preserved":len(before["files"])-len(allowed),"untracked_docs_preserved":len(untracked),"entire_refs_and_settings_preserved":True,"head_and_branch_preserved":True,"staged_files":0},indent=2))

name: systematic-debugging
description: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes
---

# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.

**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
```

If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.

## When to Use

Use for ANY technical issue:
- Test failures
- Bugs in production
- Unexpected behavior
- Performance problems
- Build failures
- Integration issues

**Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
- Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
- "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
- You've already tried multiple fixes
- Previous fix didn't work
- You don't fully understand the issue

**Don't skip when:**
- Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
- You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
- Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)

## The Four Phases

You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.

### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation

**BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**

1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
   - Don't skip past errors or warnings
   - They often contain the exact solution
   - Read stack traces completely
   - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes

2. **Reproduce Consistently**
   - Can you trigger it reliably?
   - What are the exact steps?
   - Does it happen every time?
   - If not reproducible → gather more data, don't guess

3. **Check Recent Changes**
   - What changed that could cause this?
   - Git diff, recent commits
   - New dependencies, config changes
   - Environmental differences

4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**

   **WHEN system has multiple components (CI → build → signing, API → service → database):**

   **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentation:**
   ```
   For EACH component boundary:
     - Log what data enters component
     - Log what data exits component
     - Verify environment/config propagation
     - Check state at each layer

   Run once to gather evidence showing WHERE it breaks
   THEN analyze evidence to identify failing component
   THEN investigate that specific component
   ```

   **Example (multi-layer system):**
   ```bash
   # Layer 1: Workflow
   echo "=== Secrets available in workflow: ==="
   echo "IDENTITY: $([ -n "${IDENTITY:-}" ] && echo SET || echo UNSET)"

   # Layer 2: Build script
   echo "=== Env vars in build script: ==="
   printenv IDENTITY >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "IDENTITY in environment" || echo "IDENTITY not in environment"

   # Layer 3: Signing script
   echo "=== Keychain state: ==="
   security list-keychains
   security find-identity -v

   # Layer 4: Actual signing
   codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --verbose=4 "$APP"
   ```

   **This reveals:** Which layer fails (secrets → workflow ✓, workflow → build ✗)

5. **Trace Data Flow**

   **WHEN error is deep in call stack:**

   See `root-cause-tracing.md` in this directory for the complete backward tracing technique.

   **Quick version:**
   - Where does bad value originate?
   - What called this with bad value?
   - Keep tracing up until you find the source
   - Fix at source, not at symptom

### Phase 2: Pattern Analysis

**Find the pattern before fixing:**

1. **Find Working Examples**
   - Locate similar working code in same codebase
   - What works that's similar to what's broken?

2. **Compare Against References**
   - If implementing pattern, read reference implementation COMPLETELY
   - Don't skim - read every line
   - Understand the pattern fully before applying

3. **Identify Differences**
   - What's different between working and broken?
   - List every difference, however small
   - Don't assume "that can't matter"

4. **Understand Dependencies**
   - What other components does this need?
   - What settings, config, environment?
   - What assumptions does it make?

### Phase 3: Hypothesis and Testing

**Scientific method:**

1. **Form Single Hypothesis**
   - State clearly: "I think X is the root cause because Y"
   - Write it down
   - Be specific, not vague

2. **Test Minimally**
   - Make the SMALLEST possible change to test hypothesis
   - One variable at a time
   - Don't fix multiple things at once

3. **Verify Before Continuing**
   - Did it work? Yes → Phase 4
   - Didn't work? Form NEW hypothesis
   - DON'T add more fixes on top

4. **When You Don't Know**
   - Say "I don't understand X"
   - Don't pretend to know
   - Ask for help
   - Research more

### Phase 4: Implementation

**Fix the root cause, not the symptom:**

1. **Create Failing Test Case**
   - Simplest possible reproduction
   - Automated test if possible
   - One-off test script if no framework
   - MUST have before fixing
   - Use the `superpowers:test-driven-development` skill for writing proper failing tests

2. **Implement Single Fix**
   - Address the root cause identified
   - ONE change at a time
   - No "while I'm here" improvements
   - No bundled refactoring

3. **Verify Fix**
   - Test passes now?
   - No other tests broken?
   - Issue actually resolved?
   - Use the `superpowers:verification-before-completion` skill before claiming success

4. **If Fix Doesn't Work**
   - STOP
   - Count: How many fixes have you tried?
   - If < 3: Return to Phase 1, re-analyze with new information
   - **If ≥ 3: STOP and question the architecture (step 5 below)**
   - DON'T attempt Fix #4 without architectural discussion

5. **If 3+ Fixes Failed: Question Architecture**

   **Pattern indicating architectural problem:**
   - Each fix reveals new shared state/coupling/problem in different place
   - Fixes require "massive refactoring" to implement
   - Each fix creates new symptoms elsewhere

   **STOP and question fundamentals:**
   - Is this pattern fundamentally sound?
   - Are we "sticking with it through sheer inertia"?
   - Should we refactor architecture vs. continue fixing symptoms?

   **Discuss with your human partner before attempting more fixes**

   This is NOT a failed hypothesis - this is a wrong architecture.

## Red Flags - STOP and Follow Process

If you catch yourself thinking:
- "Quick fix for now, investigate later"
- "Just try changing X and see if it works"
- "Add multiple changes, run tests"
- "Skip the test, I'll manually verify"
- "It's probably X, let me fix that"
- "I don't fully understand but this might work"
- "Pattern says X but I'll adapt it differently"
- "Here are the main problems: [lists fixes without investigation]"
- Proposing solutions before tracing data flow
- **"One more fix attempt" (when already tried 2+)**
- **Each fix reveals new problem in different place**

**ALL of these mean: STOP. Return to Phase 1.**

**If 3+ fixes failed:** Question the architecture (see Phase 4.5)

## your human partner's Signals You're Doing It Wrong

**Watch for these redirections:**
- "Is that not happening?" - You assumed without verifying
- "Will it show us...?" - You should have added evidence gathering
- "Stop guessing" - You're proposing fixes without understanding
- "Ultra-think this" - Question fundamentals, not just symptoms
- "We're stuck?" (frustrated) - Your approach isn't working

**When you see these:** STOP. Return to Phase 1.

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Issue is simple, don't need process" | Simple issues have root causes too. Process is fast for simple bugs. |
| "Emergency, no time for process" | Systematic debugging is FASTER than guess-and-check thrashing. |
| "Just try this first, then investigate" | First fix sets the pattern. Do it right from the start. |
| "I'll write test after confirming fix works" | Untested fixes don't stick. Test first proves it. |
| "Multiple fixes at once saves time" | Can't isolate what worked. Causes new bugs. |
| "Reference too long, I'll adapt the pattern" | Partial understanding guarantees bugs. Read it completely. |
| "I see the problem, let me fix it" | Seeing symptoms ≠ understanding root cause. |
| "One more fix attempt" (after 2+ failures) | 3+ failures = architectural problem. Question pattern, don't fix again. |

## Quick Reference

| Phase | Key Activities | Success Criteria |
|-------|---------------|------------------|
| **1. Root Cause** | Read errors, reproduce, check changes, gather evidence | Understand WHAT and WHY |
| **2. Pattern** | Find working examples, compare | Identify differences |
| **3. Hypothesis** | Form theory, test minimally | Confirmed or new hypothesis |
| **4. Implementation** | Create test, fix, verify | Bug resolved, tests pass |

## When Process Reveals "No Root Cause"

If systematic investigation reveals issue is truly environmental, timing-dependent, or external:

1. You've completed the process
2. Document what you investigated
3. Implement appropriate handling (retry, timeout, error message)
4. Add monitoring/logging for future investigation

**But:** 95% of "no root cause" cases are incomplete investigation.

## Supporting Techniques

These techniques are part of systematic debugging and available in this directory:

- **`root-cause-tracing.md`** - Trace bugs backward through call stack to find original trigger
- **`defense-in-depth.md`** - Add validation at multiple layers after finding root cause
- **`condition-based-waiting.md`** - Replace arbitrary timeouts with condition polling

name: verification-before-completion
description: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always
---

# Verification Before Completion

## Overview

**Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

**Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
```

If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

## The Gate Function

```
BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
   - If NO: State actual status with evidence
   - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim

Skip any step = lying, not verifying
```

## Common Failures

| Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
| Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
| Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
| Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
| Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
| Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
| Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |

## Red Flags - STOP

- Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
- Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
- About to commit/push/PR without verification
- Trusting agent success reports
- Relying on partial verification
- Thinking "just this once"
- Tired and wanting work over
- **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**

## Rationalization Prevention

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
| "I'm confident" | Confidence ≠ evidence |
| "Just this once" | No exceptions |
| "Linter passed" | Linter ≠ compiler |
| "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
| "I'm tired" | Exhaustion ≠ excuse |
| "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
| "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |

## Key Patterns

**Tests:**
```
✅ [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"
❌ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"
```

**Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**
```
✅ Write → Run (pass) → Revert fix → Run (MUST FAIL) → Restore → Run (pass)
❌ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)
```

**Build:**
```
✅ [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"
❌ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)
```

**Requirements:**
```
✅ Re-read plan → Create checklist → Verify each → Report gaps or completion
❌ "Tests pass, phase complete"
```

**Agent delegation:**
```
✅ Agent reports success → Check VCS diff → Verify changes → Report actual state
❌ Trust agent report
```

## When To Apply

**ALWAYS before:**
- ANY variation of success/completion claims
- ANY expression of satisfaction
- ANY positive statement about work state
- Committing, PR creation, task completion
- Moving to next task
- Delegating to agents

**Rule applies to:**
- Exact phrases
- Paraphrases and synonyms
- Implications of success
- ANY communication suggesting completion/correctness

# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.

**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
```

If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.

## When to Use

Use for ANY technical issue:
- Test failures
- Bugs in production
- Unexpected behavior
- Performance problems
- Build failures
- Integration issues

**Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
- Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
- "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
- You've already tried multiple fixes
- Previous fix didn't work
- You don't fully understand the issue

**Don't skip when:**
- Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
- You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
- Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)

## The Four Phases

You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.

### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation

**BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**

1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
   - Don't skip past errors or warnings
   - They often contain the exact solution
   - Read stack traces completely
   - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes

2. **Reproduce Consistently**
   - Can you trigger it reliably?
   - What are the exact steps?
   - Does it happen every time?
   - If not reproducible → gather more data, don't guess

3. **Check Recent Changes**
   - What changed that could cause this?
   - Git diff, recent commits
   - New dependencies, config changes
   - Environmental differences

4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**

   **WHEN system has multiple components (CI → build → signing, API → service → database):**

   **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentation:**
   ```
   For EACH component boundary:
     - Log what data enters component
     - Log what data exits component
     - Verify environment/config propagation
     - Check state at each layer

   Run once to gather evidence showing WHERE it breaks
   THEN analyze evidence to identify failing component
   THEN investigate that specific component
   ```

   **Example (multi-layer system):**
   ```bash
   # Layer 1: Workflow
   echo "=== Secrets available in workflow: ==="
   echo "IDENTITY: $([ -n "${IDENTITY:-}" ] && echo SET || echo UNSET)"

   # Layer 2: Build script
   echo "=== Env vars in build script: ==="
   printenv IDENTITY >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "IDENTITY in environment" || echo "IDENTITY not in environment"

   # Layer 3: Signing script
   echo "=== Keychain state: ==="
   security list-keychains
   security find-identity -v

   # Layer 4: Actual signing
   codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --verbose=4 "$APP"
   ```

   **This reveals:** Which layer fails (secrets → workflow ✓, workflow → build ✗)

5. **Trace Data Flow**

   **WHEN error is deep in call stack:**

   See `root-cause-tracing.md` in this directory for the complete backward tracing technique.

   **Quick version:**
   - Where does bad value originate?
   - What called this with bad value?
   - Keep tracing up until you find the source
   - Fix at source, not at symptom

### Phase 2: Pattern Analysis

**Find the pattern before fixing:**

1. **Find Working Examples**
   - Locate similar working code in same codebase
   - What works that's similar to what's broken?

2. **Compare Against References**
   - If implementing pattern, read reference implementation COMPLETELY
   - Don't skim - read every line
   - Understand the pattern fully before applying

3. **Identify Differences**
   - What's different between working and broken?
   - List every difference, however small
   - Don't assume "that can't matter"

4. **Understand Dependencies**
   - What other components does this need?
   - What settings, config, environment?
   - What assumptions does it make?

### Phase 3: Hypothesis and Testing

**Scientific method:**

1. **Form Single Hypothesis**
   - State clearly: "I think X is the root cause because Y"
   - Write it down
   - Be specific, not vague

2. **Test Minimally**
   - Make the SMALLEST possible change to test hypothesis
   - One variable at a time
   - Don't fix multiple things at once

3. **Verify Before Continuing**
   - Did it work? Yes → Phase 4
   - Didn't work? Form NEW hypothesis
   - DON'T add more fixes on top

4. **When You Don't Know**
   - Say "I don't understand X"
   - Don't pretend to know
   - Ask for help
   - Research more

### Phase 4: Implementation

**Fix the root cause, not the symptom:**

1. **Create Failing Test Case**
   - Simplest possible reproduction
   - Automated test if possible
   - One-off test script if no framework
   - MUST have before fixing
   - Use the `superpowers:test-driven-development` skill for writing proper failing tests

2. **Implement Single Fix**
   - Address the root cause identified
   - ONE change at a time
   - No "while I'm here" improvements
   - No bundled refactoring

3. **Verify Fix**
   - Test passes now?
   - No other tests broken?
   - Issue actually resolved?
   - Use the `superpowers:verification-before-completion` skill before claiming success

4. **If Fix Doesn't Work**
   - STOP
   - Count: How many fixes have you tried?
   - If < 3: Return to Phase 1, re-analyze with new information
   - **If ≥ 3: STOP and question the architecture (step 5 below)**
   - DON'T attempt Fix #4 without architectural discussion

5. **If 3+ Fixes Failed: Question Architecture**

   **Pattern indicating architectural problem:**
   - Each fix reveals new shared state/coupling/problem in different place
   - Fixes require "massive refactoring" to implement
   - Each fix creates new symptoms elsewhere

   **STOP and question fundamentals:**
   - Is this pattern fundamentally sound?
   - Are we "sticking with it through sheer inertia"?
   - Should we refactor architecture vs. continue fixing symptoms?

   **Discuss with your human partner before attempting more fixes**

   This is NOT a failed hypothesis - this is a wrong architecture.

- "Just try changing X and see if it works"
- "Add multiple changes, run tests"
- "Skip the test, I'll manually verify"

# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.

**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
```

If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.

## When to Use

Use for ANY technical issue:
- Test failures
- Bugs in production
- Unexpected behavior
- Performance problems
- Build failures
- Integration issues

**Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
- Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
- "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
- You've already tried multiple fixes
- Previous fix didn't work
- You don't fully understand the issue

**Don't skip when:**
- Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
- You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
- Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)

## The Four Phases

You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.

### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation

**BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**

1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
   - Don't skip past errors or warnings
   - They often contain the exact solution
   - Read stack traces completely
   - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes

2. **Reproduce Consistently**
   - Can you trigger it reliably?
   - What are the exact steps?
   - Does it happen every time?
   - If not reproducible → gather more data, don't guess

3. **Check Recent Changes**
   - What changed that could cause this?
   - Git diff, recent commits
   - New dependencies, config changes
   - Environmental differences

4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**

   **WHEN system has multiple components (CI → build → signing, API → service → database):**

   **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentation:**
   ```
   For EACH component boundary:
     - Log what data enters component
     - Log what data exits component
     - Verify environment/config propagation
     - Check state at each layer

   Run once to gather evidence showing WHERE it breaks
   THEN analyze evidence to identify failing component
   THEN investigate that specific component
   ```

   **Example (multi-layer system):**
   ```bash
   # Layer 1: Workflow
   echo "=== Secrets available in workflow: ==="
   echo "IDENTITY: $([ -n "${IDENTITY:-}" ] && echo SET || echo UNSET)"

   # Layer 2: Build script
   echo "=== Env vars in build script: ==="
   printenv IDENTITY >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "IDENTITY in environment" || echo "IDENTITY not in environment"

   # Layer 3: Signing script
   echo "=== Keychain state: ==="
   security list-keychains
   security find-identity -v

   # Layer 4: Actual signing
   codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --verbose=4 "$APP"
   ```

   **This reveals:** Which layer fails (secrets → workflow ✓, workflow → build ✗)

5. **Trace Data Flow**

   **WHEN error is deep in call stack:**

   See `root-cause-tracing.md` in this directory for the complete backward tracing technique.

   **Quick version:**
   - Where does bad value originate?
   - What called this with bad value?
   - Keep tracing up until you find the source
   - Fix at source, not at symptom

### Phase 2: Pattern Analysis

**Find the pattern before fixing:**

1. **Find Working Examples**
   - Locate similar working code in same codebase
   - What works that's similar to what's broken?

2. **Compare Against References**
   - If implementing pattern, read reference implementation COMPLETELY
   - Don't skim - read every line
   - Understand the pattern fully before applying

3. **Identify Differences**
   - What's different between working and broken?
   - List every difference, however small
   - Don't assume "that can't matter"

4. **Understand Dependencies**
   - What other components does this need?
   - What settings, config, environment?
   - What assumptions does it make?

### Phase 3: Hypothesis and Testing

**Scientific method:**

1. **Form Single Hypothesis**
   - State clearly: "I think X is the root cause because Y"
   - Write it down
   - Be specific, not vague

2. **Test Minimally**
   - Make the SMALLEST possible change to test hypothesis
   - One variable at a time
   - Don't fix multiple things at once

3. **Verify Before Continuing**
   - Did it work? Yes → Phase 4
   - Didn't work? Form NEW hypothesis
   - DON'T add more fixes on top

4. **When You Don't Know**
   - Say "I don't understand X"
   - Don't pretend to know
   - Ask for help
   - Research more

### Phase 4: Implementation

**Fix the root cause, not the symptom:**

1. **Create Failing Test Case**
   - Simplest possible reproduction
   - Automated test if possible
   - One-off test script if no framework
   - MUST have before fixing
   - Use the `superpowers:test-driven-development` skill for writing proper failing tests

2. **Implement Single Fix**
   - Address the root cause identified
   - ONE change at a time
   - No "while I'm here" improvements
   - No bundled refactoring

3. **Verify Fix**
   - Test passes now?
   - No other tests broken?
   - Issue actually resolved?
   - Use the `superpowers:verification-before-completion` skill before claiming success

4. **If Fix Doesn't Work**
   - STOP
   - Count: How many fixes have you tried?
   - If < 3: Return to Phase 1, re-analyze with new information
   - **If ≥ 3: STOP and question the architecture (step 5 below)**
   - DON'T attempt Fix #4 without architectural discussion

5. **If 3+ Fixes Failed: Question Architecture**

   **Pattern indicating architectural problem:**
   - Each fix reveals new shared state/coupling/problem in different place
   - Fixes require "massive refactoring" to implement
   - Each fix creates new symptoms elsewhere

   **STOP and question fundamentals:**
   - Is this pattern fundamentally sound?
   - Are we "sticking with it through sheer inertia"?
   - Should we refactor architecture vs. continue fixing symptoms?

   **Discuss with your human partner before attempting more fixes**

   This is NOT a failed hypothesis - this is a wrong architecture.

## Red Flags - STOP and Follow Process

If you catch yourself thinking:
- "Quick fix for now, investigate later"
- "Just try changing X and see if it works"
- "Add multiple changes, run tests"
- "Skip the test, I'll manually verify"
- "It's probably X, let me fix that"
- "I don't fully understand but this might work"
- "Pattern says X but I'll adapt it differently"
- "Here are the main problems: [lists fixes without investigation]"
- Proposing solutions before tracing data flow
- **"One more fix attempt" (when already tried 2+)**
- **Each fix reveals new problem in different place**

**ALL of these mean: STOP. Return to Phase 1.**

**If 3+ fixes failed:** Question the architecture (see Phase 4.5)

## your human partner's Signals You're Doing It Wrong

**Watch for these redirections:**
- "Is that not happening?" - You assumed without verifying
- "Will it show us...?" - You should have added evidence gathering
- "Stop guessing" - You're proposing fixes without understanding
- "Ultra-think this" - Question fundamentals, not just symptoms
- "We're stuck?" (frustrated) - Your approach isn't working

**When you see these:** STOP. Return to Phase 1.

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Issue is simple, don't need process" | Simple issues have root causes too. Process is fast for simple bugs. |
| "Emergency, no time for process" | Systematic debugging is FASTER than guess-and-check thrashing. |
| "Just try this first, then investigate" | First fix sets the pattern. Do it right from the start. |
| "I'll write test after confirming fix works" | Untested fixes don't stick. Test first proves it. |
| "Multiple fixes at once saves time" | Can't isolate what worked. Causes new bugs. |
| "Reference too long, I'll adapt the pattern" | Partial understanding guarantees bugs. Read it completely. |
| "I see the problem, let me fix it" | Seeing symptoms ≠ understanding root cause. |
| "One more fix attempt" (after 2+ failures) | 3+ failures = architectural problem. Question pattern, don't fix again. |

## Quick Reference

| Phase | Key Activities | Success Criteria |
|-------|---------------|------------------|
| **1. Root Cause** | Read errors, reproduce, check changes, gather evidence | Understand WHAT and WHY |
| **2. Pattern** | Find working examples, compare | Identify differences |
| **3. Hypothesis** | Form theory, test minimally | Confirmed or new hypothesis |
| **4. Implementation** | Create test, fix, verify | Bug resolved, tests pass |

## When Process Reveals "No Root Cause"

If systematic investigation reveals issue is truly environmental, timing-dependent, or external:

1. You've completed the process
2. Document what you investigated
3. Implement appropriate handling (retry, timeout, error message)
4. Add monitoring/logging for future investigation

**But:** 95% of "no root cause" cases are incomplete investigation.

## Supporting Techniques

These techniques are part of systematic debugging and available in this directory:

- **`root-cause-tracing.md`** - Trace bugs backward through call stack to find original trigger
- **`defense-in-depth.md`** - Add validation at multiple layers after finding root cause
- **`condition-based-waiting.md`** - Replace arbitrary timeouts with condition polling

# Verification Before Completion

## Overview

**Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

**Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
```

If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

## The Gate Function

```
BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
   - If NO: State actual status with evidence
   - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim

Skip any step = lying, not verifying
```

## Common Failures

| Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
| Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
| Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
| Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
| Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
| Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
| Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |

## Red Flags - STOP

- Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
- Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
- About to commit/push/PR without verification
- Trusting agent success reports
- Relying on partial verification
- Thinking "just this once"
- Tired and wanting work over
- **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**

## Rationalization Prevention

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
| "I'm confident" | Confidence ≠ evidence |
| "Just this once" | No exceptions |
| "Linter passed" | Linter ≠ compiler |
| "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
| "I'm tired" | Exhaustion ≠ excuse |
| "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
| "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |

## Key Patterns

**Tests:**
```
✅ [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"
❌ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"
```

**Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**
```
✅ Write → Run (pass) → Revert fix → Run (MUST FAIL) → Restore → Run (pass)
❌ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)
```

**Build:**
```
✅ [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"
❌ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)
```

**Requirements:**
```
✅ Re-read plan → Create checklist → Verify each → Report gaps or completion
❌ "Tests pass, phase complete"
```

**Agent delegation:**
```
✅ Agent reports success → Check VCS diff → Verify changes → Report actual state
❌ Trust agent report
```

## When To Apply

**ALWAYS before:**
- ANY variation of success/completion claims
- ANY expression of satisfaction
- ANY positive statement about work state
- Committing, PR creation, task completion
- Moving to next task
- Delegating to agents

**Rule applies to:**
- Exact phrases
- Paraphrases and synonyms
- Implications of success
- ANY communication suggesting completion/correctness
