def source_period(directory):
    text = (directory / "business-description.md").read_text()
    match = re.search(r"Audit period ([A-Za-z]+ \d+, \d{4}) to ([A-Za-z]+ \d+, \d{4})\.", text)
    assert match, "Original fixture must document its audit period"
    return tuple(datetime.strptime(value, "%B %d, %Y").date() for value in match.groups())


def source_subcontractors(directory):
    """Independent arithmetic for the reviewed homebuilding source fixture.

    This is a test oracle, not an adapter for arbitrary new evidence. Roofing
    invoices here have differently named proof; they require identity review.
    Full-period exact-name coverage excludes payments; missing/expired proof
    adds 60%, per CG-06 and Nadia's confirmed full-period rule.
    """
    payments = source_rows(directory / "subcontractor-payments.csv")
    certificates = source_rows(directory / "insurance-certificates.csv")
    start, end = source_period(directory)
    totals = dict.fromkeys(("basis", "added", "nonpayroll", "open_basis"), Decimal("0.00"))
    by_code, open_invoices = {}, set()
    for payment in payments:
        amount = Decimal(payment["amount_paid"])
        totals["basis"] += amount
        exact = [c for c in certificates if c["subcontractor"] == payment["subcontractor"]]
        if any(date.fromisoformat(c["coverage_from"]) <= start and
               date.fromisoformat(c["coverage_to"]) >= end for c in exact):
            totals["nonpayroll"] += amount
        elif not exact and payment["work"] == "roofing":
            assert any("roof" in c["subcontractor"].casefold() for c in certificates), "Review the changed fixture's certificate evidence"
            totals["open_basis"] += amount
            open_invoices.add(payment["invoice"])
        else:
            addition = (amount * Decimal("0.60")).quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
            code = {"framing": "H-420", "drywall": "H-420", "roofing": "R-310"}[payment["work"]]
            by_code[code] = by_code.get(code, Decimal("0.00")) + addition
            totals["added"] += addition
            totals["nonpayroll"] += amount - addition
    return totals, by_code, open_invoices

class SourceCatalog:
    """Deduplicate citations without duplicating entire source documents in output."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.entries = []
        self.identifiers = {}

    def reference(self, ref):
        key = ref.source, ref.locator, ref.line_start, ref.line_end, ref.sha256
        if key not in self.identifiers:
            identifier = f"S{len(self.entries) + 1:04d}"
            self.identifiers[key] = identifier
            self.entries.append(dict(id=identifier, source=ref.source, locator=ref.locator,
                line_start=ref.line_start, line_end=ref.line_end, sha256=ref.sha256))
        return self.identifiers[key]

    def encode(self, value):
        if isinstance(value, SourceReference):
            return self.reference(value)
        if isinstance(value, Decimal):
            return str(value)
        if isinstance(value, (date, Path)):
            return value.isoformat() if isinstance(value, date) else str(value)
        if is_dataclass(value):
            result = {field.name: self.encode(getattr(value, field.name)) for field in fields(value)}
            if hasattr(value, "reconciled"):
                result["reconciled"] = bool(value.reconciled)
            return result
        if isinstance(value, dict):
            if all(isinstance(key, str) for key in value):
                return {key: self.encode(item) for key, item in value.items()}
            return [{"key": self.encode(key), "value": self.encode(item)} for key, item in sorted(value.items(), key=lambda pair: repr(pair[0]))]
        if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
            return [self.encode(item) for item in value]
        if value is None or isinstance(value, (str, bool, int)):
            return value
        raise TypeError(f"Unsupported preview value type: {type(value).__name__}")


def _manifest(document):
    return {"path": str(document.path), "sha256": hashlib.sha256(document.text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest(),
            "kind": "csv" if hasattr(document, "columns") else "markdown"}


def _error(kind, message):

def employer_preview(directory, result, errors=()):
    """Project existing decisions; do not evaluate, repair or approve business rules."""
    catalog = SourceCatalog()

    checks = {
        "allocation": result.allocation.reconciliation if result.allocation else None,
        "independent": result.independent_reconciliation,
        "adjustments": result.adjustments.reconciliation if result.adjustments and result.adjustments.lines else None,

    if result.allocation is None or result.independent_reconciliation is None:
        errors.append(_error("ProcessingUnavailable", "; ".join(item.reason for item in result.open_items) or "No verified register/allocation is available."))
    for name, check in checks.items():
        if check is not None and not check.reconciled:
            errors.append(_error("ReconciliationError", f"{name} reconciliation failed; retain the original OPEN findings and controls."))
    weekly = {item.part_id: item for item in result.weekly_results}
    employees = []
    rule_refs = []
    for employee in result.register:
        totals = {}
        pending = 0
        parts = []
        for line in result.allocation.lines if result.allocation else ():
            if line.employee.employee_id != employee.employee_id:
                continue
            if line.status == "OPEN":
                pending += _cents(line.wages, line.part.part_id)
            else:
                totals[line.class_code] = totals.get(line.class_code, 0) + _cents(line.wages, line.part.part_id)
            detail = {"part_id": line.part.part_id, "wages": str(line.wages), "status": line.status,
                "class_code": line.class_code, "rationale_ref": line.rationale_ref, "source": catalog.encode(line.part.source),
                "scope": line.part.scope, "decision": catalog.encode(line.decision),
                "required_confirmation": list(line.required_confirmation)}
            if line.part.part_id in weekly:

                    ride_days=catalog.encode(item.ride_days), route_sources=catalog.encode(item.route_sources))
            if line.decision:
                rule_refs.extend(catalog.encode(line.decision.rule_sources))
            parts.append(detail)
        additions = {}
        for adjustment in result.adjustments.lines if result.adjustments else ():
            if (adjustment.status == "VERIFIED" and adjustment.class_code and
                getattr(adjustment.input_record, "employee_id", None) == employee.employee_id):
                code = adjustment.class_code
                additions[code] = additions.get(code, 0) + _cents(adjustment.payroll_added, adjustment.adjustment_id)
        combined = dict(totals)
        for code, value in additions.items():
            combined[code] = combined.get(code, 0) + value
        if employee.employee_id in result.employee_totals:
            combined = {code: _cents(value, employee.employee_id) for code, value in result.employee_totals[employee.employee_id].items() if code != "OPEN"}
        employees.append({"employee_id": employee.employee_id, "name": employee.name,
            "register_wages": str(employee.wages), "source": catalog.encode(employee.source),
            "verified_wages_by_code": {code: str(_money(value)) for code, value in sorted(totals.items())},
            "verified_adjustment_by_code": {code: str(_money(value)) for code, value in sorted(additions.items())},
            "verified_by_code": {code: str(_money(value)) for code, value in sorted(combined.items())},
            "open_wages": str(_money(pending)) if result.allocation else None, "parts": parts})
    proposals = [{"kind": "classification", "subject": key, "treatment": catalog.encode(value)}
                 for key, value in sorted(result.proposals.items())]
    for line in result.adjustments.lines if result.adjustments else ():
        rule_refs.extend(catalog.encode(line.rule_sources))
        if line.proposal:
            decision = line.input_record.decision
            proposals.append({"kind": "adjustment", "subject": line.adjustment_id,
                "work_code": decision.class_code if decision and decision.status == "CLASSIFIED" else None, "treatment": catalog.encode(line.proposal),
                "required_confirmation": list(line.required_confirmation), "rule_sources": catalog.encode(line.rule_sources),
                "evidence_sources": catalog.encode(line.evidence_sources)})
    review = bool(result.open_items or proposals or any(line.status == "OPEN" for line in (result.allocation.lines if result.allocation else ())))
    output = {"employer": directory.name, "directory": str(directory),
        "status": "ERROR" if errors else "REVIEW" if review else "OK", "errors": errors,
        "audit_period": catalog.encode(result.period),
        "verified_by_code": catalog.encode(result.by_code) if result.allocation else None,
        "open_wages": str(result.independent_reconciliation.unresolved_total) if result.independent_reconciliation else None,
        "open_adjustment_basis": str(result.adjustments.reconciliation.unresolved_basis) if result.adjustments and result.adjustments.lines else None,
        "employee_payroll": employees, "proposals": proposals,
        "questions": catalog.encode(result.open_items), "reconciliation": catalog.encode(checks),
        "adjustments": {"evaluation": "EVALUATED" if result.adjustments and result.adjustments.lines else "NOT_EVALUATED",
            "verified_by_code": catalog.encode(result.adjustments.by_code) if result.adjustments and result.adjustments.lines else None,
            "lines": catalog.encode(result.adjustments.lines) if result.adjustments else []},
        "application": catalog.encode(result.application), "owner": catalog.encode(result.owner_assessment),
        "governing_field": catalog.encode(result.governing_field), "receipts": catalog.encode(result.receipts),
        "rule_references": list(dict.fromkeys(rule_refs)),
        "source_manifest": [_manifest(document) for document in (result.inputs.guide, *result.inputs.records)] if result.inputs else []}
    output["sources"] = catalog.entries
    return output

def source_subcontractors(directory):
    """Independent arithmetic for the reviewed homebuilding source fixture.

    This is a test oracle, not an adapter for arbitrary new evidence. Roofing
    invoices here have differently named proof; they require identity review.
    Full-period exact-name coverage excludes payments; missing/expired proof
    adds 60%, per CG-06 and Nadia's confirmed full-period rule.
    """
    payments = source_rows(directory / "subcontractor-payments.csv")
    certificates = source_rows(directory / "insurance-certificates.csv")
    start, end = source_period(directory)
    totals = dict.fromkeys(("basis", "added", "nonpayroll", "open_basis"), Decimal("0.00"))
    by_code, open_invoices = {}, set()
    for payment in payments:
        amount = Decimal(payment["amount_paid"])
        totals["basis"] += amount
        exact = [c for c in certificates if c["subcontractor"] == payment["subcontractor"]]
        if any(date.fromisoformat(c["coverage_from"]) <= start and
               date.fromisoformat(c["coverage_to"]) >= end for c in exact):
            totals["nonpayroll"] += amount
        elif not exact and payment["work"] == "roofing":
            assert any("roof" in c["subcontractor"].casefold() for c in certificates), "Review the changed fixture's certificate evidence"
            totals["open_basis"] += amount
            open_invoices.add(payment["invoice"])
        else:
            addition = (amount * Decimal("0.60")).quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
            code = {"framing": "H-420", "drywall": "H-420", "roofing": "R-310"}[payment["work"]]
            by_code[code] = by_code.get(code, Decimal("0.00")) + addition
            totals["added"] += addition
            totals["nonpayroll"] += amount - addition
    return totals, by_code, open_invoices

class SourceCatalog:
    """Deduplicate citations without duplicating entire source documents in output."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.entries = []
        self.identifiers = {}

    def reference(self, ref):
        key = ref.source, ref.locator, ref.line_start, ref.line_end, ref.sha256
        if key not in self.identifiers:
            identifier = f"S{len(self.entries) + 1:04d}"
            self.identifiers[key] = identifier
            self.entries.append(dict(id=identifier, source=ref.source, locator=ref.locator,
                line_start=ref.line_start, line_end=ref.line_end, sha256=ref.sha256))
        return self.identifiers[key]

    def encode(self, value):
        if isinstance(value, SourceReference):
            return self.reference(value)
        if isinstance(value, Decimal):
            return str(value)
        if isinstance(value, (date, Path)):
            return value.isoformat() if isinstance(value, date) else str(value)
        if is_dataclass(value):
            result = {field.name: self.encode(getattr(value, field.name)) for field in fields(value)}
            if hasattr(value, "reconciled"):
                result["reconciled"] = bool(value.reconciled)
            return result
        if isinstance(value, dict):
            if all(isinstance(key, str) for key in value):
                return {key: self.encode(item) for key, item in value.items()}
            return [{"key": self.encode(key), "value": self.encode(item)} for key, item in sorted(value.items(), key=lambda pair: repr(pair[0]))]
        if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
            return [self.encode(item) for item in value]
        if value is None or isinstance(value, (str, bool, int)):
            return value
        raise TypeError(f"Unsupported preview value type: {type(value).__name__}")


def _manifest(document):
    return {"path": str(document.path), "sha256": hashlib.sha256(document.text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest(),
            "kind": "csv" if hasattr(document, "columns") else "markdown"}


def _error(kind, message):
    return {"type": kind, "message": str(message)}


def _unavailable(directory, errors):
    return {"employer": directory.name, "directory": str(directory), "status": "ERROR", "errors": errors,
        "verified_by_code": None, "open_wages": None, "open_adjustment_basis": None,
        "employee_payroll": [], "proposals": [], "questions": [], "reconciliation": {},
        "application": None, "source_manifest": [], "sources": []}


def employer_preview(directory, result, errors=()):
    """Project existing decisions; do not evaluate, repair or approve business rules."""
    catalog = SourceCatalog()
    errors = list(errors)
    checks = {
        "allocation": result.allocation.reconciliation if result.allocation else None,
        "independent": result.independent_reconciliation,
        "adjustments": result.adjustments.reconciliation if result.adjustments and result.adjustments.lines else None,
        "weekly": result.weekly_reconciliation,
        "combined": result.combined_reconciliation,
        "travel": result.travel_reconciliation,
    }
    if result.allocation is None or result.independent_reconciliation is None:
        errors.append(_error("ProcessingUnavailable", "; ".join(item.reason for item in result.open_items) or "No verified register/allocation is available."))
    for name, check in checks.items():
        if check is not None and not check.reconciled:
            errors.append(_error("ReconciliationError", f"{name} reconciliation failed; retain the original OPEN findings and controls."))
    weekly = {item.part_id: item for item in result.weekly_results}
    employees = []
    rule_refs = []
    for employee in result.register:
        totals = {}
        pending = 0
        parts = []
        for line in result.allocation.lines if result.allocation else ():
            if line.employee.employee_id != employee.employee_id:
                continue
            if line.status == "OPEN":
                pending += _cents(line.wages, line.part.part_id)
            else:
                totals[line.class_code] = totals.get(line.class_code, 0) + _cents(line.wages, line.part.part_id)
            detail = {"part_id": line.part.part_id, "wages": str(line.wages), "status": line.status,
                "class_code": line.class_code, "rationale_ref": line.rationale_ref, "source": catalog.encode(line.part.source),
                "scope": line.part.scope, "decision": catalog.encode(line.decision),
                "required_confirmation": list(line.required_confirmation)}
            if line.part.part_id in weekly:
                item = weekly[line.part.part_id]
                detail.update(week_start=item.week_start.isoformat(), week_end=item.week_end.isoformat(),
                    ride_days=catalog.encode(item.ride_days), route_sources=catalog.encode(item.route_sources))
            if line.decision:
                rule_refs.extend(catalog.encode(line.decision.rule_sources))
            parts.append(detail)
        additions = {}
        for adjustment in result.adjustments.lines if result.adjustments else ():
            if (adjustment.status == "VERIFIED" and adjustment.class_code and
                getattr(adjustment.input_record, "employee_id", None) == employee.employee_id):
                code = adjustment.class_code
                additions[code] = additions.get(code, 0) + _cents(adjustment.payroll_added, adjustment.adjustment_id)
        combined = dict(totals)
        for code, value in additions.items():
            combined[code] = combined.get(code, 0) + value
        if employee.employee_id in result.employee_totals:
            combined = {code: _cents(value, employee.employee_id) for code, value in result.employee_totals[employee.employee_id].items() if code != "OPEN"}
        employees.append({"employee_id": employee.employee_id, "name": employee.name,
            "register_wages": str(employee.wages), "source": catalog.encode(employee.source),
            "verified_wages_by_code": {code: str(_money(value)) for code, value in sorted(totals.items())},
            "verified_adjustment_by_code": {code: str(_money(value)) for code, value in sorted(additions.items())},
            "verified_by_code": {code: str(_money(value)) for code, value in sorted(combined.items())},
            "open_wages": str(_money(pending)) if result.allocation else None, "parts": parts})
    proposals = [{"kind": "classification", "subject": key, "treatment": catalog.encode(value)}
                 for key, value in sorted(result.proposals.items())]
    for line in result.adjustments.lines if result.adjustments else ():
        rule_refs.extend(catalog.encode(line.rule_sources))
        if line.proposal:
            decision = line.input_record.decision
            proposals.append({"kind": "adjustment", "subject": line.adjustment_id,
                "work_code": decision.class_code if decision and decision.status == "CLASSIFIED" else None, "treatment": catalog.encode(line.proposal),
                "required_confirmation": list(line.required_confirmation), "rule_sources": catalog.encode(line.rule_sources),
                "evidence_sources": catalog.encode(line.evidence_sources)})
    review = bool(result.open_items or proposals or any(line.status == "OPEN" for line in (result.allocation.lines if result.allocation else ())))
    output = {"employer": directory.name, "directory": str(directory),
        "status": "ERROR" if errors else "REVIEW" if review else "OK", "errors": errors,
        "audit_period": catalog.encode(result.period),
        "verified_by_code": catalog.encode(result.by_code) if result.allocation else None,
        "open_wages": str(result.independent_reconciliation.unresolved_total) if result.independent_reconciliation else None,
        "open_adjustment_basis": str(result.adjustments.reconciliation.unresolved_basis) if result.adjustments and result.adjustments.lines else None,
        "employee_payroll": employees, "proposals": proposals,
        "questions": catalog.encode(result.open_items), "reconciliation": catalog.encode(checks),
        "adjustments": {"evaluation": "EVALUATED" if result.adjustments and result.adjustments.lines else "NOT_EVALUATED",
            "verified_by_code": catalog.encode(result.adjustments.by_code) if result.adjustments and result.adjustments.lines else None,
            "lines": catalog.encode(result.adjustments.lines) if result.adjustments else []},
        "application": catalog.encode(result.application), "owner": catalog.encode(result.owner_assessment),
        "governing_field": catalog.encode(result.governing_field), "receipts": catalog.encode(result.receipts),
        "rule_references": list(dict.fromkeys(rule_refs)),
        "source_manifest": [_manifest(document) for document in (result.inputs.guide, *result.inputs.records)] if result.inputs else []}
    output["sources"] = catalog.entries
    return output


def _execute(guide, interview, directory, files):
    try:
        errors = [_error("MissingSource", f"Required employer source is missing: {directory / filename}")
            for filename in (files.business, files.notes, files.payroll, files.application) if not (directory / filename).is_file()]
        result = process_employer(guide, directory, interview, files=files)
        return employer_preview(directory, result, errors)
    except Exception as exc:
        # Isolate unexpected employer failures as well as source failures. Never
        # turn an exception into zero payroll or reuse a previous employer result.
        return _unavailable(directory, [_error(type(exc).__name__, exc)])

def source_period(directory):
    text = (directory / "business-description.md").read_text()
    match = re.search(r"Audit period ([A-Za-z]+ \d+, \d{4}) to ([A-Za-z]+ \d+, \d{4})\.", text)
    assert match, "Original fixture must document its audit period"
    return tuple(datetime.strptime(value, "%B %d, %Y").date() for value in match.groups())


def source_subcontractors(directory):
    """Independent arithmetic for the reviewed homebuilding source fixture.

    This is a test oracle, not an adapter for arbitrary new evidence. Roofing
    invoices here have differently named proof; they require identity review.
    Full-period exact-name coverage excludes payments; missing/expired proof
    adds 60%, per CG-06 and Nadia's confirmed full-period rule.
    """
    payments = source_rows(directory / "subcontractor-payments.csv")
    certificates = source_rows(directory / "insurance-certificates.csv")
    start, end = source_period(directory)
    totals = dict.fromkeys(("basis", "added", "nonpayroll", "open_basis"), Decimal("0.00"))
    by_code, open_invoices = {}, set()
    for payment in payments:
        amount = Decimal(payment["amount_paid"])
        totals["basis"] += amount
        exact = [c for c in certificates if c["subcontractor"] == payment["subcontractor"]]
        if any(date.fromisoformat(c["coverage_from"]) <= start and
               date.fromisoformat(c["coverage_to"]) >= end for c in exact):
            totals["nonpayroll"] += amount
        elif not exact and payment["work"] == "roofing":
            assert any("roof" in c["subcontractor"].casefold() for c in certificates), "Review the changed fixture's certificate evidence"
            totals["open_basis"] += amount
            open_invoices.add(payment["invoice"])
        else:
            addition = (amount * Decimal("0.60")).quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
            code = {"framing": "H-420", "drywall": "H-420", "roofing": "R-310"}[payment["work"]]
            by_code[code] = by_code.get(code, Decimal("0.00")) + addition
            totals["added"] += addition
            totals["nonpayroll"] += amount - addition
    return totals, by_code, open_invoices

# Brainstorming

You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
anything gets built.

People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.

## First: What Do You Actually Know?

Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
why?

- **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
  blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
- **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.

Before you start implementing, you must, in order:

1. Lay out the approaches in a message of their own, and have your
   human partner pick one (see Lay out the approaches).
2. Write the design doc, short or full (see Size the Work).
3. Get their approval of that doc.
4. Invoke the superpowers:writing-plans skill.

Two things aren't implementing: a spike they said yes to (see Spike to
feel things out), and doing what they asked once they've opted out of
the questions.

## Look Before You Ask

In an existing project, or when they've given you context (a spec, a plan,
a handoff, files they pointed at, earlier conversation), dig in before your
first message. Read what they referred to and the code or material it
connects to, and keep reading until you can explain how the relevant
parts work today and what this change would touch. Never ask what the
project or their context already answers.

## Your First Message

Move the work forward, with one of these:

- **They've already said what they want** (a spec, a plan, a detailed
  request): aim for about 200 words for the whole message. Echo their
  request back in your own words, so they can see whether you've got its
  shape: what they want, who it's for, and why, as far as they've said.
  Add what you found that bears on it: how the relevant parts work today
  and what the change would touch. If you found something they may not
  have considered that would change what they're asking for or how it
  has to be built, like a constraint, a conflict, or a cheaper path, say
  so plainly. How to build it comes later, once you understand what they
  want (see Lay out the approaches). End with one line inviting
  corrections, then one question about what they want: the thing their
  request leaves open whose answer would most change what gets built.
  Specs are often incomplete, so confirm before you build on one.
- **They haven't:** one open question, in their own terms, about the
  biggest thing their request leaves unsettled. Say why you're asking:
  what the answer would change about what you build. For "a website for
  my bakery": "If it's mostly for people deciding whether to stop by,
  I'd lead with hours and what's in the case today; taking orders is a
  different site. What do you want someone to do when they land on it?"

How the message ends depends on whether their message asked for
brainstorming:

- **They asked for it** (by name, by invoking it, or by asking for a
  design discussion): end with your question. They want this
  conversation.
- **They didn't:** they may not want a conversation at all. After your
  question, add a light, one-line offer to just get going instead, like
  "Or if you'd rather I just dive in, say so." If they take you up on
  it, this skill is done: state any significant how-it-gets-made choice
  (platform, language, medium) in one plain line, then do what they
  asked through the normal workflow.

That's the whole message.

## The Conversation

Each message ends with one question: a single sentence with no list of
example answers hanging off it. Use plain language, pitched just a little
above where your human partner is. Match their vocabulary; never use
process jargon. You never need to quote this skill to your human
partner.

Be clear and concise. Lead with what matters. Avoid jargon. When you
report what you found, give them the most important findings and offer
the rest.

**Get them describing.** Open questions come first. Their own words carry
intent that your options can't. Offer a short menu only when they're
stuck. When they say "just guess" or "what do you think?", propose
something concrete.

**How it gets made.** Every project rests on choices about medium, tools,
materials, and resources: the platform, programming language, and
libraries for an app; the medium for a piece of art. Find out early which
of those choices they want to make, which they're handing to you, and what
they already have to work with. Someone with strong views or skills will
want to talk it through. Someone counting on you needs sensible defaults,
said in plain words. When there's existing work, build on what it already
uses. Any choice you make goes in the design as your call, never as
something they agreed to.

**Ground to cover.** This is territory, not a script. Never read these
out as questions:

- what kind of thing this is, and what makes it special
- why now, and what success looks like to them
- goals, non-goals, and anti-goals (what would make this a failure even
  if it technically works)
- prior art: what they've seen elsewhere, loved or hated
- current state: what exists now, what they've tried
- the details they care about

**Make every question specific** to their project and what they've told
you. Ask Socratically, the way a sharp colleague would: build each
question on their last answer or on something you found, so it helps
them think through a consequence or a case they may have missed
("Voting closes before the meeting, and two members joined this month.
Does someone who joins mid-round get a vote?"). When the reason isn't
already plain, say what you're hoping to learn or what the answer would
change. A proposal they can correct, plus your reason for it, often
beats a question.

**Offer recon.** Once you have a bit of grounding and looking further
would help, offer to go look: deeper into their codebase or project,
their own files and data, or the web. Say what you'd look for. They
decide whether you go.

**Lay out the approaches.** Once you understand what they want, and
before you write anything up, put the ways of building it in a message
of its own. Come up with several real alternatives and drop the weak
ones, including any that work against why they want it and any the
existing work rules out. Present the two or three that remain, grounding
each in what the project actually does and saying what it trades off.
Recommend one and say why, then ask which way they want to go. When
there's genuinely one sensible way, say so and explain why the others
don't fit. This is for how it gets built; for what they want, get them
describing first.

**Show, don't tell.** Offer the visual companion (below) whenever seeing
would help more than reading:

- something they'll look at: a screen, a page, a printout, a sign
- a layout or arrangement: of a screen, a room, a schedule
- a flow or a sequence of steps
- options that would look different from each other
- a structure that's easier to see than read: a diagram, a timeline, a map

Once they've accepted, use it for mockups to react to, side-by-side
options, and throwaway prototypes they can click.

**Spike to feel things out.** Agentic work is waterfall, but very, very
fast. A quick throwaway build is often the cheapest way to learn what
they want or whether something works. Offer one when it would help.
When they just want to spike, get out of the way. Spikes get no tests
or minimal ones, aren't bulletproof, and skip the plan, implementation,
and review process. Bring what the spike taught you back into the
conversation.

## Play It Back

Play back as you go. As soon as you understand one part well enough to
describe it (what it's for and who it serves, say, or how one piece
behaves), describe that part back in about 200-300 words, then return to
questions about the next part. Playback and questions alternate through
the whole conversation; the last chunk covers whatever is left.

Only what they said goes in as theirs. Anything you filled in goes in
as your proposal, with your reason. End each chunk by asking what's wrong
or missing.

Before you send a chunk, check it: does it describe something they'll
look at, like a page, a screen, a schedule, or a printout? If so, and
they haven't seen the visual companion offer yet, send the offer instead
(its own message, below) and hold the chunk for the next message. Once
they've accepted, put a mockup next to the description.

## Size the Work

Once you understand what they want and they've picked an approach, say
how big the work is in plain words. They can override it.

| Size | The design doc |
|------|----------------|
| A small change | a short one: what you already covered together, written down |
| A project | the full written design (below) |

Short or full, the design doc has an **Approaches** part: the two or
three ways you considered building it, what each trades off, which one
they picked, and why. They pick in the conversation, before you write
the doc.

If it grows mid-task, stop, say so, and step up a size.

If this is really several independent projects, say so, agree on an
order, and brainstorm them one at a time.

## The Written Design

Write a plain document a talented builder in the domain could plan
from without going back to your human partner. Cover:

- intent and the why
- goals, non-goals, anti-goals
- constraints
- approaches (above)
- the parts of the how they decided, as they decided them
- what's left to the builder

For a small change, the short design covers the same points in a line
or two each and goes straight to your human partner, without the
builder check.

**Where it goes:** in a software repo,
`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, committed.
Otherwise, ask. Your human partner's preferences override both.

**Builder check** (for a project): dispatch a fresh subagent with
`builder-check-prompt.md` in this directory. When you tell your human
partner you're writing it up, say a reviewer will read it first and you
may come back once with a few questions. Don't hand over the document
until the check is back. Sort what the builder asks into three piles:

- **Answered already** by the conversation or the project: put the answer
  in the document.
- **Minor:** a sensible builder could settle it without changing what gets
  built. Settle it yourself and mark it in the document as your call.
- **Theirs:** only your human partner can answer it, and the answer changes
  what gets built.

Bring the "theirs" pile in one message, most important first. Update the
document with their answers, then hand it over with a short list of the
calls you made so they can check those while reading. That's the only
round of questions the check produces. Without a subagent tool, read the
document as that builder yourself.

<HARD-GATE>
Nothing gets built until your human partner approves the design doc:
the short one for a small change, the full one for a project.
Building includes writing product code, scaffolding, installing
dependencies, creating projects, and invoking an implementation skill.
Reading and exploring are fine.

Two exceptions. If they opted out of the questions, the skill is done
and the gate goes with it. A spike they said yes to may be built; it
stays labeled throwaway, and keeping what it produced is a new request
that comes back through this gate.

After the design doc is approved, the next step is the plan: invoke
superpowers:writing-plans and no other skill.
</HARD-GATE>

## Red Flags

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "I'll offer a menu of what they might want" | Options steer. Ask them to describe it first. |
| "I'll fill in sensible defaults" | Good. Say them out loud. A default they never heard is one they couldn't reject. |
| "I've answered their questions, so I'll write the doc" | Lay out the approaches first, in a message of their own. |
| "I should explain the process first" | Ask your question. The process shows itself. |
| "They said 'sounds good' to the idea" | Approval covers what you showed them. A design doc you haven't written isn't approved. |
| "The spike works, I'll keep building on it" | Keeping it is a new request. Back through the gate. |

## Visual Companion

A browser tab for showing mockups, diagrams, and prototypes. It's a
tool, not a mode: accepting it doesn't send every question to the
browser.

**Offer it just-in-time.** Offer it the first time one of the moments
above comes up, never upfront. The offer is its own message with nothing
else in it:

> "This might be easier if I show you. Want me to open a browser tab with some mockups?"

If they decline, stay in text and don't offer again unless they raise it.

**Per question, ask: would they understand this better by seeing it?**
Mockups, layouts, diagrams, and side-by-side designs go in the browser.
Requirements, scope, tradeoffs, and conceptual choices stay in text. A
question about a UI topic isn't automatically a visual question.

If they accept, read `visual-companion.md` in this directory before
starting the server.
# Writing Good Tests

**Load this reference when:** writing or changing tests, adding mocks, or
adding cleanup/helper methods for tests.

## Overview

A test exists to catch a specific break. Two principles govern everything
here:

```
1. Every test names the break it catches
2. Every test exercises the real thing
```

Strict TDD produces both naturally: a test written first and watched
failing against real code has already proven it can fail, and only earns
a mock when the real dependency proves slow or external.

## Principle 1: Name the Break

Before writing the test body, answer: **what production change should
make this test fail — and is that change a bug or a decision?** A test
earns its place by catching a wrong branch, missing side effect, wrong
argument, boundary case, or broken contract.

**Derive expectations independently.** Use literals and hand-checked
fixtures; table-driven tests with literal `want` values are the preferred
shape. An expectation computed by the code under test — or its helpers —
passes no matter what that code does:

```typescript
// ❌ Mirror assertion: the same builder computes both sides — always true
const expected = buildSearchQuery({ tag: 'urgent' });
expect(buildSearchQuery({ tag: 'urgent' })).toBe(expected);

// ✅ Hand-derived literal
expect(buildSearchQuery({ tag: 'urgent' })).toBe('tag:"urgent"');
```

**No change detectors.** If only intentional decisions can fail a test —
a constant's value, exact message wording, private structure — it fires
on redesign and sleeps through bugs. Test the behavior that depends on
the decision: not `expect(MAX_RETRIES).toBe(5)` but "a failing call is
retried 5 times and the 6th attempt never happens."

**Behavior, not text.** Asserting that a script, skill, or config
contains an exact line proves only that the source is the source. Run
scripts against controlled inputs and assert outputs, side effects, or
exit codes. Documents that instruct agents are tested by the consuming
agent's behavior (superpowers:writing-skills); prose for humans earns no
test at all.

**Your code, not the framework.** Test the contract your code makes at
its boundaries — the route you register, the query you emit, the payload
you produce. Upstream mechanics are their maintainers' tests to write
(the classic: asserting your router invokes a registered handler — that
is the framework's test, not yours). When upstream behavior genuinely
surprised you, write one narrow characterization test naming the
assumption. The same boundary applies inside your code: constructors,
getters, constants, and trivial forwarding earn tests only when they
validate, normalize, default, derive, enforce, or cause side effects —
otherwise assert the first consumer-visible result that depends on them.

### Gate Function

```
BEFORE writing the test body:
  Name the production change that would make this test fail.

  Cannot name one            → redesign around an observable behavior
  "The source text changed"  → run the artifact and assert its effects
  Only intentional decisions → change detector; test the behavior
                               that depends on the decision

  Confirm the expected value is derived without the code under test.
  IF it reuses the code's logic or helpers:
    Replace it with a literal or hand-checked fixture
```

## Principle 2: Exercise the Real Thing

**The mock earns no assertions.** A mock assertion passes when the mock
is present and fails when it is absent — it says nothing about the
component. Assert the real component's behavior; if the mock is what you
are checking, unmock it or delete the assertion.

```typescript
// ✅ Real behavior
expect(screen.getByRole('navigation')).toBeInTheDocument();

// ❌ Mock existence
expect(screen.getByTestId('sidebar-mock')).toBeInTheDocument();
```

**your human partner's correction:** "Are we testing the behavior of a
mock?"

**Mock at the right level.** Learn every side effect of the real method
before replacing it; mock the slow or external operation and keep what
the test depends on real. When unsure, run the test against the real
implementation first and observe what actually needs to happen.

```typescript
// ❌ The mock swallows the config write that duplicate detection reads
vi.mock('ToolCatalog', () => ({
  discoverAndCacheTools: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(undefined)
}));

// ✅ Mock only the slow server startup; the config write stays real
vi.mock('MCPServerManager');
```

**Make doubles specific.** When arguments, call counts, or ordering are
part of the contract, assert them — a fake that accepts anything verifies
nothing. Give each branch (success, error, malformed) its own fixture or
spy, so the wrong branch cannot satisfy the expectation.

**Mirror real data completely.** Mock the complete structure as it exists
in reality — all documented fields — not just the ones your test reads.
Partial mocks fail silently when downstream code reads an omitted field:
the test passes while integration breaks.

**Production classes carry production methods only.** Cleanup that only
tests need lives in test utilities, never as a `destroy()` on the
production class. Ask: is this method called only from tests? Does this
class own this resource's lifecycle? Wrong answers → test utility.

**Prefer real components over complex mocks.** When mock setup outgrows
the test logic, mocks miss methods the real components have, or tests
break when the mock changes, switch to an integration test with real
components. **your human partner's question:** "Do we need to be using a
mock here?"

    """Return a deterministic in-memory preview, rereading sources on every call."""
    if (employer is None) == (all_employers is None):

def run_preview(guide, interview, *, employer=None, all_employers=None, files=EmployerFiles()):
    """Return a deterministic in-memory preview, rereading sources on every call."""
    if (employer is None) == (all_employers is None):
        raise ValueError("Select exactly one employer directory or all-employers directory")
    guide, interview = (Path(path).expanduser().absolute() for path in (guide, interview))
    root = Path(employer if employer is not None else all_employers).expanduser().absolute()
    report = {"schema_version": 1, "preview_only": True, "status": "ERROR", "mode": "single" if employer is not None else "all",
        "guide": str(guide), "interview": str(interview), "shared_sources": [],
        "discovery": {"root": str(root), "method": "selected_directory" if employer is not None else "immediate_nonhidden_subdirectories", "excluded_entries": []},
        "errors": [], "employers": []}
    try:
        for source in (guide, interview):
            document = read_markdown(source)
            if source == guide and not document.paragraph_ids:
                raise InputError(f"{guide}: no classification paragraph identifiers found")
            report["shared_sources"].append(_manifest(document))
        if not root.is_dir():
            raise InputError(f"Employer input directory is missing or is not a directory: {root}")
        if employer is not None:
            directories = [root]
        else:
            entries = sorted(root.iterdir(), key=lambda path: path.name)
            directories = [path for path in entries if not path.name.startswith(".") and path.is_dir()]
            report["discovery"]["excluded_entries"] = [path.name for path in entries if path not in directories]
            if not directories:
                raise InputError(f"No employer subdirectories were discovered in {root}")
    except (InputError, OSError) as exc:
        report["errors"].append(_error(type(exc).__name__, exc))
        return report
    seen = {}
    for directory in directories:
        try:
            canonical = directory.resolve(strict=True)
            if canonical in seen:
                entry = _unavailable(directory, [_error("DuplicateDirectoryAlias", f"Directory alias duplicates {seen[canonical]}; the same employer sources are not processed twice.")])
            else:
                seen[canonical] = directory
                entry = _execute(guide, interview, directory, files)
        except (OSError, RuntimeError) as exc:
            entry = _unavailable(directory, [_error(type(exc).__name__, exc)])
        report["employers"].append(entry)
    statuses = {entry["status"] for entry in report["employers"]}
    report["status"] = "ERROR" if "ERROR" in statuses else "REVIEW" if "REVIEW" in statuses else "OK"
    return report

    lines = ["PREVIEW ONLY — no final deliverable files", f"Status: {report['status']}",

    if report["discovery"]["excluded_entries"]:
        lines.append("Excluded container entries: " + ", ".join(report["discovery"]["excluded_entries"]))
    for employer in report["employers"]:

name: verification-before-completion
description: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always
---

# Verification Before Completion

## Overview

**Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

**Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
```

If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

## The Gate Function

```
BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
   - If NO: State actual status with evidence
   - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim

Skip any step = lying, not verifying
```

## Common Failures

| Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
| Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
| Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
| Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
| Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
| Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
| Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |

## Red Flags - STOP

- Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
- Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
- About to commit/push/PR without verification
- Trusting agent success reports
- Relying on partial verification
- Thinking "just this once"
- Tired and wanting work over
- **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**

## Rationalization Prevention

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
| "I'm confident" | Confidence ≠ evidence |
| "Just this once" | No exceptions |
| "Linter passed" | Linter ≠ compiler |
| "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
| "I'm tired" | Exhaustion ≠ excuse |
| "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
| "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |

## Key Patterns

**Tests:**
```
✅ [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"
❌ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"
```

**Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**
```
✅ Write → Run (pass) → Revert fix → Run (MUST FAIL) → Restore → Run (pass)
❌ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)
```

**Build:**
```
✅ [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"
❌ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)
```

**Requirements:**
```
✅ Re-read plan → Create checklist → Verify each → Report gaps or completion
❌ "Tests pass, phase complete"
```

**Agent delegation:**
```
✅ Agent reports success → Check VCS diff → Verify changes → Report actual state
❌ Trust agent report
```

## When To Apply

**ALWAYS before:**
- ANY variation of success/completion claims
- ANY expression of satisfaction
- ANY positive statement about work state
- Committing, PR creation, task completion
- Moving to next task
- Delegating to agents

**Rule applies to:**
- Exact phrases
- Paraphrases and synonyms
- Implications of success
- ANY communication suggesting completion/correctness

name: verification-before-completion
description: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always
---

# Verification Before Completion

## Overview

**Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

**Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
```

If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

## The Gate Function

```
BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
   - If NO: State actual status with evidence
   - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim

Skip any step = lying, not verifying
```

## Common Failures

| Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
| Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
| Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
| Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
| Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
| Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
| Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |

## Red Flags - STOP

- Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
- Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
- About to commit/push/PR without verification
- Trusting agent success reports
- Relying on partial verification
- Thinking "just this once"
- Tired and wanting work over
- **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**

## Rationalization Prevention

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
| "I'm confident" | Confidence ≠ evidence |
| "Just this once" | No exceptions |
| "Linter passed" | Linter ≠ compiler |
| "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
| "I'm tired" | Exhaustion ≠ excuse |
| "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
| "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |

## Key Patterns

**Tests:**
```
✅ [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"
❌ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"
```

**Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**
```
✅ Write → Run (pass) → Revert fix → Run (MUST FAIL) → Restore → Run (pass)
❌ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)
```

**Build:**
```
✅ [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"
❌ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)
```

**Requirements:**
```
✅ Re-read plan → Create checklist → Verify each → Report gaps or completion
❌ "Tests pass, phase complete"
```

**Agent delegation:**
```
✅ Agent reports success → Check VCS diff → Verify changes → Report actual state
❌ Trust agent report
```

## When To Apply

**ALWAYS before:**
- ANY variation of success/completion claims
- ANY expression of satisfaction
- ANY positive statement about work state
- Committing, PR creation, task completion
- Moving to next task
- Delegating to agents

**Rule applies to:**
- Exact phrases
- Paraphrases and synonyms
- Implications of success
- ANY communication suggesting completion/correctness

# Class Code and Premium Audit Assistant — INSURANCE-01

This reusable Agent Skill reads employer records, applies Linden Shore Mutual's
verified company rules, allocates payroll with Decimal, and produces classification
CSVs, confirmation questions and an audit report. Unsupported decisions remain
OPEN for human review. It calculates no rates or insurance premiums.

The Skill instructions are in
[skills/class-code-assistant/SKILL.md](skills/class-code-assistant/SKILL.md).
The CLI uses the same existing processing engine; another employer using a
supported evidence schema needs different input paths, not Python source edits.

## Setup

Use Python **3.10 or newer**. The runtime and unittest suite use only the Python
standard library, including `decimal`, `csv`, `json`, `hashlib`, `pathlib` and
`unittest`. No pip installation, virtual environment, API key or network service
is required. Verification for this checkout used Python 3.12.3 on Linux/WSL.

Open a Bash-compatible terminal at the repository root, where this README and
`skills/` are located. Check the interpreter:

```bash
python3 -B -c 'import sys; assert sys.version_info >= (3, 10), "Python 3.10+ required"; print(sys.version)'
```

`-B` avoids writing Python bytecode into the source tree. Paths may contain spaces;
keep the quotes used below. Bash and `mktemp` are used by the example shell setup;
the Python components themselves require neither Bash nor `mktemp`.

## Current sources and preserved development snapshots

For each new audit, obtain the authoritative source locations from the auditor.

| Input | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Classification Guide | Current readable UTF-8 Markdown with original `CG-xx` paragraph definitions. Use company rules; public manuals are not substitutes. |
| Interview evidence | Complete original Markdown export containing verified house practices, timestamps and applicability clarifications. Preserve original bytes and metadata. |
| Employer records | One employer directory, or a container of employer directories. Base files are `business-description.md`, `field-notes.md`, `payroll-register.csv` and `application.md`. |
| Supporting records | Activity, receipts, certificates, subcontractor payments, weekly payroll and travel evidence required by that business; see the schema reference below. |
| Original assignment | Retain as the output/scope authority. It is a human reference; the runtime does not parse its DOCX or extract a ZIP. |

Every invocation rereads the selected Guide, interview and employer records.
Question/report generation obtains their locations from the supplied review-state
file, rereads them, and rejects results that disagree with that state. There is no
automatic fallback to a development snapshot. Keep sources stable during a run;
SHA-256 checks detect changes but do not authenticate documents.

This workstation has local development snapshots at
`/home/maxg/insurance01-inputs/classification-guide.md` and
`/home/maxg/insurance01-inputs/employer-files/` (six employer folders, 34 records).
The original assignment, Guide and employer ZIP remain unchanged under
`/mnt/c/Users/PC/Downloads/`. These external files are not bundled into the
repository or guaranteed available on another computer. The preserved final
interview export is
[interviews/ch03-premium-audit-20261105-0222(1).md](<interviews/ch03-premium-audit-20261105-0222(1).md>).
The preserved repository deliverables are results from those snapshots, not a
source of classification answers for a new run.

Set these shell variables to current auditor-supplied locations:

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH` | Absolute path to the current Guide Markdown. |
| `AUDIT_INTERVIEW_PATH` | Absolute path to the complete original interview Markdown. |
| `AUDIT_EMPLOYER_DIR` | One selected employer directory. |
| `AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT` | Container holding employer directories for an all-employer run. |
| `AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR` | Fresh output directory, outside authoritative sources. |

To reproduce the preserved six-employer development run on **this workstation**,
use the explicit snapshot configuration below. For another audit, replace the
source values with the auditor's current locations; these examples are not
authoritative defaults. The temporary output directory protects existing deliverables:

```bash
export AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH='/home/maxg/insurance01-inputs/classification-guide.md'
export AUDIT_INTERVIEW_PATH="$PWD/interviews/ch03-premium-audit-20261105-0222(1).md"
export AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT='/home/maxg/insurance01-inputs/employer-files'
export AUDIT_EMPLOYER_DIR="$AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT/patuxent-electric"
export AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR="$(mktemp -d /tmp/insurance01-rerun.XXXXXX)"
```

## Preview one employer or every discovered employer

Preview one selected employer; this writes only to stdout:

```bash
python3 -B skills/class-code-assistant/preview.py \
  --guide "$AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH" \
  --interview "$AUDIT_INTERVIEW_PATH" \
  --employer "$AUDIT_EMPLOYER_DIR"
```

Preview all immediate nonhidden employer directories. With the development
configuration above, this discovers all six employers:

```bash
python3 -B skills/class-code-assistant/preview.py \
  --guide "$AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH" \
  --interview "$AUDIT_INTERVIEW_PATH" \
  --all-employers "$AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT"
```

Add `--format json` for structured stdout with Decimal amounts encoded as strings.
Discovery is sorted, does not recurse into nested employer containers, and keeps
employer identities/results separate. Root files and hidden entries are excluded
and reported; incomplete employer directories produce errors, not silent skips.

For a new employer, put its current records in a separate directory, set
`AUDIT_EMPLOYER_DIR` to that location, and run the first command. For a new batch,
change `AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT` and run the second. No employer list or answer table
needs editing. Existing adapters support restaurant/catering, legal offices,
roofing/siding contractors, residential homebuilders, couriers and electrical work.
This is a narrow evidence adapter: unknown duties, other industries and
unrecognized evidence need human review.

The base payroll schema is `employee_id,name,position,wages_paid`. CSVs must be
UTF-8, comma-delimited, correctly quoted and have unique nonblank headers and
consistent field counts. Currency is plain decimal dollars with at most two
fractional digits; dollar signs, thousands separators, scientific notation and
non-finite amounts are invalid. Negative inputs are retained for review, not
automatically accepted by every calculation. See
[EMPLOYER_PROCESSING.md](skills/class-code-assistant/EMPLOYER_PROCESSING.md) for
the exact supported narrative/activity schemas and supporting files.

Use `--file payroll=records/wages.csv` when a supported record has a different
relative filename. Repeat `--file FIELD=RELATIVE_PATH` for distinct fields, using
the same overrides in the CSV, question and report commands. All-employer
overrides apply to every selected folder. This changes filenames, not column
schemas or business rules. Absolute paths, parent traversal and unknown/duplicate
override fields are rejected. A new schema may require a separately reviewed
adapter; do not edit code or borrow another industry's rule to force a result.

## Regenerate the CSVs, review state, questions and report

Run these commands in order using the variables above. The regenerated set goes
into `AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR`, leaving the repository's existing `deliverables/` untouched.

First generate all discovered employer CSVs and the required machine-readable state:

```bash
python3 -B skills/class-code-assistant/generate_codes.py \
  --guide "$AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH" \
  --interview "$AUDIT_INTERVIEW_PATH" \
  --all-employers "$AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT" \
  --output-dir "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/codes" \
  --review-state "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/classification-review.json"
```

For a single-employer deliverable set, replace `--all-employers
"$AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT"` with `--employer "$AUDIT_EMPLOYER_DIR"` and choose a
fresh output directory. Later commands infer that selection from the review state
and work for either mode.

Generate the unanswered confirmation questions from current sources and validated
CSVs/review state:

```bash
python3 -B skills/class-code-assistant/audit_questions.py \
  --review-state "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/classification-review.json" \
  --codes-dir "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/codes" \
  --output "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/audit-questions.md"
```

Generate the report using those same dependencies:

```bash
python3 -B skills/class-code-assistant/audit_report.py \
  --review-state "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/classification-review.json" \
  --codes-dir "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/codes" \
  --questions "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/audit-questions.md" \
  --output "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/audit-report.md"
```

The existing required outputs are:

| Location | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `deliverables/codes/` | `annapolis-courier.csv`, `bay-crest-exteriors.csv`, `harbor-point-legal.csv`, `larkspur-lane-bistro.csv`, `patuxent-electric.csv`, `severn-homebuilders.csv`. |
| `deliverables/classification-review.json` | Verified-only scope, complete processing/source state, OPEN amounts, proposals, reconciliations, CSV rows/paths/hashes. |
| `deliverables/audit-questions.md` | Unanswered questions, payment/employee identifiers, recorded priorities, source/record coverage index. |
| `deliverables/audit-report.md` | Reported versus verified payroll/differences, every adjustment, evidence, human-review requirements, reconciliations and separate OPEN/proposed treatments. |

The regenerated set uses the same filenames under your chosen directory. CSV
filenames derive from employer folder slugs; conflicting/empty slugs are errors.
Each CSV has exactly `class_code,payroll_allocated,rationale_ref`, one nonzero
verified row per code, two-decimal payroll and the exact original Guide paragraph
defining that code. The JSON state is a required supporting artifact, not a
substitute for either Markdown deliverable.

See [CSV_GENERATION.md](skills/class-code-assistant/CSV_GENERATION.md),
[AUDIT_QUESTIONS.md](skills/class-code-assistant/AUDIT_QUESTIONS.md) and
[AUDIT_REPORT.md](skills/class-code-assistant/AUDIT_REPORT.md) for validation/API details.

## Interpret results and obtain human approval

- **VERIFIED**: current evidence supports the calculation/classification; this
  is not employer confirmation or final audit sign-off. Verified corrections
  remain in the report and CSVs even when another item for that employer is OPEN.
- **OPEN**: classification, identity, rule applicability or evidence needs human
  resolution. OPEN wages remain in register reconciliation but are excluded from
  verified CSVs. Unresolved payment basis is separate and is not automatically payroll.
- **PROPOSED**: a conditional, unapproved alternative with specific evidence and
  approval requirements. Never add it to verified totals. No supported proposal
  means no guessed treatment.

Employee payroll must reconcile to the cent: verified base wages plus OPEN wages
equal the register. Verified adjustments are then added once. Evaluated payments
equal payroll additions plus excluded/nonpayroll amounts plus unresolved payment
basis. Known payroll may include OPEN wages; it is not all verified/classified.
An absent adjustment check is NOT EVALUATED, not a verified zero. A negative
application difference caused by omitted OPEN wages is provisional, not a verified
wage reduction. Code transfers do not add the same wages a second time.

References preserve original filenames, employee/payment IDs, dates/pay weeks,
exact `CG-xx` identifiers, interview timestamps, line spans and SHA-256. Source IDs
are local to each employer. The questions' record index maps physical CSV rows to
confirmations. Hashes identify bytes; they do not establish authentic/complete
evidence, insurance coverage or employee identity.

The employer payroll/records contact confirms facts and supplies records. The
assigned human auditor decides policy applicability and approves proposed
treatments and application corrections. Capture confirmations without rewriting
original evidence, then rerun with supported current inputs. The report generator
validates the exact **unanswered** question document; edited/answered questions
are not an implemented approval ledger and will be rejected as changed.
Arithmetic balance and exit code 0 never approve an OPEN case.

## Errors, reruns and limitations

| Condition | Behavior / next action |
| --- | --- |
| Missing/unreadable base files, malformed CSV, invalid money | Contextual error; correct records/paths and rerun. Never substitute snapshots or zero payroll. |
| Missing activity evidence, changed rules, unknown duties, identity conflicts or unsupported scope | ERROR or OPEN/REVIEW depending on the adapter; obtain evidence and auditor decisions. No invented code. |
| One employer errors in a batch | Preview/CSV stages retain separate successful results and identify errors. Require a complete error-free CSV/review set before questions/report. |
| Current sources, CSVs or questions disagree with state | Stop dependent generation. Stabilize sources and regenerate the dependency chain into a fresh directory. |
| Identical rerun at the same paths | Identical output bytes are reused without changing output mtimes. |
| Changed results or different selection at occupied destinations | Differing outputs and symbolic-link output files are refused. Use fresh paths; preserve reviewed work. |
| New output directory | CSVs can match byte-for-byte; JSON/Markdown record new output paths and dependent hashes. Compare financial/evidence content separately from declared run metadata. |

"""Fresh real-source dependency chains; never replace the published artifacts."""

from dataclasses import dataclass
import csv
from datetime import date, datetime
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import tempfile
import unittest

from audit_questions import generate_questions
from audit_report import generate_report
from generate_codes import generate_csvs


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RealAuditChain:
    inputs: Path
    guide: Path
    interview: Path
    codes: Path
    review: Path
    questions: Path
    output: Path
    state: dict
    question_result: dict
    report: dict


def fresh_real_chain(register_cleanup):
    """Reread configurable sources and build every dependency in a new directory."""
    component = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
    inputs = Path(os.environ.get("INSURANCE01_TEST_INPUTS", Path.home() / "insurance01-inputs")).expanduser().resolve()
    guide = inputs / "classification-guide.md"
    employers = inputs / "employer-files"
    interview = Path(os.environ.get("INSURANCE01_TEST_INTERVIEW",
        component.parents[1] / "interviews/ch03-premium-audit-20261105-0222(1).md")).expanduser().resolve()
    if not guide.is_file() or not employers.is_dir() or not interview.is_file():
        raise unittest.SkipTest("Auditor-supplied local sources are unavailable; synthetic tests remain portable")
    temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="independent real audit ")
    register_cleanup(temporary.cleanup)
    root = Path(temporary.name)
    codes, review = root / "codes", root / "classification-review.json"
    questions, output = root / "audit-questions.md", root / "audit-report.md"
    state = generate_csvs(guide, interview, all_employers=employers,
                         output_dir=codes, review_state=review)
    if state["errors"] or state["processing"]["errors"] or state["status"] == "ERROR":
        errors = [*state["errors"], *state["processing"]["errors"],
                  *(error for entry in state["processing"]["employers"] for error in entry["errors"])]
        raise AssertionError(f"Fresh real-source processing failed: {errors}")
    question_result = generate_questions(review, codes_dir=codes, output=questions)
    report = generate_report(review, codes_dir=codes, questions=questions, output=output)
    return RealAuditChain(inputs, guide, interview, codes, review, questions, output,
                         state, question_result, report)


def source_rows(path):
    """Read original CSV values independently of the production input reader."""
    with Path(path).open(encoding="utf-8", newline="") as stream:
        return list(csv.DictReader(stream))


def source_period(directory):
    text = (directory / "business-description.md").read_text()
    match = re.search(r"Audit period ([A-Za-z]+ \d+, \d{4}) to ([A-Za-z]+ \d+, \d{4})\.", text)
    assert match, "Original fixture must document its audit period"
    return tuple(datetime.strptime(value, "%B %d, %Y").date() for value in match.groups())


def source_subcontractors(directory):
    """Independent arithmetic for the reviewed homebuilding source fixture.

    This is a test oracle, not an adapter for arbitrary new evidence. Roofing
    invoices here have differently named proof; they require identity review.
    Full-period exact-name coverage excludes payments; missing/expired proof
    adds 60%, per CG-06 and Nadia's confirmed full-period rule.
    """
    payments = source_rows(directory / "subcontractor-payments.csv")
    certificates = source_rows(directory / "insurance-certificates.csv")
    start, end = source_period(directory)
    totals = dict.fromkeys(("basis", "added", "nonpayroll", "open_basis"), Decimal("0.00"))
    by_code, open_invoices = {}, set()
    for payment in payments:
        amount = Decimal(payment["amount_paid"])
        totals["basis"] += amount
        exact = [c for c in certificates if c["subcontractor"] == payment["subcontractor"]]
        if any(date.fromisoformat(c["coverage_from"]) <= start and
               date.fromisoformat(c["coverage_to"]) >= end for c in exact):
            totals["nonpayroll"] += amount
        elif not exact and payment["work"] == "roofing":
            assert any("roof" in c["subcontractor"].casefold() for c in certificates), "Review the changed fixture's certificate evidence"
            totals["open_basis"] += amount
            open_invoices.add(payment["invoice"])
        else:
            addition = (amount * Decimal("0.60")).quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
            code = {"framing": "H-420", "drywall": "H-420", "roofing": "R-310"}[payment["work"]]
            by_code[code] = by_code.get(code, Decimal("0.00")) + addition
            totals["added"] += addition
            totals["nonpayroll"] += amount - addition
    return totals, by_code, open_invoices


def source_controls(inputs):
    """Resum original registers/payments under the reviewed evidence boundaries.

    No generated decisions, CSVs, review JSON or report totals are read here.
    Legal site visits lack an established field rule; mixed catering duties
    lack complete audit-period receipts. Their original wages stay OPEN.
    Allowances above $47/documented day count; zero-day allowances stay OPEN.
    """
    portfolio = dict.fromkeys(("register", "added", "open_wages", "basis", "nonpayroll", "open_basis"), Decimal("0.00"))
    employers = {}
    for directory in sorted((inputs / "employer-files").iterdir()):
        if not directory.is_dir() or directory.name.startswith("."):
            continue
        payroll = source_rows(directory / "payroll-register.csv")
        values = dict.fromkeys(portfolio, Decimal("0.00"))
        values["register"] = sum((Decimal(r["wages_paid"]) for r in payroll), Decimal("0.00"))
        open_workers = source_open_workers(directory, payroll)
        values["open_wages"] = sum((Decimal(r["wages_paid"]) for r in payroll
                                    if r["employee_id"] in open_workers), Decimal("0.00"))
        if (directory / "subcontractor-payments.csv").is_file():
            subcontractors, _, _ = source_subcontractors(directory)
            for key, amount in subcontractors.items():
                values[key] += amount
        for row in payroll:
            if "travel_allowance_paid" not in row:
                continue
            allowance, days = Decimal(row["travel_allowance_paid"]), int(row["travel_days"])
            values["basis"] += allowance
            if days == 0 and allowance:
                values["open_basis"] += allowance
            else:
                excluded = min(allowance, Decimal("47") * days)
                values["nonpayroll"] += excluded
                values["added"] += allowance - excluded
        for key in portfolio:
            portfolio[key] += values[key]
        employers[directory.name] = values
    for values in [portfolio, *employers.values()]:
        values["verified"] = values["register"] - values["open_wages"] + values["added"]
        values["cash"] = values["register"] + values["basis"]
        values["known_payroll"] = values["register"] + values["added"]
    return portfolio, employers


def source_open_workers(directory, payroll):
    """Identify the reviewed fixture's unsupported duties from original records."""
    business = " ".join((directory / "business-description.md").read_text().split())
    if "law office" in business:
        visits = source_rows(directory / "site-signin-log.csv")
        return {r["employee_id"] for r in visits}
    if (directory / "gross-receipts.csv").is_file():
        receipts = source_rows(directory / "gross-receipts.csv")
        _, end = source_period(directory)
        assert end.strftime("%Y-%m") not in {r["month"] for r in receipts}, "Review newly complete catering evidence"
        return {r["employee_id"] for r in payroll if r["position"] in {"Catering Lead", "Event Cook", "Event Server"}}
    return set()

# Class Code and Premium Audit Assistant — INSURANCE-01

This reusable Agent Skill reads employer records, applies Linden Shore Mutual's
verified company rules, allocates payroll with Decimal, and produces classification
CSVs, confirmation questions and an audit report. Unsupported decisions remain
OPEN for human review. It calculates no rates or insurance premiums.

The Skill instructions are in
[skills/class-code-assistant/SKILL.md](skills/class-code-assistant/SKILL.md).
The CLI uses the same existing processing engine; another employer using a
supported evidence schema needs different input paths, not Python source edits.

## Setup

Use Python **3.10 or newer**. The runtime and unittest suite use only the Python
standard library, including `decimal`, `csv`, `json`, `hashlib`, `pathlib` and
`unittest`. No pip installation, virtual environment, API key or network service
is required. Verification for this checkout used Python 3.12.3 on Linux/WSL.

Open a Bash-compatible terminal at the repository root, where this README and
`skills/` are located. Check the interpreter:

```bash
python3 -B -c 'import sys; assert sys.version_info >= (3, 10), "Python 3.10+ required"; print(sys.version)'
```

`-B` avoids writing Python bytecode into the source tree. Paths may contain spaces;
keep the quotes used below. Bash and `mktemp` are used by the example shell setup;
the Python components themselves require neither Bash nor `mktemp`.

## Current sources and preserved development snapshots

For each new audit, obtain the authoritative source locations from the auditor.

| Input | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Classification Guide | Current readable UTF-8 Markdown with original `CG-xx` paragraph definitions. Use company rules; public manuals are not substitutes. |
| Interview evidence | Complete original Markdown export containing verified house practices, timestamps and applicability clarifications. Preserve original bytes and metadata. |
| Employer records | One employer directory, or a container of employer directories. Base files are `business-description.md`, `field-notes.md`, `payroll-register.csv` and `application.md`. |
| Supporting records | Activity, receipts, certificates, subcontractor payments, weekly payroll and travel evidence required by that business; see the schema reference below. |
| Original assignment | Retain as the output/scope authority. It is a human reference; the runtime does not parse its DOCX or extract a ZIP. |

Every invocation rereads the selected Guide, interview and employer records.
Question/report generation obtains their locations from the supplied review-state
file, rereads them, and rejects results that disagree with that state. There is no
automatic fallback to a development snapshot. Keep sources stable during a run;
SHA-256 checks detect changes but do not authenticate documents.

This workstation has local development snapshots at
`/home/maxg/insurance01-inputs/classification-guide.md` and
`/home/maxg/insurance01-inputs/employer-files/` (six employer folders, 34 records).
The original assignment, Guide and employer ZIP remain unchanged under
`/mnt/c/Users/PC/Downloads/`. These external files are not bundled into the
repository or guaranteed available on another computer. The preserved final
interview export is
[interviews/ch03-premium-audit-20261105-0222(1).md](<interviews/ch03-premium-audit-20261105-0222(1).md>).
The preserved repository deliverables are results from those snapshots, not a
source of classification answers for a new run.

Set these shell variables to current auditor-supplied locations:

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH` | Absolute path to the current Guide Markdown. |
| `AUDIT_INTERVIEW_PATH` | Absolute path to the complete original interview Markdown. |

| `AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT` | Container holding employer directories for an all-employer run. |
| `AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR` | Fresh output directory, outside authoritative sources. |

To reproduce the preserved six-employer development run on **this workstation**,

## Preview one employer or every discovered employer

Preview one selected employer; this writes only to stdout:

  --guide "$AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH" \

Preview all immediate nonhidden employer directories. With the development
