Add `--format json` for structured stdout with Decimal amounts encoded as strings.
Discovery is sorted, does not recurse into nested employer containers, and keeps
employer identities/results separate. Root files and hidden entries are excluded
and reported; incomplete employer directories produce errors, not silent skips.

For a new employer, put its current records in a separate directory, set
`AUDIT_EMPLOYER_DIR` to that location, and run the first command. For a new batch,
change `AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT` and run the second. No employer list or answer table
needs editing. Existing adapters support restaurant/catering, legal offices,
roofing/siding contractors, residential homebuilders, couriers and electrical work.
This is a narrow evidence adapter: unknown duties, other industries and
unrecognized evidence need human review.

The base payroll schema is `employee_id,name,position,wages_paid`. CSVs must be
UTF-8, comma-delimited, correctly quoted and have unique nonblank headers and
consistent field counts. Currency is plain decimal dollars with at most two
fractional digits; dollar signs, thousands separators, scientific notation and

automatically accepted by every calculation. See

the same overrides in the CSV, question and report commands. All-employer
overrides apply to every selected folder. This changes filenames, not column
schemas or business rules. Absolute paths, parent traversal and unknown/duplicate
override fields are rejected. A new schema may require a separately reviewed
adapter; do not edit code or borrow another industry's rule to force a result.

Run these commands in order using the variables above. The regenerated set goes
into `AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR`, leaving the repository's existing `deliverables/` untouched.

and work for either mode.

Generate the unanswered confirmation questions from current sources and validated

Generate the report using those same dependencies:

```bash
python3 -B skills/class-code-assistant/audit_report.py \
  --review-state "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/classification-review.json" \
  --codes-dir "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/codes" \
  --questions "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/audit-questions.md" \
  --output "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/audit-report.md"
```

| `deliverables/classification-review.json` | Verified-only scope, complete processing/source state, OPEN amounts, proposals, reconciliations, CSV rows/paths/hashes. |
| `deliverables/audit-questions.md` | Unanswered questions, payment/employee identifiers, recorded priorities, source/record coverage index. |
| `deliverables/audit-report.md` | Reported versus verified payroll/differences, every adjustment, evidence, human-review requirements, reconciliations and separate OPEN/proposed treatments. |

The regenerated set uses the same filenames under your chosen directory. CSV
filenames derive from employer folder slugs; conflicting/empty slugs are errors.
Each CSV has exactly `class_code,payroll_allocated,rationale_ref`, one nonzero
verified row per code, two-decimal payroll and the exact original Guide paragraph
defining that code. The JSON state is a required supporting artifact, not a
substitute for either Markdown deliverable.

See [CSV_GENERATION.md](skills/class-code-assistant/CSV_GENERATION.md),
[AUDIT_QUESTIONS.md](skills/class-code-assistant/AUDIT_QUESTIONS.md) and
[AUDIT_REPORT.md](skills/class-code-assistant/AUDIT_REPORT.md) for validation/API details.

## Interpret results and obtain human approval

- **VERIFIED**: current evidence supports the calculation/classification; this
  is not employer confirmation or final audit sign-off. Verified corrections
  remain in the report and CSVs even when another item for that employer is OPEN.
- **OPEN**: classification, identity, rule applicability or evidence needs human
  resolution. OPEN wages remain in register reconciliation but are excluded from
  verified CSVs. Unresolved payment basis is separate and is not automatically payroll.
- **PROPOSED**: a conditional, unapproved alternative with specific evidence and
  approval requirements. Never add it to verified totals. No supported proposal
  means no guessed treatment.

Employee payroll must reconcile to the cent: verified base wages plus OPEN wages
equal the register. Verified adjustments are then added once. Evaluated payments
equal payroll additions plus excluded/nonpayroll amounts plus unresolved payment
basis. Known payroll may include OPEN wages; it is not all verified/classified.
An absent adjustment check is NOT EVALUATED, not a verified zero. A negative
application difference caused by omitted OPEN wages is provisional, not a verified
wage reduction. Code transfers do not add the same wages a second time.

References preserve original filenames, employee/payment IDs, dates/pay weeks,
exact `CG-xx` identifiers, interview timestamps, line spans and SHA-256. Source IDs
are local to each employer. The questions' record index maps physical CSV rows to
confirmations. Hashes identify bytes; they do not establish authentic/complete
evidence, insurance coverage or employee identity.

The employer payroll/records contact confirms facts and supplies records. The
assigned human auditor decides policy applicability and approves proposed
treatments and application corrections. Capture confirmations without rewriting
original evidence, then rerun with supported current inputs. The report generator
validates the exact **unanswered** question document; edited/answered questions
are not an implemented approval ledger and will be rejected as changed.
Arithmetic balance and exit code 0 never approve an OPEN case.

## Errors, reruns and limitations

| Condition | Behavior / next action |
| --- | --- |
| Missing/unreadable base files, malformed CSV, invalid money | Contextual error; correct records/paths and rerun. Never substitute snapshots or zero payroll. |
| Missing activity evidence, changed rules, unknown duties, identity conflicts or unsupported scope | ERROR or OPEN/REVIEW depending on the adapter; obtain evidence and auditor decisions. No invented code. |
| One employer errors in a batch | Preview/CSV stages retain separate successful results and identify errors. Require a complete error-free CSV/review set before questions/report. |
| Current sources, CSVs or questions disagree with state | Stop dependent generation. Stabilize sources and regenerate the dependency chain into a fresh directory. |
| Identical rerun at the same paths | Identical output bytes are reused without changing output mtimes. |
| Changed results or different selection at occupied destinations | Differing outputs and symbolic-link output files are refused. Use fresh paths; preserve reviewed work. |
| New output directory | CSVs can match byte-for-byte; JSON/Markdown record new output paths and dependent hashes. Compare financial/evidence content separately from declared run metadata. |

"""Fresh real-source dependency chains; never replace the published artifacts."""

from dataclasses import dataclass
import csv
from datetime import date, datetime
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import tempfile
import unittest

from audit_questions import generate_questions
from audit_report import generate_report
from generate_codes import generate_csvs


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RealAuditChain:
    inputs: Path
    guide: Path
    interview: Path
    codes: Path
    review: Path
    questions: Path
    output: Path
    state: dict
    question_result: dict
    report: dict


def fresh_real_chain(register_cleanup):
    """Reread configurable sources and build every dependency in a new directory."""
    component = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
    inputs = Path(os.environ.get("INSURANCE01_TEST_INPUTS", Path.home() / "insurance01-inputs")).expanduser().resolve()
    guide = inputs / "classification-guide.md"
    employers = inputs / "employer-files"
    interview = Path(os.environ.get("INSURANCE01_TEST_INTERVIEW",
        component.parents[1] / "interviews/ch03-premium-audit-20261105-0222(1).md")).expanduser().resolve()
    if not guide.is_file() or not employers.is_dir() or not interview.is_file():
        raise unittest.SkipTest("Auditor-supplied local sources are unavailable; synthetic tests remain portable")
    temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="independent real audit ")
    register_cleanup(temporary.cleanup)
    root = Path(temporary.name)
    codes, review = root / "codes", root / "classification-review.json"
    questions, output = root / "audit-questions.md", root / "audit-report.md"
    state = generate_csvs(guide, interview, all_employers=employers,
                         output_dir=codes, review_state=review)
    if state["errors"] or state["processing"]["errors"] or state["status"] == "ERROR":
        errors = [*state["errors"], *state["processing"]["errors"],
                  *(error for entry in state["processing"]["employers"] for error in entry["errors"])]
        raise AssertionError(f"Fresh real-source processing failed: {errors}")
    question_result = generate_questions(review, codes_dir=codes, output=questions)
    report = generate_report(review, codes_dir=codes, questions=questions, output=output)
    return RealAuditChain(inputs, guide, interview, codes, review, questions, output,
                         state, question_result, report)


def source_rows(path):
    """Read original CSV values independently of the production input reader."""
    with Path(path).open(encoding="utf-8", newline="") as stream:
        return list(csv.DictReader(stream))


def source_period(directory):
    text = (directory / "business-description.md").read_text()
    match = re.search(r"Audit period ([A-Za-z]+ \d+, \d{4}) to ([A-Za-z]+ \d+, \d{4})\.", text)
    assert match, "Original fixture must document its audit period"
    return tuple(datetime.strptime(value, "%B %d, %Y").date() for value in match.groups())


def source_subcontractors(directory):
    """Independent arithmetic for the reviewed homebuilding source fixture.

    This is a test oracle, not an adapter for arbitrary new evidence. Roofing
    invoices here have differently named proof; they require identity review.
    Full-period exact-name coverage excludes payments; missing/expired proof
    adds 60%, per CG-06 and Nadia's confirmed full-period rule.
    """
    payments = source_rows(directory / "subcontractor-payments.csv")
    certificates = source_rows(directory / "insurance-certificates.csv")
    start, end = source_period(directory)
    totals = dict.fromkeys(("basis", "added", "nonpayroll", "open_basis"), Decimal("0.00"))
    by_code, open_invoices = {}, set()
    for payment in payments:
        amount = Decimal(payment["amount_paid"])
        totals["basis"] += amount
        exact = [c for c in certificates if c["subcontractor"] == payment["subcontractor"]]
        if any(date.fromisoformat(c["coverage_from"]) <= start and
               date.fromisoformat(c["coverage_to"]) >= end for c in exact):
            totals["nonpayroll"] += amount
        elif not exact and payment["work"] == "roofing":
            assert any("roof" in c["subcontractor"].casefold() for c in certificates), "Review the changed fixture's certificate evidence"
            totals["open_basis"] += amount
            open_invoices.add(payment["invoice"])
        else:
            addition = (amount * Decimal("0.60")).quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
            code = {"framing": "H-420", "drywall": "H-420", "roofing": "R-310"}[payment["work"]]
            by_code[code] = by_code.get(code, Decimal("0.00")) + addition
            totals["added"] += addition
            totals["nonpayroll"] += amount - addition
    return totals, by_code, open_invoices


def source_controls(inputs):
    """Resum original registers/payments under the reviewed evidence boundaries.

    No generated decisions, CSVs, review JSON or report totals are read here.
    Legal site visits lack an established field rule; mixed catering duties
    lack complete audit-period receipts. Their original wages stay OPEN.
    Allowances above $47/documented day count; zero-day allowances stay OPEN.
    """
    portfolio = dict.fromkeys(("register", "added", "open_wages", "basis", "nonpayroll", "open_basis"), Decimal("0.00"))
    employers = {}
    for directory in sorted((inputs / "employer-files").iterdir()):
        if not directory.is_dir() or directory.name.startswith("."):
            continue
        payroll = source_rows(directory / "payroll-register.csv")
        values = dict.fromkeys(portfolio, Decimal("0.00"))
        values["register"] = sum((Decimal(r["wages_paid"]) for r in payroll), Decimal("0.00"))
        open_workers = source_open_workers(directory, payroll)
        values["open_wages"] = sum((Decimal(r["wages_paid"]) for r in payroll
                                    if r["employee_id"] in open_workers), Decimal("0.00"))
        if (directory / "subcontractor-payments.csv").is_file():
            subcontractors, _, _ = source_subcontractors(directory)
            for key, amount in subcontractors.items():
                values[key] += amount
        for row in payroll:
            if "travel_allowance_paid" not in row:
                continue
            allowance, days = Decimal(row["travel_allowance_paid"]), int(row["travel_days"])
            values["basis"] += allowance
            if days == 0 and allowance:
                values["open_basis"] += allowance
            else:
                excluded = min(allowance, Decimal("47") * days)
                values["nonpayroll"] += excluded
                values["added"] += allowance - excluded
        for key in portfolio:
            portfolio[key] += values[key]
        employers[directory.name] = values
    for values in [portfolio, *employers.values()]:
        values["verified"] = values["register"] - values["open_wages"] + values["added"]
        values["cash"] = values["register"] + values["basis"]
        values["known_payroll"] = values["register"] + values["added"]
    return portfolio, employers


def source_open_workers(directory, payroll):
    """Identify the reviewed fixture's unsupported duties from original records."""
    business = " ".join((directory / "business-description.md").read_text().split())
    if "law office" in business:
        visits = source_rows(directory / "site-signin-log.csv")
        return {r["employee_id"] for r in visits}
    if (directory / "gross-receipts.csv").is_file():
        receipts = source_rows(directory / "gross-receipts.csv")
        _, end = source_period(directory)
        assert end.strftime("%Y-%m") not in {r["month"] for r in receipts}, "Review newly complete catering evidence"
        return {r["employee_id"] for r in payroll if r["position"] in {"Catering Lead", "Event Cook", "Event Server"}}
    return set()

# Class Code and Premium Audit Assistant — INSURANCE-01

This reusable Agent Skill reads employer records, applies Linden Shore Mutual's
verified company rules, allocates payroll with Decimal, and produces classification
CSVs, confirmation questions and an audit report. Unsupported decisions remain
OPEN for human review. It calculates no rates or insurance premiums.

The Skill instructions are in
[skills/class-code-assistant/SKILL.md](skills/class-code-assistant/SKILL.md).
The CLI uses the same existing processing engine; another employer using a
supported evidence schema needs different input paths, not Python source edits.

## Setup

Use Python **3.10 or newer**. The runtime and unittest suite use only the Python
standard library, including `decimal`, `csv`, `json`, `hashlib`, `pathlib` and
`unittest`. No pip installation, virtual environment, API key or network service
is required. Verification for this checkout used Python 3.12.3 on Linux/WSL.

Open a Bash-compatible terminal at the repository root, where this README and
`skills/` are located. Check the interpreter:

```bash
python3 -B -c 'import sys; assert sys.version_info >= (3, 10), "Python 3.10+ required"; print(sys.version)'
```

`-B` avoids writing Python bytecode into the source tree. Paths may contain spaces;
keep the quotes used below. Bash and `mktemp` are used by the example shell setup;
the Python components themselves require neither Bash nor `mktemp`.

## Current sources and preserved development snapshots

For each new audit, obtain the authoritative source locations from the auditor.

| Input | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Classification Guide | Current readable UTF-8 Markdown with original `CG-xx` paragraph definitions. Use company rules; public manuals are not substitutes. |
| Interview evidence | Complete original Markdown export containing verified house practices, timestamps and applicability clarifications. Preserve original bytes and metadata. |
| Employer records | One employer directory, or a container of employer directories. Base files are `business-description.md`, `field-notes.md`, `payroll-register.csv` and `application.md`. |
| Supporting records | Activity, receipts, certificates, subcontractor payments, weekly payroll and travel evidence required by that business; see the schema reference below. |
| Original assignment | Retain as the output/scope authority. It is a human reference; the runtime does not parse its DOCX or extract a ZIP. |

Every invocation rereads the selected Guide, interview and employer records.
Question/report generation obtains their locations from the supplied review-state
file, rereads them, and rejects results that disagree with that state. There is no
automatic fallback to a development snapshot. Keep sources stable during a run;
SHA-256 checks detect changes but do not authenticate documents.

This workstation has local development snapshots at
`/home/maxg/insurance01-inputs/classification-guide.md` and
`/home/maxg/insurance01-inputs/employer-files/` (six employer folders, 34 records).
The original assignment, Guide and employer ZIP remain unchanged under
`/mnt/c/Users/PC/Downloads/`. These external files are not bundled into the
repository or guaranteed available on another computer. The preserved final
interview export is
[interviews/ch03-premium-audit-20261105-0222(1).md](<interviews/ch03-premium-audit-20261105-0222(1).md>).
The preserved repository deliverables are results from those snapshots, not a
source of classification answers for a new run.

Set these shell variables to current auditor-supplied locations:

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH` | Absolute path to the current Guide Markdown. |
| `AUDIT_INTERVIEW_PATH` | Absolute path to the complete original interview Markdown. |
| `AUDIT_EMPLOYER_DIR` | One selected employer directory. |
| `AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT` | Container holding employer directories for an all-employer run. |
| `AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR` | Fresh output directory, outside authoritative sources. |

To reproduce the preserved six-employer development run on **this workstation**,
use the explicit snapshot configuration below. For another audit, replace the
source values with the auditor's current locations; these examples are not
authoritative defaults. The temporary output directory protects existing deliverables:

```bash
export AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH='/home/maxg/insurance01-inputs/classification-guide.md'
export AUDIT_INTERVIEW_PATH="$PWD/interviews/ch03-premium-audit-20261105-0222(1).md"
export AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT='/home/maxg/insurance01-inputs/employer-files'
export AUDIT_EMPLOYER_DIR="$AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT/patuxent-electric"
export AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR="$(mktemp -d /tmp/insurance01-rerun.XXXXXX)"
```

## Preview one employer or every discovered employer

Preview one selected employer; this writes only to stdout:

```bash
python3 -B skills/class-code-assistant/preview.py \
  --guide "$AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH" \
  --interview "$AUDIT_INTERVIEW_PATH" \
  --employer "$AUDIT_EMPLOYER_DIR"
```

Preview all immediate nonhidden employer directories. With the development
configuration above, this discovers all six employers:

```bash
python3 -B skills/class-code-assistant/preview.py \
  --guide "$AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH" \
  --interview "$AUDIT_INTERVIEW_PATH" \
  --all-employers "$AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT"
```

Add `--format json` for structured stdout with Decimal amounts encoded as strings.
Discovery is sorted, does not recurse into nested employer containers, and keeps
employer identities/results separate. Root files and hidden entries are excluded
and reported; incomplete employer directories produce errors, not silent skips.

For a new employer, put its current records in a separate directory, set
`AUDIT_EMPLOYER_DIR` to that location, and run the first command. For a new batch,
change `AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT` and run the second. No employer list or answer table
needs editing. Existing adapters support restaurant/catering, legal offices,
roofing/siding contractors, residential homebuilders, couriers and electrical work.
This is a narrow evidence adapter: unknown duties, other industries and
unrecognized evidence need human review.

The base payroll schema is `employee_id,name,position,wages_paid`. CSVs must be
UTF-8, comma-delimited, correctly quoted and have unique nonblank headers and
consistent field counts. Currency is plain decimal dollars with at most two
fractional digits; dollar signs, thousands separators, scientific notation and
non-finite amounts are invalid. Negative inputs are retained for review, not
automatically accepted by every calculation. See
[EMPLOYER_PROCESSING.md](skills/class-code-assistant/EMPLOYER_PROCESSING.md) for
the exact supported narrative/activity schemas and supporting files.

Use `--file payroll=records/wages.csv` when a supported record has a different
relative filename. Repeat `--file FIELD=RELATIVE_PATH` for distinct fields, using
the same overrides in the CSV, question and report commands. All-employer
overrides apply to every selected folder. This changes filenames, not column
schemas or business rules. Absolute paths, parent traversal and unknown/duplicate
override fields are rejected. A new schema may require a separately reviewed
adapter; do not edit code or borrow another industry's rule to force a result.

## Regenerate the CSVs, review state, questions and report

Run these commands in order using the variables above. The regenerated set goes
into `AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR`, leaving the repository's existing `deliverables/` untouched.

First generate all discovered employer CSVs and the required machine-readable state:

```bash
python3 -B skills/class-code-assistant/generate_codes.py \
  --guide "$AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH" \
  --interview "$AUDIT_INTERVIEW_PATH" \
  --all-employers "$AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT" \
  --output-dir "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/codes" \
  --review-state "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/classification-review.json"
```

For a single-employer deliverable set, replace `--all-employers
"$AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT"` with `--employer "$AUDIT_EMPLOYER_DIR"` and choose a
fresh output directory. Later commands infer that selection from the review state
and work for either mode.

Generate the unanswered confirmation questions from current sources and validated
CSVs/review state:

```bash
python3 -B skills/class-code-assistant/audit_questions.py \
  --review-state "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/classification-review.json" \
  --codes-dir "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/codes" \
  --output "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/audit-questions.md"
```

Generate the report using those same dependencies:

```bash
python3 -B skills/class-code-assistant/audit_report.py \
  --review-state "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/classification-review.json" \
  --codes-dir "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/codes" \
  --questions "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/audit-questions.md" \
  --output "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/audit-report.md"
```

The existing required outputs are:

| Location | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `deliverables/codes/` | `annapolis-courier.csv`, `bay-crest-exteriors.csv`, `harbor-point-legal.csv`, `larkspur-lane-bistro.csv`, `patuxent-electric.csv`, `severn-homebuilders.csv`. |
| `deliverables/classification-review.json` | Verified-only scope, complete processing/source state, OPEN amounts, proposals, reconciliations, CSV rows/paths/hashes. |
| `deliverables/audit-questions.md` | Unanswered questions, payment/employee identifiers, recorded priorities, source/record coverage index. |
| `deliverables/audit-report.md` | Reported versus verified payroll/differences, every adjustment, evidence, human-review requirements, reconciliations and separate OPEN/proposed treatments. |

The regenerated set uses the same filenames under your chosen directory. CSV
filenames derive from employer folder slugs; conflicting/empty slugs are errors.
Each CSV has exactly `class_code,payroll_allocated,rationale_ref`, one nonzero
verified row per code, two-decimal payroll and the exact original Guide paragraph
defining that code. The JSON state is a required supporting artifact, not a
substitute for either Markdown deliverable.

See [CSV_GENERATION.md](skills/class-code-assistant/CSV_GENERATION.md),
[AUDIT_QUESTIONS.md](skills/class-code-assistant/AUDIT_QUESTIONS.md) and
[AUDIT_REPORT.md](skills/class-code-assistant/AUDIT_REPORT.md) for validation/API details.

## Interpret results and obtain human approval

- **VERIFIED**: current evidence supports the calculation/classification; this
  is not employer confirmation or final audit sign-off. Verified corrections
  remain in the report and CSVs even when another item for that employer is OPEN.
- **OPEN**: classification, identity, rule applicability or evidence needs human
  resolution. OPEN wages remain in register reconciliation but are excluded from
  verified CSVs. Unresolved payment basis is separate and is not automatically payroll.
- **PROPOSED**: a conditional, unapproved alternative with specific evidence and
  approval requirements. Never add it to verified totals. No supported proposal
  means no guessed treatment.

Employee payroll must reconcile to the cent: verified base wages plus OPEN wages
equal the register. Verified adjustments are then added once. Evaluated payments
equal payroll additions plus excluded/nonpayroll amounts plus unresolved payment
basis. Known payroll may include OPEN wages; it is not all verified/classified.
An absent adjustment check is NOT EVALUATED, not a verified zero. A negative
application difference caused by omitted OPEN wages is provisional, not a verified
wage reduction. Code transfers do not add the same wages a second time.

References preserve original filenames, employee/payment IDs, dates/pay weeks,
exact `CG-xx` identifiers, interview timestamps, line spans and SHA-256. Source IDs
are local to each employer. The questions' record index maps physical CSV rows to
confirmations. Hashes identify bytes; they do not establish authentic/complete
evidence, insurance coverage or employee identity.

The employer payroll/records contact confirms facts and supplies records. The
assigned human auditor decides policy applicability and approves proposed
treatments and application corrections. Capture confirmations without rewriting
original evidence, then rerun with supported current inputs. The report generator
validates the exact **unanswered** question document; edited/answered questions
are not an implemented approval ledger and will be rejected as changed.
Arithmetic balance and exit code 0 never approve an OPEN case.

## Errors, reruns and limitations

| Condition | Behavior / next action |
| --- | --- |
| Missing/unreadable base files, malformed CSV, invalid money | Contextual error; correct records/paths and rerun. Never substitute snapshots or zero payroll. |
| Missing activity evidence, changed rules, unknown duties, identity conflicts or unsupported scope | ERROR or OPEN/REVIEW depending on the adapter; obtain evidence and auditor decisions. No invented code. |
| One employer errors in a batch | Preview/CSV stages retain separate successful results and identify errors. Require a complete error-free CSV/review set before questions/report. |
| Current sources, CSVs or questions disagree with state | Stop dependent generation. Stabilize sources and regenerate the dependency chain into a fresh directory. |
| Identical rerun at the same paths | Identical output bytes are reused without changing output mtimes. |
| Changed results or different selection at occupied destinations | Differing outputs and symbolic-link output files are refused. Use fresh paths; preserve reviewed work. |
| New output directory | CSVs can match byte-for-byte; JSON/Markdown record new output paths and dependent hashes. Compare financial/evidence content separately from declared run metadata. |

"""Fresh real-source dependency chains; never replace the published artifacts."""

from dataclasses import dataclass
import csv
from datetime import date, datetime
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import tempfile
import unittest

from audit_questions import generate_questions
from audit_report import generate_report
from generate_codes import generate_csvs


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RealAuditChain:
    inputs: Path
    guide: Path
    interview: Path
    codes: Path
    review: Path
    questions: Path
    output: Path
    state: dict
    question_result: dict
    report: dict


def fresh_real_chain(register_cleanup):
    """Reread configurable sources and build every dependency in a new directory."""
    component = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
    inputs = Path(os.environ.get("INSURANCE01_TEST_INPUTS", Path.home() / "insurance01-inputs")).expanduser().resolve()
    guide = inputs / "classification-guide.md"
    employers = inputs / "employer-files"
    interview = Path(os.environ.get("INSURANCE01_TEST_INTERVIEW",
        component.parents[1] / "interviews/ch03-premium-audit-20261105-0222(1).md")).expanduser().resolve()
    if not guide.is_file() or not employers.is_dir() or not interview.is_file():
        raise unittest.SkipTest("Auditor-supplied local sources are unavailable; synthetic tests remain portable")
    temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="independent real audit ")
    register_cleanup(temporary.cleanup)
    root = Path(temporary.name)
    codes, review = root / "codes", root / "classification-review.json"
    questions, output = root / "audit-questions.md", root / "audit-report.md"
    state = generate_csvs(guide, interview, all_employers=employers,
                         output_dir=codes, review_state=review)
    if state["errors"] or state["processing"]["errors"] or state["status"] == "ERROR":
        errors = [*state["errors"], *state["processing"]["errors"],
                  *(error for entry in state["processing"]["employers"] for error in entry["errors"])]
        raise AssertionError(f"Fresh real-source processing failed: {errors}")
    question_result = generate_questions(review, codes_dir=codes, output=questions)
    report = generate_report(review, codes_dir=codes, questions=questions, output=output)
    return RealAuditChain(inputs, guide, interview, codes, review, questions, output,
                         state, question_result, report)


def source_rows(path):
    """Read original CSV values independently of the production input reader."""
    with Path(path).open(encoding="utf-8", newline="") as stream:
        return list(csv.DictReader(stream))


def source_period(directory):
    text = (directory / "business-description.md").read_text()
    match = re.search(r"Audit period ([A-Za-z]+ \d+, \d{4}) to ([A-Za-z]+ \d+, \d{4})\.", text)
    assert match, "Original fixture must document its audit period"
    return tuple(datetime.strptime(value, "%B %d, %Y").date() for value in match.groups())


def source_subcontractors(directory):
    """Independent arithmetic for the reviewed homebuilding source fixture.

    This is a test oracle, not an adapter for arbitrary new evidence. Roofing
    invoices here have differently named proof; they require identity review.
    Full-period exact-name coverage excludes payments; missing/expired proof
    adds 60%, per CG-06 and Nadia's confirmed full-period rule.
    """
    payments = source_rows(directory / "subcontractor-payments.csv")
    certificates = source_rows(directory / "insurance-certificates.csv")
    start, end = source_period(directory)
    totals = dict.fromkeys(("basis", "added", "nonpayroll", "open_basis"), Decimal("0.00"))
    by_code, open_invoices = {}, set()
    for payment in payments:
        amount = Decimal(payment["amount_paid"])
        totals["basis"] += amount
        exact = [c for c in certificates if c["subcontractor"] == payment["subcontractor"]]
        if any(date.fromisoformat(c["coverage_from"]) <= start and
               date.fromisoformat(c["coverage_to"]) >= end for c in exact):
            totals["nonpayroll"] += amount
        elif not exact and payment["work"] == "roofing":
            assert any("roof" in c["subcontractor"].casefold() for c in certificates), "Review the changed fixture's certificate evidence"
            totals["open_basis"] += amount
            open_invoices.add(payment["invoice"])
        else:
            addition = (amount * Decimal("0.60")).quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
            code = {"framing": "H-420", "drywall": "H-420", "roofing": "R-310"}[payment["work"]]
            by_code[code] = by_code.get(code, Decimal("0.00")) + addition
            totals["added"] += addition
            totals["nonpayroll"] += amount - addition
    return totals, by_code, open_invoices


def source_controls(inputs):
    """Resum original registers/payments under the reviewed evidence boundaries.

    No generated decisions, CSVs, review JSON or report totals are read here.
    Legal site visits lack an established field rule; mixed catering duties
    lack complete audit-period receipts. Their original wages stay OPEN.
    Allowances above $47/documented day count; zero-day allowances stay OPEN.
    """
    portfolio = dict.fromkeys(("register", "added", "open_wages", "basis", "nonpayroll", "open_basis"), Decimal("0.00"))
    employers = {}
    for directory in sorted((inputs / "employer-files").iterdir()):
        if not directory.is_dir() or directory.name.startswith("."):
            continue
        payroll = source_rows(directory / "payroll-register.csv")
        values = dict.fromkeys(portfolio, Decimal("0.00"))
        values["register"] = sum((Decimal(r["wages_paid"]) for r in payroll), Decimal("0.00"))
        open_workers = source_open_workers(directory, payroll)
        values["open_wages"] = sum((Decimal(r["wages_paid"]) for r in payroll
                                    if r["employee_id"] in open_workers), Decimal("0.00"))
        if (directory / "subcontractor-payments.csv").is_file():
            subcontractors, _, _ = source_subcontractors(directory)
            for key, amount in subcontractors.items():
                values[key] += amount
        for row in payroll:
            if "travel_allowance_paid" not in row:
                continue
            allowance, days = Decimal(row["travel_allowance_paid"]), int(row["travel_days"])
            values["basis"] += allowance
            if days == 0 and allowance:
                values["open_basis"] += allowance
            else:
                excluded = min(allowance, Decimal("47") * days)
                values["nonpayroll"] += excluded
                values["added"] += allowance - excluded
        for key in portfolio:
            portfolio[key] += values[key]
        employers[directory.name] = values
    for values in [portfolio, *employers.values()]:
        values["verified"] = values["register"] - values["open_wages"] + values["added"]
        values["cash"] = values["register"] + values["basis"]
        values["known_payroll"] = values["register"] + values["added"]
    return portfolio, employers


def source_open_workers(directory, payroll):
    """Identify the reviewed fixture's unsupported duties from original records."""
    business = " ".join((directory / "business-description.md").read_text().split())
    if "law office" in business:
        visits = source_rows(directory / "site-signin-log.csv")
        return {r["employee_id"] for r in visits}
    if (directory / "gross-receipts.csv").is_file():
        receipts = source_rows(directory / "gross-receipts.csv")
        _, end = source_period(directory)
        assert end.strftime("%Y-%m") not in {r["month"] for r in receipts}, "Review newly complete catering evidence"
        return {r["employee_id"] for r in payroll if r["position"] in {"Catering Lead", "Event Cook", "Event Server"}}
    return set()

# Class Code and Premium Audit Assistant — INSURANCE-01

This reusable Agent Skill reads employer records, applies Linden Shore Mutual's
verified company rules, allocates payroll with Decimal, and produces classification
CSVs, confirmation questions and an audit report. Unsupported decisions remain
OPEN for human review. It calculates no rates or insurance premiums.

The Skill instructions are in
[skills/class-code-assistant/SKILL.md](skills/class-code-assistant/SKILL.md).
The CLI uses the same existing processing engine; another employer using a
supported evidence schema needs different input paths, not Python source edits.

## Setup

Use Python **3.10 or newer**. The runtime and unittest suite use only the Python
standard library, including `decimal`, `csv`, `json`, `hashlib`, `pathlib` and
`unittest`. No pip installation, virtual environment, API key or network service
is required. Verification for this checkout used Python 3.12.3 on Linux/WSL.

Open a Bash-compatible terminal at the repository root, where this README and
`skills/` are located. Check the interpreter:

```bash
python3 -B -c 'import sys; assert sys.version_info >= (3, 10), "Python 3.10+ required"; print(sys.version)'
```

`-B` avoids writing Python bytecode into the source tree. Paths may contain spaces;
keep the quotes used below. Bash and `mktemp` are used by the example shell setup;
the Python components themselves require neither Bash nor `mktemp`.

## Current sources and preserved development snapshots

For each new audit, obtain the authoritative source locations from the auditor.

| Input | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Classification Guide | Current readable UTF-8 Markdown with original `CG-xx` paragraph definitions. Use company rules; public manuals are not substitutes. |
| Interview evidence | Complete original Markdown export containing verified house practices, timestamps and applicability clarifications. Preserve original bytes and metadata. |
| Employer records | One employer directory, or a container of employer directories. Base files are `business-description.md`, `field-notes.md`, `payroll-register.csv` and `application.md`. |
| Supporting records | Activity, receipts, certificates, subcontractor payments, weekly payroll and travel evidence required by that business; see the schema reference below. |
| Original assignment | Retain as the output/scope authority. It is a human reference; the runtime does not parse its DOCX or extract a ZIP. |

Every invocation rereads the selected Guide, interview and employer records.
Question/report generation obtains their locations from the supplied review-state
file, rereads them, and rejects results that disagree with that state. There is no
automatic fallback to a development snapshot. Keep sources stable during a run;
SHA-256 checks detect changes but do not authenticate documents.

This workstation has local development snapshots at
`/home/maxg/insurance01-inputs/classification-guide.md` and
`/home/maxg/insurance01-inputs/employer-files/` (six employer folders, 34 records).
The original assignment, Guide and employer ZIP remain unchanged under
`/mnt/c/Users/PC/Downloads/`. These external files are not bundled into the
repository or guaranteed available on another computer. The preserved final
interview export is
[interviews/ch03-premium-audit-20261105-0222(1).md](<interviews/ch03-premium-audit-20261105-0222(1).md>).
The preserved repository deliverables are results from those snapshots, not a
source of classification answers for a new run.

Set these shell variables to current auditor-supplied locations:

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH` | Absolute path to the current Guide Markdown. |
| `AUDIT_INTERVIEW_PATH` | Absolute path to the complete original interview Markdown. |
| `AUDIT_EMPLOYER_DIR` | One selected employer directory. |
| `AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT` | Container holding employer directories for an all-employer run. |
| `AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR` | Fresh output directory, outside authoritative sources. |

To reproduce the preserved six-employer development run on **this workstation**,
use the explicit snapshot configuration below. For another audit, replace the
source values with the auditor's current locations; these examples are not
authoritative defaults. The temporary output directory protects existing deliverables:

```bash
export AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH='/home/maxg/insurance01-inputs/classification-guide.md'
export AUDIT_INTERVIEW_PATH="$PWD/interviews/ch03-premium-audit-20261105-0222(1).md"
export AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT='/home/maxg/insurance01-inputs/employer-files'
export AUDIT_EMPLOYER_DIR="$AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT/patuxent-electric"
export AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR="$(mktemp -d /tmp/insurance01-rerun.XXXXXX)"
```

## Preview one employer or every discovered employer

Preview one selected employer; this writes only to stdout:

```bash
python3 -B skills/class-code-assistant/preview.py \
  --guide "$AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH" \
  --interview "$AUDIT_INTERVIEW_PATH" \
  --employer "$AUDIT_EMPLOYER_DIR"
```

Preview all immediate nonhidden employer directories. With the development
configuration above, this discovers all six employers:

```bash
python3 -B skills/class-code-assistant/preview.py \
  --guide "$AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH" \
  --interview "$AUDIT_INTERVIEW_PATH" \
  --all-employers "$AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT"
```

Add `--format json` for structured stdout with Decimal amounts encoded as strings.
Discovery is sorted, does not recurse into nested employer containers, and keeps
employer identities/results separate. Root files and hidden entries are excluded
and reported; incomplete employer directories produce errors, not silent skips.

For a new employer, put its current records in a separate directory, set
`AUDIT_EMPLOYER_DIR` to that location, and run the first command. For a new batch,
change `AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT` and run the second. No employer list or answer table
needs editing. Existing adapters support restaurant/catering, legal offices,
roofing/siding contractors, residential homebuilders, couriers and electrical work.
This is a narrow evidence adapter: unknown duties, other industries and
unrecognized evidence need human review.

The base payroll schema is `employee_id,name,position,wages_paid`. CSVs must be
UTF-8, comma-delimited, correctly quoted and have unique nonblank headers and
consistent field counts. Currency is plain decimal dollars with at most two
fractional digits; dollar signs, thousands separators, scientific notation and
non-finite amounts are invalid. Negative inputs are retained for review, not
automatically accepted by every calculation. See
[EMPLOYER_PROCESSING.md](skills/class-code-assistant/EMPLOYER_PROCESSING.md) for
the exact supported narrative/activity schemas and supporting files.

Use `--file payroll=records/wages.csv` when a supported record has a different
relative filename. Repeat `--file FIELD=RELATIVE_PATH` for distinct fields, using
the same overrides in the CSV, question and report commands. All-employer
overrides apply to every selected folder. This changes filenames, not column
schemas or business rules. Absolute paths, parent traversal and unknown/duplicate
override fields are rejected. A new schema may require a separately reviewed
adapter; do not edit code or borrow another industry's rule to force a result.

## Regenerate the CSVs, review state, questions and report

Run these commands in order using the variables above. The regenerated set goes
into `AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR`, leaving the repository's existing `deliverables/` untouched.

First generate all discovered employer CSVs and the required machine-readable state:

```bash
python3 -B skills/class-code-assistant/generate_codes.py \
  --guide "$AUDIT_GUIDE_PATH" \
  --interview "$AUDIT_INTERVIEW_PATH" \
  --all-employers "$AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT" \
  --output-dir "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/codes" \
  --review-state "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/classification-review.json"
```

For a single-employer deliverable set, replace `--all-employers
"$AUDIT_EMPLOYERS_ROOT"` with `--employer "$AUDIT_EMPLOYER_DIR"` and choose a
fresh output directory. Later commands infer that selection from the review state
and work for either mode.

Generate the unanswered confirmation questions from current sources and validated
CSVs/review state:

```bash
python3 -B skills/class-code-assistant/audit_questions.py \
  --review-state "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/classification-review.json" \
  --codes-dir "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/codes" \
  --output "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/audit-questions.md"
```

Generate the report using those same dependencies:

```bash
python3 -B skills/class-code-assistant/audit_report.py \
  --review-state "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/classification-review.json" \
  --codes-dir "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/codes" \
  --questions "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/audit-questions.md" \
  --output "$AUDIT_OUTPUT_DIR/audit-report.md"
```

The existing required outputs are:

| Location | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `deliverables/codes/` | `annapolis-courier.csv`, `bay-crest-exteriors.csv`, `harbor-point-legal.csv`, `larkspur-lane-bistro.csv`, `patuxent-electric.csv`, `severn-homebuilders.csv`. |
| `deliverables/classification-review.json` | Verified-only scope, complete processing/source state, OPEN amounts, proposals, reconciliations, CSV rows/paths/hashes. |
| `deliverables/audit-questions.md` | Unanswered questions, payment/employee identifiers, recorded priorities, source/record coverage index. |
| `deliverables/audit-report.md` | Reported versus verified payroll/differences, every adjustment, evidence, human-review requirements, reconciliations and separate OPEN/proposed treatments. |

The regenerated set uses the same filenames under your chosen directory. CSV
filenames derive from employer folder slugs; conflicting/empty slugs are errors.
Each CSV has exactly `class_code,payroll_allocated,rationale_ref`, one nonzero
verified row per code, two-decimal payroll and the exact original Guide paragraph
defining that code. The JSON state is a required supporting artifact, not a
substitute for either Markdown deliverable.

See [CSV_GENERATION.md](skills/class-code-assistant/CSV_GENERATION.md),
[AUDIT_QUESTIONS.md](skills/class-code-assistant/AUDIT_QUESTIONS.md) and
[AUDIT_REPORT.md](skills/class-code-assistant/AUDIT_REPORT.md) for validation/API details.

## Interpret results and obtain human approval

- **VERIFIED**: current evidence supports the calculation/classification; this
  is not employer confirmation or final audit sign-off. Verified corrections
  remain in the report and CSVs even when another item for that employer is OPEN.
- **OPEN**: classification, identity, rule applicability or evidence needs human
  resolution. OPEN wages remain in register reconciliation but are excluded from
  verified CSVs. Unresolved payment basis is separate and is not automatically payroll.
- **PROPOSED**: a conditional, unapproved alternative with specific evidence and
  approval requirements. Never add it to verified totals. No supported proposal
  means no guessed treatment.

Employee payroll must reconcile to the cent: verified base wages plus OPEN wages
equal the register. Verified adjustments are then added once. Evaluated payments
equal payroll additions plus excluded/nonpayroll amounts plus unresolved payment
basis. Known payroll may include OPEN wages; it is not all verified/classified.
An absent adjustment check is NOT EVALUATED, not a verified zero. A negative
application difference caused by omitted OPEN wages is provisional, not a verified
wage reduction. Code transfers do not add the same wages a second time.

References preserve original filenames, employee/payment IDs, dates/pay weeks,
exact `CG-xx` identifiers, interview timestamps, line spans and SHA-256. Source IDs
are local to each employer. The questions' record index maps physical CSV rows to
confirmations. Hashes identify bytes; they do not establish authentic/complete
evidence, insurance coverage or employee identity.

The employer payroll/records contact confirms facts and supplies records. The
assigned human auditor decides policy applicability and approves proposed
treatments and application corrections. Capture confirmations without rewriting
original evidence, then rerun with supported current inputs. The report generator
validates the exact **unanswered** question document; edited/answered questions
are not an implemented approval ledger and will be rejected as changed.
Arithmetic balance and exit code 0 never approve an OPEN case.

## Errors, reruns and limitations

| Condition | Behavior / next action |
| --- | --- |
| Missing/unreadable base files, malformed CSV, invalid money | Contextual error; correct records/paths and rerun. Never substitute snapshots or zero payroll. |
| Missing activity evidence, changed rules, unknown duties, identity conflicts or unsupported scope | ERROR or OPEN/REVIEW depending on the adapter; obtain evidence and auditor decisions. No invented code. |
| One employer errors in a batch | Preview/CSV stages retain separate successful results and identify errors. Require a complete error-free CSV/review set before questions/report. |
| Current sources, CSVs or questions disagree with state | Stop dependent generation. Stabilize sources and regenerate the dependency chain into a fresh directory. |
| Identical rerun at the same paths | Identical output bytes are reused without changing output mtimes. |
| Changed results or different selection at occupied destinations | Differing outputs and symbolic-link output files are refused. Use fresh paths; preserve reviewed work. |
| New output directory | CSVs can match byte-for-byte; JSON/Markdown record new output paths and dependent hashes. Compare financial/evidence content separately from declared run metadata. |

"""Fresh real-source dependency chains; never replace the published artifacts."""

from dataclasses import dataclass
import csv
from datetime import date, datetime
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import tempfile
import unittest

from audit_questions import generate_questions
from audit_report import generate_report
from generate_codes import generate_csvs


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RealAuditChain:
    inputs: Path
    guide: Path
    interview: Path
    codes: Path
    review: Path
    questions: Path
    output: Path
    state: dict
    question_result: dict
    report: dict


def fresh_real_chain(register_cleanup):
    """Reread configurable sources and build every dependency in a new directory."""
    component = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
    inputs = Path(os.environ.get("INSURANCE01_TEST_INPUTS", Path.home() / "insurance01-inputs")).expanduser().resolve()
    guide = inputs / "classification-guide.md"
    employers = inputs / "employer-files"
    interview = Path(os.environ.get("INSURANCE01_TEST_INTERVIEW",
        component.parents[1] / "interviews/ch03-premium-audit-20261105-0222(1).md")).expanduser().resolve()
    if not guide.is_file() or not employers.is_dir() or not interview.is_file():
        raise unittest.SkipTest("Auditor-supplied local sources are unavailable; synthetic tests remain portable")
    temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="independent real audit ")
    register_cleanup(temporary.cleanup)
    root = Path(temporary.name)
    codes, review = root / "codes", root / "classification-review.json"
    questions, output = root / "audit-questions.md", root / "audit-report.md"
    state = generate_csvs(guide, interview, all_employers=employers,
                         output_dir=codes, review_state=review)
    if state["errors"] or state["processing"]["errors"] or state["status"] == "ERROR":
        errors = [*state["errors"], *state["processing"]["errors"],
                  *(error for entry in state["processing"]["employers"] for error in entry["errors"])]
        raise AssertionError(f"Fresh real-source processing failed: {errors}")
    question_result = generate_questions(review, codes_dir=codes, output=questions)
    report = generate_report(review, codes_dir=codes, questions=questions, output=output)
    return RealAuditChain(inputs, guide, interview, codes, review, questions, output,
                         state, question_result, report)


def source_rows(path):
    """Read original CSV values independently of the production input reader."""
    with Path(path).open(encoding="utf-8", newline="") as stream:
        return list(csv.DictReader(stream))


def source_period(directory):
    text = (directory / "business-description.md").read_text()
    match = re.search(r"Audit period ([A-Za-z]+ \d+, \d{4}) to ([A-Za-z]+ \d+, \d{4})\.", text)
    assert match, "Original fixture must document its audit period"
    return tuple(datetime.strptime(value, "%B %d, %Y").date() for value in match.groups())


def source_subcontractors(directory):
    """Independent arithmetic for the reviewed homebuilding source fixture.

    This is a test oracle, not an adapter for arbitrary new evidence. Roofing
    invoices here have differently named proof; they require identity review.
    Full-period exact-name coverage excludes payments; missing/expired proof
    adds 60%, per CG-06 and Nadia's confirmed full-period rule.
    """
    payments = source_rows(directory / "subcontractor-payments.csv")
    certificates = source_rows(directory / "insurance-certificates.csv")
    start, end = source_period(directory)
    totals = dict.fromkeys(("basis", "added", "nonpayroll", "open_basis"), Decimal("0.00"))
    by_code, open_invoices = {}, set()
    for payment in payments:
        amount = Decimal(payment["amount_paid"])
        totals["basis"] += amount
        exact = [c for c in certificates if c["subcontractor"] == payment["subcontractor"]]
        if any(date.fromisoformat(c["coverage_from"]) <= start and
               date.fromisoformat(c["coverage_to"]) >= end for c in exact):
            totals["nonpayroll"] += amount
        elif not exact and payment["work"] == "roofing":
            assert any("roof" in c["subcontractor"].casefold() for c in certificates), "Review the changed fixture's certificate evidence"
            totals["open_basis"] += amount
            open_invoices.add(payment["invoice"])
        else:
            addition = (amount * Decimal("0.60")).quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
            code = {"framing": "H-420", "drywall": "H-420", "roofing": "R-310"}[payment["work"]]
            by_code[code] = by_code.get(code, Decimal("0.00")) + addition
            totals["added"] += addition
            totals["nonpayroll"] += amount - addition
    return totals, by_code, open_invoices


def source_controls(inputs):
    """Resum original registers/payments under the reviewed evidence boundaries.

    No generated decisions, CSVs, review JSON or report totals are read here.
    Legal site visits lack an established field rule; mixed catering duties
    lack complete audit-period receipts. Their original wages stay OPEN.
    Allowances above $47/documented day count; zero-day allowances stay OPEN.
    """
    portfolio = dict.fromkeys(("register", "added", "open_wages", "basis", "nonpayroll", "open_basis"), Decimal("0.00"))
    employers = {}
    for directory in sorted((inputs / "employer-files").iterdir()):
        if not directory.is_dir() or directory.name.startswith("."):
            continue
        payroll = source_rows(directory / "payroll-register.csv")
        values = dict.fromkeys(portfolio, Decimal("0.00"))
        values["register"] = sum((Decimal(r["wages_paid"]) for r in payroll), Decimal("0.00"))
        open_workers = source_open_workers(directory, payroll)
        values["open_wages"] = sum((Decimal(r["wages_paid"]) for r in payroll
                                    if r["employee_id"] in open_workers), Decimal("0.00"))
        if (directory / "subcontractor-payments.csv").is_file():
            subcontractors, _, _ = source_subcontractors(directory)
            for key, amount in subcontractors.items():
                values[key] += amount
        for row in payroll:
            if "travel_allowance_paid" not in row:
                continue
            allowance, days = Decimal(row["travel_allowance_paid"]), int(row["travel_days"])
            values["basis"] += allowance
            if days == 0 and allowance:
                values["open_basis"] += allowance
            else:
                excluded = min(allowance, Decimal("47") * days)
                values["nonpayroll"] += excluded
                values["added"] += allowance - excluded
        for key in portfolio:
            portfolio[key] += values[key]
        employers[directory.name] = values
    for values in [portfolio, *employers.values()]:
        values["verified"] = values["register"] - values["open_wages"] + values["added"]
        values["cash"] = values["register"] + values["basis"]
        values["known_payroll"] = values["register"] + values["added"]
    return portfolio, employers


def source_open_workers(directory, payroll):
    """Identify the reviewed fixture's unsupported duties from original records."""
    business = " ".join((directory / "business-description.md").read_text().split())
    if "law office" in business:
        visits = source_rows(directory / "site-signin-log.csv")
        return {r["employee_id"] for r in visits}
    if (directory / "gross-receipts.csv").is_file():
        receipts = source_rows(directory / "gross-receipts.csv")
        _, end = source_period(directory)
        assert end.strftime("%Y-%m") not in {r["month"] for r in receipts}, "Review newly complete catering evidence"
        return {r["employee_id"] for r in payroll if r["position"] in {"Catering Lead", "Event Cook", "Event Server"}}
    return set()
"}

# Verification Before Completion

## Overview

**Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

**Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
```

If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

## The Gate Function

```
BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
   - If NO: State actual status with evidence
   - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim

Skip any step = lying, not verifying
```

## Common Failures

| Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
| Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
| Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
| Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
| Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
| Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
| Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |

## Red Flags - STOP

- Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
- Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
- About to commit/push/PR without verification
- Trusting agent success reports
- Relying on partial verification
- Thinking "just this once"
- Tired and wanting work over
- **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**

## Rationalization Prevention

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
| "I'm confident" | Confidence ≠ evidence |
| "Just this once" | No exceptions |
| "Linter passed" | Linter ≠ compiler |
| "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
| "I'm tired" | Exhaustion ≠ excuse |
| "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
| "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |

## Key Patterns

**Tests:**
```
✅ [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"
❌ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"
```

**Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**
```
✅ Write → Run (pass) → Revert fix → Run (MUST FAIL) → Restore → Run (pass)
❌ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)
```

**Build:**
```
✅ [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"
❌ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)
```

**Requirements:**
```
✅ Re-read plan → Create checklist → Verify each → Report gaps or completion
❌ "Tests pass, phase complete"
```

**Agent delegation:**
```
✅ Agent reports success → Check VCS diff → Verify changes → Report actual state
❌ Trust agent report
```

## When To Apply

**ALWAYS before:**
- ANY variation of success/completion claims
- ANY expression of satisfaction
- ANY positive statement about work state
- Committing, PR creation, task completion
- Moving to next task
- Delegating to agents

**Rule applies to:**
- Exact phrases
- Paraphrases and synonyms
- Implications of success
- ANY communication suggesting completion/correctness

def _priorities(interview, employers, natives, files):
    messages = list(_MESSAGE.finditer(interview.text))
    acknowledgements = []
    for index, match in enumerate(messages):
        end = messages[index + 1].start() if index + 1 < len(messages) else len(interview.text)
        body = interview.text[match.end():end]
        choice = re.search(r"I have noted your choices of (.+?), along with your reasoning regarding (.+?)\.", body, re.S)
        if match.group(1) == "Nadia Brennan" and choice:
            acknowledgements.append((match, end, choice))
    if len(acknowledgements) > 1:
        raise QuestionGenerationError("Multiple priority acknowledgements require human confirmation; no ranking is inferred")
    if not acknowledgements:
        return []
    match, end, choice = acknowledgements[0]
    normalize = lambda text: " ".join(text.casefold().split())
    recorded_text = choice.group(1).strip()
    identities = {}
    for employer in employers:
        identities.setdefault(normalize(employer["name"]), []).append(employer)
    # Exact identity matching permits case/spacing variants only. A prefix
    # such as Independent cannot stand for Independent Electric. Preserve a full
    # company name containing 'and' when it matches exactly; otherwise parse the
    # acknowledgement's explicit list separators conservatively.
    recorded_names = [recorded_text] if normalize(recorded_text) in identities else re.split(r",\s*(?:and\s+)?|\s+and\s+", recorded_text)
    selected = []
    seen = set()
    for position, name in enumerate(recorded_names):
        matching = identities.get(normalize(name), [])
        if len(matching) > 1:
            raise QuestionGenerationError(f"Ambiguous recorded priority identity: {name}")
        if not matching:
            # A partial list could instead be a single compound legal name, such
            # as Independent and Sons. Do not revive Independent as an alias.
            return []
        employer = matching[0]
        if employer["directory"] in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(employer["directory"])
        native = natives[employer["directory"]]
        reasons = []
        adjustments = employer["entry"]["adjustments"]["lines"]
        subcontractors = [line for line in adjustments if line["kind"] == "subcontractor"]
        if subcontractors:
            reasons.append("Subcontractor certificate coverage and identity require confirmation: "
                f"verified additions ${_sum_money(line['payroll_added'] for line in subcontractors)}, "
                f"OPEN payment basis ${_sum_money(line['unresolved_basis'] for line in subcontractors)}. "
                + " ".join(dict.fromkeys(line["reason"] for line in subcontractors)))
        changes = [item for item in native.employee_comparisons.values() if item.status == "CHANGE"]
        if changes:
            reasons.append(f"Work-record classification changes affect {len(changes)} employees and ${_sum_money(str(item.wages) for item in changes)} of wages. "
                "The employer's application and employee-attribution questions must be confirmed against actual work records.")
            if native.roofing_days:
                reasons.append(f"{files.crew_timesheets} and {files.site_signins} support substantial field work rather than the reported clerical split; confirm each changed employee's records below.")
        reported = employer["entry"]["application"]
        if reported:
            reasons.append("Reported split: " + "; ".join(f"{row['class_code']}: {row['employees']} employees, ${row['payroll']}" for row in reported["reported"]) + ".")
        selected.append((position, {"employer": employer["employer"], "name": employer["name"],
            "reason": " ".join(reasons) or f"Recorded reason: {choice.group(2).strip()}; confirm the supporting records below.",
            "source": asdict(_reference(interview, match.start(), end, f"Nadia Brennan · {match.group(2)}"))}))
    return [item for _, item in sorted(selected, key=lambda item: item[0])]

def _priorities(interview, employers, natives, files):
    messages = list(_MESSAGE.finditer(interview.text))
    acknowledgements = []
    for index, match in enumerate(messages):
        end = messages[index + 1].start() if index + 1 < len(messages) else len(interview.text)
        body = interview.text[match.end():end]
        choice = re.search(r"I have noted your choices of (.+?), along with your reasoning regarding (.+?)\.", body, re.S)
        if match.group(1) == "Nadia Brennan" and choice:
            acknowledgements.append((match, end, choice))
    if len(acknowledgements) > 1:
        raise QuestionGenerationError("Multiple priority acknowledgements require human confirmation; no ranking is inferred")
    if not acknowledgements:
        return []
    match, end, choice = acknowledgements[0]
    normalize = lambda text: " ".join(text.casefold().split())
    recorded_text = choice.group(1).strip()
    identities = {}
    for employer in employers:
        identities.setdefault(normalize(employer["name"]), []).append(employer)
    # Exact identity matching permits case/spacing variants only. A prefix
    # such as Independent cannot stand for Independent Electric. Preserve a full
    # company name containing 'and' when it matches exactly; otherwise parse the
    # acknowledgement's explicit list separators conservatively.
    recorded_names = [recorded_text] if normalize(recorded_text) in identities else re.split(r",\s*(?:and\s+)?|\s+and\s+", recorded_text)
    selected = []
    seen = set()
    for position, name in enumerate(recorded_names):
        matching = identities.get(normalize(name), [])
        if len(matching) > 1:
            raise QuestionGenerationError(f"Ambiguous recorded priority identity: {name}")
        if not matching:
            # A partial list could instead be a single compound legal name, such
            # as Independent and Sons. Do not revive Independent as an alias.
            return []
        employer = matching[0]
        if employer["directory"] in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(employer["directory"])
        native = natives[employer["directory"]]
        reasons = []
        adjustments = employer["entry"]["adjustments"]["lines"]
        subcontractors = [line for line in adjustments if line["kind"] == "subcontractor"]
        if subcontractors:
            reasons.append("Subcontractor certificate coverage and identity require confirmation: "
                f"verified additions ${_sum_money(line['payroll_added'] for line in subcontractors)}, "
                f"OPEN payment basis ${_sum_money(line['unresolved_basis'] for line in subcontractors)}. "
                + " ".join(dict.fromkeys(line["reason"] for line in subcontractors)))
        changes = [item for item in native.employee_comparisons.values() if item.status == "CHANGE"]
        if changes:
            reasons.append(f"Work-record classification changes affect {len(changes)} employees and ${_sum_money(str(item.wages) for item in changes)} of wages. "
                "The employer's application and employee-attribution questions must be confirmed against actual work records.")
            if native.roofing_days:
                reasons.append(f"{files.crew_timesheets} and {files.site_signins} support substantial field work rather than the reported clerical split; confirm each changed employee's records below.")
        reported = employer["entry"]["application"]
        if reported:
            reasons.append("Reported split: " + "; ".join(f"{row['class_code']}: {row['employees']} employees, ${row['payroll']}" for row in reported["reported"]) + ".")
        selected.append((position, {"employer": employer["employer"], "name": employer["name"],
            "reason": " ".join(reasons) or f"Recorded reason: {choice.group(2).strip()}; confirm the supporting records below.",
            "source": asdict(_reference(interview, match.start(), end, f"Nadia Brennan · {match.group(2)}"))}))
    return [item for _, item in sorted(selected, key=lambda item: item[0])]

    for index, match in enumerate(messages):

        choice = re.search(r"I have noted your choices of (.+?), along with your reasoning regarding (.+?)\.", body, re.S)

    if not acknowledgements:
        return []
    match, end, choice = acknowledgements[0]
    normalize = lambda text: " ".join(text.casefold().split())
    recorded_text = choice.group(1).strip()
    identities = {}
    for employer in employers:
        identities.setdefault(normalize(employer["name"]), []).append(employer)
    # Exact identity matching permits case/spacing variants only. A prefix
    # such as Independent cannot stand for Independent Electric. Preserve a full
    # company name containing 'and' when it matches exactly; otherwise parse the
    # acknowledgement's explicit list separators conservatively.
    recorded_names = [recorded_text] if normalize(recorded_text) in identities else re.split(r",\s*(?:and\s+)?|\s+and\s+", recorded_text)

        matching = identities.get(normalize(name), [])
        if len(matching) > 1:
            raise QuestionGenerationError(f"Ambiguous recorded priority identity: {name}")
        if not matching:
            # A partial list could instead be a single compound legal name, such
            # as Independent and Sons. Do not revive Independent as an alias.
            return []
        employer = matching[0]
        if employer["directory"] in seen:
            continue

        reasons = []
        adjustments = employer["entry"]["adjustments"]["lines"]
        subcontractors = [line for line in adjustments if line["kind"] == "subcontractor"]
        if subcontractors:
            reasons.append("Subcontractor certificate coverage and identity require confirmation: "
                f"verified additions ${_sum_money(line['payroll_added'] for line in subcontractors)}, "
                f"OPEN payment basis ${_sum_money(line['unresolved_basis'] for line in subcontractors)}. "
                + " ".join(dict.fromkeys(line["reason"] for line in subcontractors)))
        changes = [item for item in native.employee_comparisons.values() if item.status == "CHANGE"]

                "The employer's application and employee-attribution questions must be confirmed against actual work records.")

            reasons.append("Reported split: " + "; ".join(f"{row['class_code']}: {row['employees']} employees, ${row['payroll']}" for row in reported["reported"]) + ".")

            "source": asdict(_reference(interview, match.start(), end, f"Nadia Brennan · {match.group(2)}"))}))

155:An office employee keeps the clerical code C-110 only if the site sign-in log shows them on a job site on four days or fewer in the audit period.
187:A daily allowance paid to crews working out-of-town is left out of payroll up to forty-seven dollars per worker per day. Anything paid above that amount counts as payroll.
219:The daily allowance practice is based on a fixed figure of forty-seven dollars per worker per day, without accounting for inflation.
299:I classify people by what they actually do. For example, an audit shows whether an office employee spent five or more days on a job site, which moves their entire payroll to the governing field code.
303:What happens if somebody works on multiple job sites in five days?
307:If an office employee is on a job site for five or more days, their entire payroll moves to the employer's governing field code carrying the most payroll.
427:Yes, the daily allowance threshold is the forty-seven dollars a day for out-of-town crews.
507:The caterer code F-720 applies only if off-site catering is 40 percent or more of gross receipts. Otherwise, the catering crew stays under the restaurant code F-710 with everyone else.
515:Contractors doing both roofing and siding classify field workers with 15 or more days on a roof entirely under R-310, and those with fewer days entirely under R-320.
519:Just to confirm, the 40 percent threshold is calculated using the total restaurant and off-site catering gross receipts for the audited policy period, correct?
523:Yes, the 40 percent threshold is based on the off-site catering gross receipts compared to the employer's total gross receipts for the audit period.
531:When an inside employee rides on a delivery route on two or more days in a Monday-to-Sunday pay week, their whole week's pay is allocated as driver payroll under T-610; a week with only one ride day stays entirely under C-110.

555:A field worker with 15 or more days on a roof goes entirely under R-310, and with fewer than 15 days entirely under R-320.
655:Now I want to understand for contractors like Baycrest or Severn, if a field worker spends 15 or more days on a roof, their entire payroll for the policy goes under R-310 roofing?

const root=load("omega2_step10_temp");
const script=`import hashlib,json,sys
from pathlib import Path
root=Path(sys.argv[1]); sys.path.insert(0,str(root))
import prepare
from audit_report import load_report_plan,render_report,report_coverage_gaps
from audit_questions import coverage_gaps,render_questions
from generate_codes import generate_csvs
repo=prepare.REPO; dest=repo/"deliverables"
state=json.loads((dest/"classification-review.json").read_text())
# An idempotent generator pass independently reconstructs every CSV/state byte
# at the actual destination; differing output would be refused before writes.
paths=[p for p in dest.rglob("*") if p.is_file()]
before={str(p):(p.read_bytes(),p.stat().st_mtime_ns) for p in paths}
again=generate_csvs(prepare.GUIDE,prepare.INTERVIEW,all_employers=prepare.INPUTS/"employer-files",output_dir=dest/"codes",review_state=dest/"classification-review.json")
assert again==state
plan=load_report_plan(dest/"classification-review.json",codes_dir=dest/"codes",questions=dest/"audit-questions.md")
plan["questions_link"]="audit-questions.md"
assert render_questions(plan).encode()==(dest/"audit-questions.md").read_bytes()
assert render_report(plan).encode()==(dest/"audit-report.md").read_bytes()
assert not coverage_gaps(plan) and not report_coverage_gaps(plan)
financial=prepare.independent(state,plan,(dest/"audit-questions.md").read_text(),(dest/"audit-report.md").read_text(),dest/"codes")
for p in paths:
    assert (p.read_bytes(),p.stat().st_mtime_ns)==before[str(p)],str(p)
validation=json.loads((root/"validation.json").read_text())
for name,digest in validation["candidate_hashes"].items():
    assert hashlib.sha256((dest/name).read_bytes()).hexdigest()==digest,name
result={"status":"PASS","artifacts":len(paths),"independent":financial,"priorities":[{"name":p["name"],"reason":p["reason"],"source":p["source"]["locator"]} for p in plan["priorities"]],"uncovered_questions":coverage_gaps(plan),"uncovered_report":report_coverage_gaps(plan),"idempotent_csv_state_generation":True,"all_artifact_bytes_and_mtimes_preserved_by_validation":True}
(root/"final-validation.json").write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+"\\n")
print(json.dumps(result,indent=2))
`;
const quote=s=>"'"+s.replace(/'/g,"'\"'\"'")+"'";
text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"python3 -B -c "+quote(script)+" "+quote(root),max_output_tokens:4500,yield_time_ms:1000}));
store("omega2_step10_postvalidation_script",script);
text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"python3 -B -m unittest discover -s skills/class-code-assistant/tests","max_output_tokens":4500,"yield_time_ms":1000}));
